en: The Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka Sūtra:
The First Chapter, titled "Setting in Motion the Wheel of Dharma"
Oṃ, homage to all the glorious Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
Having prostrated to the Buddha, the omniscient one, and to the Dharma and the Saṅgha, a mine of virtues,
I shall proclaim this Bodhisattva Sūtra known as the Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka.
Thus have I heard.

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain together with a great saṅgha of twelve hundred bhikṣus, all of whom were arhats, whose outflows were exhausted, who were free from afflictions, and who had attained mastery.

[It was] with great śrāvakas who were well-liberated in mind, well-liberated in wisdom, noble thoroughbreds, great dragons, who had accomplished their task, completed what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own goal, exhausted the fetters of existence, whose minds were well-liberated through right knowledge, who had reached the supreme perfection of mastery over all mental states, and were renowned for their supernormal powers; namely: (KpSū 2) as follows:
and with the venerable Ājñātakauṇḍinya, the venerable Aśvajit, the venerable Bāṣpa, the venerable Mahāsthāman, the venerable Bhadrika, the venerable Mahākāśyapa, the venerable Urubilvākāśyapa,
the venerable Gayākāśyapa, the venerable Śāriputra, and the venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana.
And with Mahākātyāyana, the venerable Aniruddha, the venerable Revata, the venerable Kaṃphilla, the venerable Gavāmpati, the venerable Pilindavatsa, the venerable Bakula,
the venerable Mahākauṣṭhila, the venerable Bharadvāja, the venerable Mahānanda, and the venerable Upananda.

And with the venerable Sundarananda, the venerable Pūrṇa, the venerable Subhūti, and the venerable Rāhula; likewise with many other great śrāvakas headed by these, and with the venerable Ānanda who was still in training,
and with two thousand other monks, both those in training and those beyond training.
and with six thousand bhikṣuṇīs headed by Mahāprajāpatī, and the bhikṣuṇī Yaśodharā, the mother of Rāhula, together with her retinue;
and with eighty thousand bodhisattvas, all of whom were irreversible and bound to only one more birth before attaining unsurpassed [enlightenment].
They had attained the *dhāraṇīs* for perfect enlightenment, were established in great eloquence, and turned the irreversible wheel of Dharma.

They had attended upon many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, and been praised by many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas. Their bodies and minds were permeated with loving-kindness; they were skilled in causing others to enter the wisdom of the Tathāgata, possessed great wisdom, and had reached the further shore of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
Their fame resounded through many hundreds of thousands of world-systems, and they were protectors of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of living beings.

They were as follows: the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta; Avalokiteśvara; Mahāsthāmaprāpta; Sarvārthasiddha; Nityodyukta; Anikṣiptadhura; Ratnapāṇi; Bhaiṣajyarāja; Bhaiṣajyasamudgata; Vyūharāja; Pradānaśūra; and Ratnacandra.
And with Pūrṇacandra, Mahāvikramin, Anantavikramin, Trailokyavikramin, Mahāpratibhāna,
Satatasamitābhiyukta,
Dharaṇīdhara, Akṣayamati, Mahāmati, Śāntamati, and Nakṣatrarāja.
and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnavairocana, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Siṃha;
together with the sixteen virtuous men (satpuruṣa) headed by Bhadrapāla, namely:
Bhadrapāla, Ratnākara, Susārthavāha, Naradatta, and Guhagupta.
And with Varuṇadatta and Indradatta and Uttaramati and Viśeṣamati and Vardhamānamati and Amoghadarśin and Susaṃprasthita and Suvikrāntavikramin and Anupamamati and Sūryagarbha and Dharaṇīndhara.
Thus, together with eighty thousand bodhisattvas headed by these,
and with Śakra, the lord of the gods, accompanied by a retinue of twenty thousand sons of the gods—
namely, the son of the gods Candra, Sūrya, Samantagandha, Ratnaprabha, and Avabhāsaprabha.
Thus, together with other prominent sons of the gods,
along with the four great kings and their retinues,
along with Brahmā Sahāpati and twelve thousand deities of the Brahmakāyika realm, and with the Brahmā Śikhin and the Brahmā Jyotiḥprabha.
Thus, together with twelve thousand leading sons of the gods from the Brahma-realm,
eight dragon kings accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of millions of dragons,
and four kinnara kings accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of millions of kinnaras;
Together with four sons of gods belonging to the Gandharva host, accompanied by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of Gandharvas;
together with four lords of the Asuras, accompanied by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of millions of Asuras;
and together with four lords of the Garuḍas, accompanied by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Garuḍas.
And together with King Ajātaśatru of Māgadha, the son of Vaidehī, he was accompanied by a retinue of many people, including kings, ministers, and citizens from the towns and countryside.
Now at that time, the Blessed One was surrounded and honored by the four assemblies; he was revered, esteemed, respected, worshipped, adored, and venerated.

At that moment, [he taught] the exposition of the gateway to the dhāraṇī of the array of the meditative absorption (*samādhi*) which manifests the range of the bodhisattvas and arrays the vow for the manifestation of that range.
He began to speak the Dharma discourse, the sūtra entitled *Caryāvaiśāradya*, a great vaipulya text followed by bodhisattvas and sustained by all the Buddhas;
at that time, rays of light of various colors issued forth, and by their radiance this triple-thousand great-thousand world-system was filled with a vast illumination.
By that light, the intermediate spaces between worlds—those voids filled with ruins, shrouded in blinding darkness—were revealed.

Where even these two— the moon and the sun, possessed of great supernatural power, great majesty, and great renown— do not prevail nor shine, there the beings who have been reborn do not see even their own outstretched arms;
yet, being fully suffused by that light, they see one another and recognize one another.
All the Buddha-fields were clearly visible; they were seen as clearly as far as the great Avīci hell and as far as the Brahma-world.
And all the sentient beings who were in those fields within the six realms of existence were all clearly seen.
Furthermore, whatever Buddhas, Blessed Ones, were staying, remaining, and maintaining themselves in those Buddha-fields, and whatever Dharma they were teaching—all of that was heard in its entirety.

And those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen in those Buddha-fields— whether they were practitioners of yoga, followers of the yoga-way, or those who had attained the fruits of the path, or those who had not— they all appeared there.

And those bodhisattva mahāsattvas in those Buddha-fields, who practiced the conduct of awakening through various and manifold objects of hearing, focal points, inclinations, causes, and skillful means— all of them also appeared there.
And all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who had entered final nirvana in those Buddha-fields were also visible;
and all those jewel-encrusted reliquary stupas of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who had entered final nirvana there were also visible.
A rain of flowers fell from the sky,
and the celestial drums of the Māras resounded with pleasing sounds;
and this entire great trichiliocosm world-system shook, trembled, and quaked in six ways, manifesting eighteen great omens.
It shook, it shook violently, it shook intensely;
it trembled, it trembled violently, it trembled intensely;
it quaked, it quaked violently, it quaked intensely.
It resounded, it resounded loudly, it resounded intensely; it roared, it roared loudly, it roared intensely.
At that moment, in all worlds, sounds were heard that were gladdening, satisfying, pleasing, beautiful to behold, refreshing, and delightful to the mind.
And there was no affliction, terror, fear, or paralysis for any sentient being;
nor were the lights of other divine worlds perceived.
All beings born in the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama became free from suffering and were endowed with every happiness.

And no sentient being was afflicted by passion, hatred, delusion, stinginess, envy, pride, hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, malice, or burning resentment. All sentient beings, moreover, possessed minds of mutual friendship and benevolence, regarding one another as their own mothers and fathers.

Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Ratnavairocana, having seen that great miracle of omens, suddenly rose, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows:
“O Blessed One, I have attained a state of supreme wonder and amazement: from where have these rays come?
Whose is this power?”
“Blessed One, what indeed is the cause here? What will be the condition?
Then the Blessed One said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnavairocana: “Listen, son of good family; attend well and thoroughly, and I shall speak to you.”
“Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! Ratnavairocana replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One then said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnavairocana:
“There is, noble son, in the southeastern direction...”

Beyond this world-system, past as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of millions of Ganges rivers, there is a world-system named Padmā, adorned with various qualities, stirred by various flowers, filled with various fragrances, embellished with jewel-trees,
and strewn with jewel-mountains.
There, the ground consists of blue beryl,
crowded with bodhisattvas and resounding with the sound of the Dharma; moreover, that ground of beryl is soft, like the touch of *acalindika* cloth, and pleasant to the touch.
When the foot is set down, it sinks four finger-breadths; when the foot is lifted, it rises four finger-breadths;
and it is strewn with various lotuses.
And there, trees made of the seven precious gems rise to a height of seven yojanas;
upon those trees hang divine saffron-colored garments,
and divine musical instruments play enchanting melodies.
And upon those trees, various birds utter sounds pleasing to the mind that correspond to the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment;
when the leaves of those trees touch one another, they produce the sound of divine musical instruments surpassing the fivefold orchestra;
and from each individual tree, a sublime fragrance exceeding the divine spreads for a thousand yojanas.
And upon those trees hung divine ornaments;
and within those trees were gabled mansions made of the seven precious gems, five hundred yojanas in height and one hundred and twenty-five yojanas in width.
And around those gabled pavilions on all four sides were gateways;
and outside those gateways, extending beyond the pavilions, were lotus ponds eighty yojanas in length and fifty yojanas in width.
And from those lotus ponds, there were stairs made of the seven precious gems extending in all four directions;
and the areas surrounding the lotus ponds were filled with lotuses made of the seven precious gems,
and each single lotus— (KpSū 9)
It is one yojana in extent.
And from those lotus filaments, bodhisattva mahāsattvas are born;
they take birth upon those lotus filaments during the first watch of the night.
And they pass that night in the full lotus posture,
experiencing the joy and bliss of liberation.
Then, at the time of dawn during that night, cool, fragrant, soft breezes, moving with a pleasant touch, begin to blow.
And they cause those closed flowers to bloom.
Then those bodhisattvas, having arisen from meditative concentration and having calmed themselves with the joy and bliss of liberation, descend upon the filaments of the lotuses;
entering into those gabled pavilions, they sit cross-legged on seats made of the seven precious gems and listen to the Dharma.
And within those tree-pavilions, in the four directions, there were mountains made of Jāmbūnada gold,
twenty yojanas in height and three yojanas in width;
and upon those mountains, many hundreds of thousands of sun-crystals, moon-crystals, sapphires, and jyotīrasa gems were seen here and there.

The radiance of the Buddha Padmottara fell upon those mountain jewels; and by that radiance of the Buddha and the radiance of the jewels, that entire world-system Padmā was suffused with a constant, sublime light.
Furthermore, the radiance of the moon and sun was no longer perceived there.
Except for when the lotuses close and the birds become silent, at which time the designation "night" occurs; by the opposite condition, it is "day.
And upon those mountains are gabled chambers made of blue beryl, sixty *yojanas* in height and twenty *yojanas* in width.

And from those gabled pavilions, in the four directions, there were archways made of the seven precious gems; and from those gabled pavilions there were couches made of the seven precious gems, upon which bodhisattvas bound by only one more birth sit and listen to the Dharma.
O son of good family, in that world-system Padmā, there is a Bodhi tree named Indra, three thousand yojanas in height and five hundred yojanas in width.
Its branches, leaves, and foliage extend for a thousand yojanas and are well-proportioned.
At the foot of that Bodhi tree is a lotus with a silver stalk five hundred yojanas in height;
its petals, numbering one hundred thousand times ten million, are made of gold and are fifteen yojanas in height.
And upon all the filaments were pericarp-bases made of emerald;
the filaments themselves were composed of the seven precious gems, ten yojanas in height and seven yojanas in width.
There, during the first night, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
“On all sides of that lotus throne of the Buddha were lotuses where the bodhisattvas were seated, and there they beheld the miraculous displays of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara.
When this was said, the bodhisattva Ratnavairocana addressed the Blessed One: “Of what form, Blessed One, is the Tathāgata Padmottara?”
“Did he perform the great miracles?

When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the bodhisattva Ratnavairocana: “During the last watch of this very night, at the time of dawn on the following morning, the Tathāgata Padmottara, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, performed such a miraculous feat of supernatural power.”
Having manifested himself as far as the Brahma-world, he emits from the crown of his head sixty hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of light rays;
with these rays, he illuminates the world-systems in the upward direction, as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field.
Furthermore, at that time, those bodhisattvas who were situated in the upward direction looked down toward the downward direction.
To them, neither Sumeru appears, nor the Cakravāḍa and Mahācakravāḍa mountain ranges, nor the Kāla mountains.
And those bodhisattvas from those world-systems who have received their predictions, who have attained meditative absorptions, and who have attained dhāraṇīs— [to them these things do not appear].
Those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who had attained patient acceptance (*kṣānti*), those who had transcended the stages (*bhūmi*), and those who were bound to only one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*)—

they too were suffused by that radiance; and having joined their palms in reverence, they gazed upon the body of the Tathāgata Padmottara, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*).

Having seen his body adorned with the eighty secondary marks, and having seen that assembly of bodhisattvas, the world-system Padmā, and the magnificent arrays of qualities of that buddha-field, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas were filled with supreme joy and gladness;
they had come from world-systems as numerous as the atoms within the supreme buddha-fields, beyond all calculation.

Leaving their respective world-systems by the power of their supernatural faculties (*ṛddhi*), those bodhisattvas arrived at the world-system Padma in order to honor, pay homage to, and attend upon the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara.

And that noble son, the Tathāgata Padmottara, having extended his tongue-faculty from his mouth, [covered] this entire four-continent world-system with his tongue-faculty while they were seated, standing, or walking.
He covered [the assembly].

And those bodhisattvas who were absorbed in meditative attainments there emerged from their samādhis, and the entire assembly became intent upon performing acts of worship for the Tathāgata Padmottara.
Then, noble son, the Tathāgata Padmottara, having withdrawn the miraculous manifestation of his tongue-faculty, [continued].

Furthermore, the Tathāgata Padmottara, from every part of his body and from every single pore, emitted sixty hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of light rays; having pervaded with a magnificent radiance the world systems in each of the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, he—
Those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who had attained meditative concentration were prophesied from those world-systems;
those bodhisattva mahāsattvas also arrived at the world-system Padmā by means of their own miraculous power, through the splendor of their respective buddha-fields, before Padmottara.
In order to see, pay homage to, worship, and attend upon the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.

Then, noble son, the Tathāgata Padmottara, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, having withdrawn his miraculous power, turned for the entire assembly of bodhisattvas the righteous wheel of Dharma called the Irreversible Wheel.

He set it in motion for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the sake, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans, and for the purpose of fulfilling the Mahāyāna.”
Thus ends the first chapter, titled "Setting in Motion the Wheel of Dharma," in the Mahāyāna sūtra *The White Lotus of Compassion*. // 1 //
(KpSū 14) The Second Chapter: The Gateway to Dhāraṇīs.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ratnavairocana addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Venerable Blessed One, how is night and day reckoned in the world-system Padmā?"
What kind of sounds are heard there? With what kind of intention are those bodhisattvas endowed? Or by what dwelling do they dwell?
The Blessed One said: “Noble son, the world-system Padma is constantly illuminated by the light of the Buddha.
There, when the flowers close and the birds become silent, [it is known that the night has come].”
When the Blessed One and those bodhisattvas sport with meditative absorptions and experience the joy and bliss of liberation,
then it is known as night;
but when those flowers are stirred by the wind, [it is known as day].
Birds warbled melodiously,
a rain of flowers fell from above,
and in the four directions, winds blew that were supremely fragrant, charming, soft, and pleasant to the touch.

And the Blessed One, having arisen from that meditative absorption, set aside the discourse on the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas for the sake of the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, and taught the Dharma of the Bodhisattva-piṭaka;
by that means, a day was made known there.
Furthermore, O son of good family, the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, were never separated there from the sound of "Buddha" and the sound of "Dharma."

By means of the word "Saṅgha," the word "fearlessness," the word "unconditioned," the word "non-arising," the word "non-ceasing," the word "peaceful," the word "calmed," the word "thoroughly pacified," the word "great loving-kindness," the word "great compassion," the word "the non-arising of phenomena," and the word "attainment of the stage of consecration."
They are never separated from the words "Buddha" and "Bodhisattva";
those bodhisattvas constantly hear such sounds.
Furthermore, noble son, as for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been reborn in the world-system Padmā:

Or, all those who shall be reborn will be endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, possessing a radiance extending for a league, and being of a nature not subject to falling into the lower realms until they reach the limit of enlightenment.
All those Bodhisattvas will possess minds of loving-kindness, gentle minds, untroubled minds, disciplined minds, and patient minds.
With concentrated minds, serene minds, unobstructed minds, pure minds, virtuous minds, minds delighted in the Dharma,
minds intent on pacifying the afflictions of all sentient beings, minds equal to the earth, minds that take no delight in worldly discourse,
minds that take delight in supramundane discourse, minds seeking all wholesome qualities, [they were established] in the state beyond acquisitions.

With minds constantly applied, with minds pacified regarding sickness, old age, and death, with minds that burn away all afflictions, with minds that pacify all fetters, and with minds that do not conceive pride toward any phenomena;
they possess the power of intention, the power of application, the power of conditions, the power of aspiration, the power of unwavering penetration through the insubstantial,
the power of profound conviction, the power of roots of goodness, the power of meditative concentration, the power of learning, the power of ethical discipline, and the power of relinquishment.

They possess the power of patience, the power of vigor, the power of meditative concentration, the power of wisdom, the power of tranquility, the power of insight, the power of the superknowledges, the power of mindfulness, the power of awakening, the power of utterly destroying all Māras, the power of crushing all the forces of Māra, the power of subduing all opponents through the Dharma, and the power of crushing all afflictions.

And those bodhisattvas who have been born, or will be born, in the world-system Padmā are indeed those who have performed services under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas and have planted roots of merit.

Furthermore, those bodhisattvas who have been born, or will be born, in that Buddha-field, the world-system Padmā, subsist on meditation, subsist on the Dharma, and subsist on fragrance, just like the gods.
They belong to the Brahmakāyika realm,
and there no food consisting of mouthfuls is known;
furthermore, even the name of anything unwholesome does not exist there in any way whatsoever.
And there, in every respect, even the name of "woman" does not exist,
nor does even the designation for it; and there, in every respect, the word "suffering" does not exist.

In every respect, there is no word for "pleasant" or "unpleasant," and so forth; there is no word for "affliction," no grasping, and herein there is no darkness, no foul odor, no fatigue of mind, no fatigue of body, and no word for the hells, the animal realm, or the world of Yama;
even the designation of "states of woe" does not exist.

There were no thorns, thickets, stones, or pebbles; neither fire, nor the moon and sun, nor the forms of stars; neither great oceans, nor Mount Sumeru, nor the Cakravāḍa mountains, nor the intermediate spaces between worlds, nor the Black Mountains, nor dung-stones, nor dust-mountains;
there was no sound of clouds or rain, nor any sound of turbid winds.
In every respect, the word "unfortunate rebirth" does not exist;
in every respect, the word "inauspicious state" does not exist.
Furthermore, the world-system Padma is constantly filled with the splendor of Buddhas, the splendor of Bodhisattvas, the splendor of merit, and the splendor of jewels, pervaded by a sublime radiance.
And here, indeed, the beautiful and affectionate birds, with their respective songs, proclaimed the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment.
Then the Bodhisattva Ratnavairocana said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, how great is that world-system Padmā?

How long has that Tathāgata Padmottara remained, stayed, and maintained himself, and taught the Dharma, by whom the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment was realized not long ago this very night?"
How long will the True Dharma remain after he has entered parinirvāṇa?
How long will those bodhisattvas who have been born, or will be born, in the lotus world-system, that buddha-field, continue to abide?
Are those bodhisattvas deprived of the sight of the Buddha, the hearing of the Dharma, and attendance upon the Saṅgha, or are they not?
What was the name of that world-system Padmā in the past?
Or how long ago did the sun of the Jina set there, immediately after which the Tathāgata Padmottara awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment?

And what is the cause for some seeing the miraculous displays and the supernatural feats of the Buddhas—the Blessed Ones who perform such miracles in other Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions?
“Why do some not see it?
The Blessed One said, “It is just as if, noble son, Sumeru, the king of mountains,
were sixty-eight thousand yojanas in height and eighty-four thousand yojanas in breadth.”
Suppose some man were to come who was heroic and powerful,
and by the power of his concentration, he were to break that Sumeru, the king of mountains, down to the size of a mustard seed;
those mustard seeds would be beyond counting.
It is not possible for anyone, except through the knowledge of an omniscient one, to count those mustard seeds;
as many mustard seeds as there are, so many four-continent worlds would be their measure.
The Buddha-field Padmā is filled with bodhisattvas, just as the world-system Sukhāvatī is filled with bodhisattvas.
Noble son, the lifespan of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara—while he remains, stays, maintains himself, and teaches the Dharma—is thirty intermediate kalpas.
Noble son, after the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara has passed into parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma will remain for ten intermediate kalpas.
And as for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have been born or will be born in that world-system Padmā, their lifespan shall measure forty intermediate kalpas.
Furthermore, noble son, formerly that world-system Padmā was named Candanā;
however, it was neither so pure nor so filled with pure beings as this world-system Padmā is now.
In the world-system Candanā, O son of good family, there was a Tathāgata named Candrottama— an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha,
endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.
He, too, taught the Dharma for twenty intermediate kalpas.
At the time of his final nirvāṇa,
some bodhisattvas, through the power of their vows, departed for other buddha-fields.
And to those bodhisattvas who remained, he said this: "Tonight, in the middle watch, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottama will pass into parinirvāṇa.

After the Blessed One has passed into parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma will remain for ten intermediate kalpas. Who, immediately following the disappearance of the True Dharma, will realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening?"
Furthermore, at that time, there was a bodhisattva named Gaganamudra,
who had been prophesied by the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottama through his former vow:
"Noble son, after I have passed into parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain for ten intermediate kalpas."
"In the first watch of the night my true Dharma will disappear;
in that very same night, in the final watch, you will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

You shall become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One, named Padmottara."
At that time, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas approached the place where the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Bhagavān Candrottama was;

having approached, all those bodhisattvas, through the power of their meditative concentration, performed various kinds of bodhisattva transformations before the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottama.

Having made offerings to the Tathāgata and circumambulated him three times, they said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable Blessed One, we wish to pass these ten intermediate kalpas with our minds focused on cessation.
Then, noble son, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottama [addressed] the Bodhisattva Gaganamudra.

Addressing the Mahāsattva, he said this: "Take up, noble son, this entrance into the dhāraṇī-door of the aspects of omniscience, which was taught by all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past and the future for the sake of Bodhisattvas consecrated as crown princes;

and those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who currently reside, stay, and maintain themselves in all the world-systems throughout the ten directions—they too [have taught it] for the sake of the Bodhisattvas consecrated as crown princes."

Those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who will appear in the future time, they too will teach this entrance into the dhāraṇī-door of the aspects of omniscience to the Bodhisattvas who have been consecrated to the position of crown prince.
It is as follows: *jalijalini mahājalini phutke butke sammade mahāsammade devāṃ aṭi caṭi ṭake ṭharaṭhakke amimakasi*.
Hilicili-tili, Ruruke Mahāruruke, Jaye Durjaye Jayamati, Śānte Śāntanirghoṣaṇi, Amūle Ale Amūlaparicchinne, Mārasainyavitrāsane, Mukte Muktapariśuddhe, Abhīte Bhayamocane,
Bhāradroharaṇā Dānta Vidyāvidyā Varottame!

The subduing of adversaries, the favoring of those who speak the Dharma, and the protection of those who speak the Dharma— this is the phrase that elucidates the basis of conviction regarding the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*).
In the aspiration for Buddhahood, in being without "mine," in being without immersion, in the non-distinctive meaning, in the determination of meaning, in the world’s conviction, and in cultivation—
these are the phrases that elucidate the basis of conviction regarding the four lineages of the noble ones (*āryavaṃśa*).

In speech, you speak; in holding, you hold; in the secret, the auspicious, the bestower of the auspicious, the fruit thereof, the supreme fruit, the non-fruitless, O Nila, the well-released, the unreleased, the completely released, the unafraid, the one who possesses liberation, the fruit of liberation, the unyoked, as if in heaven, in the light, in delight, equal, the measure, non-violence, thus far, having gone, not having gone, all worlds, the unshakable, the unblemished, the stainless, the one whose mind is slain.
For those who have entered the foremost of dwellings, whether fruitless or with fruit— this is the stage of resolute conviction for these three who are protected.
(KpSū 23)
From dullness, one is not to be described as non-removing; this is the fruit, the fruit of discipline. For the sake of its full attainment, behold the All-pervading One:
Sāmantra, Anumanta, Akumanta, Chedāvane, Mantrasta, Daśabala, Vigrahastha, Isusthita, Sunikhama, Tīkṣṇamati, Āloka, Atitṛṣṇā, and Adimati.
In the *Pratyutpanna-buddha-pūrvaprahāra*, this is the section revealing the stage of resolve for the four right efforts (*samyakprahāṇa*).
*anye manye mane mamane vire virate śame śamitā viśānte mukte nirakṣame same samasame kṣaye akṣaye ajiti śānte samiṣṭhe dhāraṇī ālokāvabhāse ratnavrate raśmyavate jñānavate.*

Like Mount Meru, it is the manifestation of destruction and the manifestation of the lamp of the world; this is the stage of illuminating the words of conviction regarding the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*).

It is the manifestation of the appearance of the eye and the manifestation of the light of gnosis (*jñāna*); in its radiance, it transcends the level of all the sense faculties, and in every way, it brings all exhaustion to an end at the mouth of the bull.
O Lord who observes the worlds,
this is the section on the manifestation of the stage of resolute belief regarding the four bases of psychic power.
(KpSū 24)

O Immovable One! O Buddha of firm movement! O Being, grant me success! O Trembling One! O Prohibited One! O Smahiddhe! O Parekasire! O Some! O Caṇḍe! O Datve! O Acale! O Acale! O Apare! O Vicivale! O Nipare! O Pracacale! O Prasare! O Anayan! O Prabhāvini! O Same! O Nijase! O Grakrame! O Nayute! In the practice of recitation, may there be trembling and power.
This is the phrase that elucidates the basis for conviction regarding the faculties and the powers:
*puṣpe supuṣpe drumaparihāre abhayarucire cekaratke akṣayamastu ninile mamale pañcaśiśire lokasya vijñāne nayasaṃgṛhīte ca yukte succendena*.
This is the phrase that elucidates the basis for conviction regarding the seven factors of enlightenment.

O Cakra-vajra! O you who have entered the meditative absorption of loving-kindness (*maitrī*), who have transcended, who are the banner of compassion, who gaze with the form of joy, who are perfected in patience, who are without spokes, supreme, fierce, fierce, rootless, the root, and the means of accomplishment!
This is the word that illuminates the state of resolve regarding the four grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*).

O you who turn the wheel, the holder of the wheel, the possessor of the excellent wheel, the supreme, the one who sends forth, the one who strikes down, the one who holds, the one who has transcended the formless realm, the one who roars, according to the breaking of the tongue, according to the *niṃbara*, according to the fire, according to the other, in the conduct of the destroyer of fear, the one who dwells in the peak of fearlessness.

The accomplishment of truth; the accomplishment of vigor that overcomes old age and impurity; the accomplishment of the path; the accomplishment of meditative concentration; the accomplishment of wisdom; the accomplishment of liberation; the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation; the accomplishment of the constellations; the accomplishment of the moon; the accomplishment of the sun.

The feet of the Tathāgata, increasing by four [syllables each], are marvelous yet not marvelous; he is the perfectly awakened one, the unawakened, the awakened here, the awakened there; he who has gone beyond others, the ungraspable, the ungraspable, the pure, the very pure; O dweller in the house of blessings at the end of that place, the purifier, the complete purifier; the one whose movement is ceased and stilled, the destroyer, the binder of destruction, the cutter, the cutter of holes, O supreme one, come here to my heart.
In the ocean, filled with the roar of destruction, in the breaking, in the *bhire-bhire*, in the *ruṣara*, in the refuge, in the rending, it proceeds in the *varaṇāḍaya*.

O *vidranvumā*, O *varakhumā*, O celibate one (*brahmacārin*), O you who delight in Indra (*indravani*), O you who possess firm resolve (*dhidhirāyani*), O you who sport as the Great Lord (*maheśvaralalani*), O you who are sufficient for my life-force (*mamasume*), O you who are sufficient (*alamini*), O you who deceive with a single syllable (*ekākṣaraci vaṃcani*), you move through the world. O *ābhicaṇḍāla*, O hero (*sūre*), all the gods (*sarvasurā*) and the gods of the lower realms (*āvarasurā*) have been purified again.

"O wise ones, this is the chapter on the manifestation of resolve regarding the ten powers, within the gate of the *dhāraṇī* empowered by the Buddha, which was proclaimed here in Gandhāra by the sage Āyina Kaṇḍi, who has ascended to the stage of *bhiruhiṇī*, who is perfected in measure and possesses the vision of measure."
(KpSū 26) Immediately upon the Blessed One’s commencement of this entrance into the gateway of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience,
this trichiliocosm great thousandfold world-system shook, trembled, and quaked in six ways.
It quaked, trembled, and shook; it was agitated, stirred, and thoroughly convulsed; it roared, thundered, and resounded; it rose up, sank down, and heaved.
And such a radiance appeared that world-systems in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of more than countless Ganges rivers, became suffused with a sublime light.
At that time, neither Sumeru, nor the Cakravāḍa mountains, nor the Mahācakravāḍa mountains appeared within the range of his vision;
rather, world-systems in the ten directions, beyond all calculation, were seen as level as the palm of a hand.
Furthermore, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who dwell in world-systems in the ten directions, beyond all calculation, [were also seen].

Those who had attained meditative concentration (*samādhi*), mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇī*), and patient acceptance (*kṣānti*) vanished from their respective buddha-fields by means of the power of the Tathāgata and came to this Sahā world-system. Having arrived at Vulture Peak Mountain, they approached the Blessed One;

having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and, having performed worship of the Blessed One with various kinds of manifold bodhisattva transformations, they sat down right there in order to hear the entrance into the gateways of the *dhāraṇīs* of the aspects of omniscience.
And countless gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, kumbhāṇḍas, and piśācas approached the Gṛdhrakūṭa mountain and the place where the Blessed One was;
having arrived, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One.
They sat to one side in order to hear this entry into the gate of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience.
And all those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who had assembled there saw the buddha-field Padma,
and the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Padmottara, surrounded by a great host of bodhisattvas.

Immediately after the Blessed One had proclaimed this entry into the door of the *dhāraṇī* of the aspects of omniscience, seventy-two times as many bodhisattva mahāsattvas as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges attained this *dhāraṇī*.
Having attained the *dhāraṇī*, those bodhisattvas beheld the Buddha Bhagavans residing in world-systems throughout the ten directions— numbers beyond calculation—
and they beheld all the magnificent arrays of qualities of those buddha-fields.
Filled with wonder, they performed worship to the Buddha through the power of their meditative absorption and the miraculous transformations of the bodhisattvas, and then stood there.

The Blessed One said to them: "Noble sons, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates this entrance into the dhāraṇī-gateways of the aspects of omniscience, he attains eighty-four thousand dhāraṇī-gateways."
He attains seventy-two thousand gateways of dhāraṇīs and sixty thousand gateways of samādhis,
and this dhāraṇī (KpSū 28).
Having attained this, the bodhisattva mahāsattva attains great loving-kindness and attains great compassion.
Merely for the sake of attaining this samādhi, the bodhisattva mahāsattva realizes the thirty-seven factors conducive to enlightenment and attains the knowledge of omniscience;
herein lies the complete acquisition of all the qualities of a buddha.
Having realized this dhāraṇī by its very nature, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, teach the Dharma to sentient beings and do not pass into final nirvāṇa too quickly.
Behold, noble sons, how through the power of this dhāraṇī— the entrance into the gateway of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience— this great earthquake has manifested.
And there was a great radiance, by which radiance infinite and boundless buddha-fields were suffused with a sublime light;

and by that radiance these infinite and boundless bodhisattvas had come from infinite and boundless buddha-fields in order to hear this entrance into the door of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience.

And whatever infinite and boundless gods of the desire realm and the form realm, as well as nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, humans, or non-humans, who are here in this Sahā world-system, upon hearing this entrance into the door of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience, they become irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment through that entrance into the door of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience.
Furthermore, while writing it, one is never separated from the vision of the Buddha, the hearing of the Dharma, the service of the Saṅgha, and so on, up to unsurpassed parinirvāṇa.
When a bodhisattva recites this entrance into the dhāraṇī-door of the aspects of omniscience, they exhaust all heavy karmic actions without remainder and,
upon the transition of birth, enters the first stage.
And when a bodhisattva mahāsattva cultivates this entrance into the dhāraṇī-door of the aspects of omniscience, [they likewise attain these results].
If that bodhisattva has committed and accumulated the five deeds of immediate retribution (*pañcānantarya-karmāṇi*), even those will be completely exhausted,
such that by means of that very transformation of birth he enters the first stage (*bhūmi*);
whereas for one who has not committed the deeds of immediate retribution, all other karmas are completely exhausted without remainder in that same lifetime.
And by means of a single rebirth, he enters the first stage (*bhūmi*).

Even one who neither meditates nor recites [the sūtra], but merely hears it and ties a silk ribbon (*paṭṭa*) around the head of the Dharma-preacher, to him the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones—equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā—residing, remaining, and maintaining themselves in other world-systems, will grant their approval, saying, "Well done! (sādhukāra).

Those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, will also grant him the prophecy of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; and before long, that Bodhisattva will be consecrated to the position of crown prince by the relinquishing of his turban, and he will become bound to only one more birth before attaining unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
In the same way, whoever performs worship with incense will, before long, become a recipient of the fragrance of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
and by performing worship with flowers,
one obtains the unexcelled flowers of wisdom from the Dharma-preacher.
By giving food, drink, and edibles to a Dharma-preacher, the Bodhisattva becomes a recipient of the unsurpassed food of the Tathāgata;
by clothing the Dharma-preacher, he becomes a recipient of the unsurpassed complexion of a Tathāgata;
and whoever covers the Dharma-preacher with jewels will, before long, become a recipient of the thirty-seven jewels of the factors conducive to enlightenment.
Thus, noble son, this entrance into the gateway of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience is of great significance for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas.
Why is that?
Because herein the entire Bodhisattvapiṭaka is taught in its entirety.
And by this entrance into the dhāraṇī-door of the aspects of omniscience, a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains unimpeded eloquence and attains the fourfold set of pleasing qualities.
Noble son, when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottama spoke thus to the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gaganamudrā through these entrances into the dhāraṇī-door of the aspects of omniscience...
In that very way, there was an earthquake,
and a great radiance appeared in the world; and incalculable Buddha-fields in the ten directions became suffused with a sublime light.
In this very way, uneven places on the earth appear as level as the palm of the hand.
And those Bodhisattvas who have assembled there behold the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in Buddha-fields in the ten directions that transcend all calculation.

In the same way, from incalculable Buddha-fields in the ten directions, incalculable bodhisattvas approached the Candanā world-system in order to pay homage to and attend upon the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottama.
"In order to hear this very entrance into the dhāraṇī-door of the aspects of omniscience."
In that regard, noble son, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottama addressed the bodhisattva mahāsattvas: "I recall, noble son, those bodhisattvas who are bound to only one more birth;
having dwelt for these ten intermediate kalpas with their minds absorbed in cessation, the remaining bodhisattvas [shall enter] this Gaganamudra..."
From the presence of that Bodhisattva, they heard this very entrance into the door of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience, which is the Bodhisattva-piṭaka, for ten intermediate kalpas.
Having heard the Dharma for these ten intermediate kalpas, [they went] to those countless Buddha-fields in the ten directions.
While those who had transcended all calculation remained, stayed, and lived, they developed a serene confidence in the presence of the Blessed Ones;
having planted roots of merit through that cause of mental serenity, they performed various kinds of bodhisattva miracles as an offering to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottama.

They said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, after the passing of these ten intermediate kalpas, will the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gaganamudra turn the unsurpassed, righteous wheel of Dharma? Candrottama replied: "It is even so, noble son."
After the passing of these ten intermediate kalpas, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganamudrā will fully awaken to unsurpassed,

perfect, and complete enlightenment; on that very same night, having passed away, he will turn the wheel of Dharma in accordance with the truth, and for ten intermediate kalpas, he will teach here to the Bodhisattvas this very entrance into the dhāraṇī-door of the aspects of omniscience.
There, whichever bodhisattva mahāsattva hears the Dharma from him and, having heard that Dharma, plants roots of merit,
at the time when the bodhisattva Gaganamudra awakens to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment—

having awakened to that enlightenment and set in motion the righteous wheel of Dharma, the supreme wheel, the irreversible wheel— he will establish many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of bodhisattvas in the state of irreversibility.

Those bodhisattvas who here, for ten intermediate eons, shall hear this Dharma— the entrance into the door of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience— being taught by him, having heard that Dharma at that time, will become bound to only one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*).
But those bodhisattvas who shall hear it for an entire eon, at that time they will enter the [bodhisattva] stages (*bhūmi*).
"And they shall become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
at that very moment, they will fully obtain this dhāraṇī," having said this, [he continued]:

The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrottama, having displayed various miraculous feats within the domain of the Buddhas to the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and having demonstrated the Nārāyaṇa samādhi to the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gaganamudra,
empowered his own body as being composed of adamant and manifested the Prabhāvyūha samādhi.

By him the wheel of Dharma was set in motion; here, for ten intermediate kalpas, he teaches this Dharma— the entrance into the dhāraṇī-doors of the aspects of omniscience for bodhisattvas— and by the power of the Buddhas, he is seen manifesting in all Buddha-fields, illuminated by the primary and secondary marks.
He demonstrates the vajra-maṇḍala samādhi, by which he, having well set in motion the wheel of Dharma at the seat of awakening, teaches the Dharma to the bodhisattvas;
he demonstrates the wheel-array samādhi.

Knowing that by turning the wheel of Dharma he establishes many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of living beings in the state of non-retrogression for the sake of turning the wheel of Dharma, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganamudra, together with an immeasurable assembly of Bodhisattvas, performed worship to the Blessed One; having entered their respective gabled palaces, they remained there, along with Candrottama.

On that very night, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha entered final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder; and those bodhisattvas, having passed away on that same night, performed worship for the body of that Blessed One and entered their respective gabled palaces.
Other bodhisattvas, however, departed for their own respective buddha-fields.

And those bodhisattvas there who were bound to only one more birth passed these ten intermediate kalpas in the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodha-samādhi*). The bodhisattva mahāsattva Gaganamudra taught the Dharma concerning those bodhisattva mahāsattvas,
and he planted roots of merit for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas during those ten intermediate kalpas.
This very night he has awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
and today he has set in motion the wheel of Dharma and performed the great miracle.
Many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of living beings were established in non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. Furthermore,

while this entrance into the door of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience was being taught, eighty hundred thousand nayutas of bodhisattvas attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena,
and ninety-two kotis of living beings were established in non-retrogression regarding unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

And seventy-two nayutas of bodhisattvas attained this dhāraṇī, the entrance into the gate of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience; and among gods and humans beyond counting, the resolve for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment was generated.”
(KpSū 35) Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Ratnacandravairocana addressed the Blessed One in this way: “Blessed Lord, endowed with what qualities does a bodhisattva mahāsattva obtain this dhāraṇī?”
The Blessed One said: "Noble son, endowed with four qualities, a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains this dhāraṇī.
What are the four?
Here, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is established in the four noble lineages."
In which four?
Here, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is content with whatever robe he receives; being content with whatever robe he receives, he speaks in praise of such contentment.
He does not engage in improper seeking for the sake of robes;
he does not feel distress when he has not obtained a robe, and having obtained a robe, he uses it without attachment.

Unattached, ungreedy, unbound, undeluded, without fixation, and not having fallen into obsession, seeing the danger and knowing the escape, he partakes [of food]. In this first noble lineage, the bodhisattva mahāsattva is established.

As it is with robes, so it is with alms-food and bedding and seats. Furthermore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is content with whatever medicinal requisites for the sick he may receive from time to time; and being content with whatever medicinal requisites for the sick he receives from time to time, he speaks in praise of such contentment.
For the sake of medicinal requisites for the sick, he does not engage in improper seeking. Not obtaining medicinal requisites for the sick, he does not become distressed;
having obtained them, he uses them without attachment, being free from greed, unbound, undeluded, without infatuation, and not fallen into obsession, seeing the danger and understanding the escape.
He becomes established in these four noble lineages (*āryavaṃśa*).
Endowed with these four qualities, a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains and cultivates this dhāraṇī.

Furthermore, endowed with five other qualities, a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains this dhāraṇī that enters the gateway of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience (*sarvajñatākāradhāraṇīmukhapraveśadhāraṇī*).
By which five?
Here, a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells himself possessed of ethical discipline,
restrained by the restraint of the Prātimokṣa.
Perfect in conduct and range of activity, seeing danger even in the slightest faults,
he trains himself by undertaking the precepts of training;
moreover, seeing others who are devoid of ethical discipline, he encourages them toward the perfection of morality, disciplines them, establishes them, and settles them therein.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva is endowed with this first quality.

Furthermore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, having raised up beings who have fallen into the calamity of views and wrong views, causes them to adopt right view, disciplines them, establishes them, and settles them therein;
by this second [quality].
A bodhisattva mahāsattva is endowed with this dharma.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva encourages, disciplines, introduces, and establishes beings who have fallen into misconduct and misfortune in right conduct;
by this third dharma, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is endowed.
Furthermore, he encourages, disciplines, introduces, and establishes beings who have failed in their intention (*āśaya*) in the perfection of intention.
Endowed with this fourth quality, a bodhisattva mahāsattva [is so called].

Furthermore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva encourages, disciplines, and introduces beings who have set out in the vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (*anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi*).
Endowed with this fifth quality, a bodhisattva mahāsattva—
endowed with these five qualities— a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains this dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, endowed with six other qualities, a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains this dhāraṇī.
By which six?
Here, a bodhisattva mahāsattva himself becomes one who is much-heard, a retainer of what has been heard, and a storehouse of what has been heard;

for him, those teachings that are virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, and virtuous in the end, excellent in meaning and excellent in phrasing, which are unique, complete, and perfectly pure—(KpSū 38)
Proclaiming a holy life that is completely pure and cleansed, they speak in praise of it;
such are the many teachings he has heard, retained verbally, mastered through recitation, examined with the mind, and well-penetrated by vision.
Being thus one of great learning, he encourages, disciplines, settles, and establishes other beings who have not heard them in the state of great learning.
He is endowed with this first quality.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is free from envy and free from stinginess;
he encourages other beings who are overcome by envy and stinginess toward non-envy and the perfection of generosity, and establishes them therein.
By this second quality, a bodhisattva mahāsattva is endowed.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva is by nature one who does not harm sentient beings and is a bestower of fearlessness;
he liberates from various calamities those beings who are afflicted by them.
He is free from hypocrisy and is not a chatterer; he is without guile and is free from deceit, and he dwells frequently in emptiness.
Endowed with these six qualities, a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains this dhāraṇī of entering the gateway of the dhāraṇīs of the aspects of omniscience.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva endowed with such qualities [expounds] all these [teachings] both concisely and in detail for seven years. (KpSū 39)

Having recited these Dravidian mantra-words three times during the day while seated in the five-fold posture (*pañcamuṇḍala*), having established mindfulness directed toward the body, and dwelling in emptiness, one should dispel these very Dravidian mantra-words by rising up and constantly recollecting the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, as they abide, remain, and move throughout the ten directions;
and by cultivating the constant recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*) for seven years, one [attains] this *dhāraṇī* that enters the gateway of the *dhāraṇī* of all-knowing aspects.
The bodhisattva mahāsattva attains it. By the attainment of this dhāraṇī, the bodhisattva mahāsattva attains such a noble eye of wisdom (*prajñācakṣus*) that,

by means of that eye of wisdom, he sees everything— those [Buddhas] who are staying, maintaining themselves, and subsisting, and who are displaying great miracles, in Buddha-fields in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
Having seen the display of smiles by those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, he attains eighty-four thousand gateways of dhāraṇīs, seventy-two thousand gateways of samādhis,
and sixty thousand gateways of dharmas.
And when a bodhisattva mahāsattva is established in this dhāraṇī that is the entrance to the dhāraṇīs of the aspects of omniscience, he attains great loving-kindness and attains great compassion.
If a bodhisattva mahāsattva by whom this dhāraṇī has been attained should have committed the five deeds of immediate retribution, [they are purified].
In his next birth they go to complete exhaustion;
in the third birth those karmas become destroyed without remainder.
And he enters the tenth stage.
However, for that bodhisattva who has not committed the deeds of immediate retribution, all other karmic obstructions go to complete exhaustion;
through a single transition of birth, he transcends the ten stages.
Before long, one now attains the thirty-seven factors conducive to enlightenment and attains the knowledge of omniscience.
Noble son, this entrance into the door of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience is thus of great benefit to bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas.

Constantly and continuously, having witnessed the miracle of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, through their display of smiles, the bodhisattva mahāsattva becomes endowed with such a range of supernatural power (*ṛddhiviṣaya*) that,

after making offerings to as many Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges within world-systems as numerous as the grains of sand in the river Ganges, and having heard the Dharma from those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, they return to this very buddha-field, possessing various kinds of meditative concentrations (*samādhi*), patiences (*kṣānti*), and mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇī*).

In this way, noble son, the entrance into the gateway of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience for bodhisattva mahāsattvas leads to the exhaustion of karma and the increase of wholesome qualities.

And, noble son, those beings who hear the name of this dhāraṇī of the entrance into the gateway of the aspects of omniscience and of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Candrottama, [will likewise attain these benefits].
"Their all karmic obscurations will go to exhaustion, and they will become destined for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Then those bodhisattvas said this: "Venerable Blessed One, while we were with the past Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—who were staying, remaining, and maintaining themselves—we [did not hear] this..."
“The dhāraṇī has been heard and attained.
Others said, “By us [it was attained] after [the passage of time equal to] the sands of two Ganges rivers,” and others, “after three.”
Others say "by four," others say "by five," and others say "by six."
Others say "with seven," others say "with eight";
still others speak thus:

“Having heard this dhāraṇī for entering the gateway of the dhāraṇī of the aspects of omniscience from nine past perfectly enlightened ones, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā— while they were staying, remaining, and maintaining themselves— we have attained it in every aspect.”
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya spoke thus: "After ten Ganges-river-sands of kalpas had passed, there occurred a great eon named Santāraṇa.
At that time, this buddha-field was named Sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣita.

There, a Buddha appeared named Sālendrarāja, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One."

Surrounded by a community of monks numbering hundreds of thousands of nayutas of infinite koṭis, and likewise surrounded by bodhisattvas beyond calculation, he spoke this very dhāraṇī, the entrance into the gateway of the dhāraṇīs of all-knowing forms;
in his presence, I heard this dhāraṇī, and through cultivation, it was fully realized.

Thus, throughout immeasurable, more than immeasurable, and even more than incalculable eons, I have performed worship to the past perfectly enlightened Buddhas—while they were staying, remaining, and maintaining their lives—by means of incalculable bodhisattva-transformations.

Having planted immeasurable, incalculable, incomparable, and boundless roots of merit in the presence of each and every Buddha, I have gathered a mass of merit; by virtue of those roots of merit, I have been prophesied by many thousands of Buddhas.
Having observed the right time, I have wandered for a long time in saṃsāra solely by means of the scope of my vow;
because while wandering previously in saṃsāra, I did not fully awaken to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
I have now been consecrated by the Blessed One with the office of crown prince.
"And the turban of liberation has been bound upon my head of wisdom for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Then the Blessed One said this to the Bodhisattva Maitreya: "It is even so, Maitreya, that you have received from the presence of the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Sālendrarāja this dhāraṇī for entering the gateways of the dhāraṇīs of the aspects of omniscience."
Maitreya, if you so desire, after the passing of ten eons, you shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; yet, Maitreya,
just as your aspiration has been fulfilled, you are also capable, Maitreya, of entering the realm of nirvana without remainder very swiftly through unsurpassed knowledge.

And as for the fact that you, Maitreya, have remained delighted in saṃsāra for so long, all of that was by the power of your vow, awaiting the proper time; therefore, Maitreya, you have now received the status of crown prince from me, and you have also received the status of crown prince in the presence of the Tathāgatas of the past.”
Thereupon the Blessed One surveyed the entire assembly;

having looked upon the assembly of bodhisattvas, the assembly of monks, the assembly of nuns, laymen, and laywomen, as well as the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, humans, and non-humans, at that moment he spoke these mantra-words:

“The stage of the tamed, the stage of self-control, the stage of mindfulness, the stage of wisdom, the stage of fearlessness, the stage of analytical knowledge, the stage of non-removal, the stage of equanimity through the exhaustion of evenness, the stage of the exhaustion of birth— Manuja-vinmuja, Malanmuja, Visāgra, Daśāvate, Veśata, Teraṇa, Vesalagra, Śamuśavata, Vimati, Vimati-yopahira. (KpSū 44)

The lineage of the Vasiṣṭhas is thus proclaimed: for me, there is the seal of the Great One (*mekhamudrā*), the small one (*daharamudrā*), and the primordial water of wisdom (*prajñākṣābubu*). Those who have transcended the sequence of burning are possessed of faults; they are without essence, without foundation, unconditioned, and not blind. They possess meaning and power; through them, the two [extremes] are abandoned. They do not speak, nor do they act; they are equal, radiant, beloved, and possessed of beloved strength. Here and there, they perform what is beneficial and what is pleasant, and how so? Everywhere.
Sarvataru, Aniruddha, Dīrgha, Ṣaṇṭambhi, Bahuphala, Śataphala, and Śīṣṭavat— indeed,
the Blessed One revealed to the gods the points of resolute conviction associated with dependent origination;
while these were being revealed, sixty million gods attained the vision of the Truth.
"O Lalaha, Alaha, Nilaṃhare, Vacatakhya! This fruit is the supreme fruit, the fruit of discipline, the fruit of non-arising, the wheel of liberation, the wheel of wisdom, and the wheel of knowledge.
Through these words of inspired confidence, the minds of ten million gods were set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and they became established therein as non-retrogressive.
"Behold, O Māmatī! Anumata, Akumata,
Akumatī, Chīdratraka, Mantrastha, Deśabala, Vipravastha, Īśasthita, Atimati, Tīkṣṇamati, and Ālokaste rituṣṇa—
by these words of resolute conviction, the minds of sixty-four thousand nāgas were set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment."
And there, they became irreversible;
[namely] Aprabhāsa, Madana, Ahadya, Bhagadyota, Karaṇyakṣa, Siddhamati, Samantakṣobha, Alabala, Piṭakara,
Mahābala, Ojadara, Dharaṇi, Migalekṣa, Udākṣa, Kudākṣa, Kukākṣa, Viroca, Virūpamukha, and Akṣihasta.

With the words "Saṃkṣiptabala" and "Asurovina Asuropramardane," through these points of resolute belief, the minds of twelve koṭis of yakṣas were set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; they became irreversible right there.
When the meaning is profound, difficult to penetrate, and subtle, he does not become discouraged; he is honored by both gods and humans. He is joyful, exhilarated, and possesses wisdom.

O Hero, you have attained the *dhāraṇīs*, together with Indra, the gods, the *nāgas*, the *yakṣas*, the *asuras*, and the gods. You possess the analytical knowledge (*nirukti*) and its retinue, and you have obtained the analytical knowledge of language (*nirukta-lābhin*). You have obtained the retinue of mindfulness, wisdom, and intelligence, and you have obtained the stability of conduct and steadfastness (*gatidhṛti-lābhin*). (KpSū 46)
Having practiced in former beneficial deeds, possessing aspiration, possessing heroism, possessing long-standing vigor, and being possessed of fearlessness,
[enter] into the path-seal in the white portion, the direction-drawing, the removal of obstacles, the divine seal, the celestial seal, the yakṣa seal, the rākṣasa seal,
the sacrificial altar, the boundary of the altar, the heat, the intense heat, the burning, the devouring, the ninefold to be maintained, and the purification of the directions.

Through purity of speech, purity of the tongue, and the refinement of vocal expression— through the wisdom, intelligence, mindfulness, discernment, understanding, steadfastness, calculation, and reliance upon the wheel of victory, the wheel of emptiness, and the wheel of exhaustion— by means of these points of resolute conviction, the minds of fifty-six thousand asuras were set toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
And they are established as non-retrogressive.

There, the Blessed One addressed the bodhisattva named Vaiśāradyasamavasaraṇa: "It is rare, noble son, for Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas to appear in the world; rare, too, are these mantra-words, which are permeated by ethical discipline, meditative concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
For the benefit of sentient beings and for the sake of accomplishing the qualities of a bodhisattva, noble son, they have been [taught] by the Tathāgata."

Formerly, while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, he embraced generosity, self-control, restraint, patience, vigor, meditative concentration, and wisdom; he attended upon many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas,
giving gifts in some instances and maintaining ethical discipline in others.
In some places the holy life was practiced, in some places meditation was cultivated,
and in some places patience was developed.
In some places vigor was initiated, in some places concentration was accomplished, and in some places wisdom was cultivated.
"O son of good family, immeasurable, diverse, and manifold kinds of wholesome karma were performed by me, by virtue of which I have now attained this unsurpassed knowledge.
For many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of eons, while formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, the Tathāgata avoided false speech, slander, harsh words, and frivolous chatter."
“Various kinds of wholesome verbal action were practiced and cultivated by him,
by which he has now obtained a broad tongue;
for indeed, O son of good family, the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones do not speak otherwise.”

Then the Blessed One performed a feat of supernatural power (*ṛddhyabhisaṃskāra*) from that assembly; by means of that performed feat of supernatural power, he entered the meditative absorption named "The Convergence of All Merit" (*sarvapuṇyasamavasaraṇa*).
Extending his tongue from his mouth, he covered his own facial circle, and from that tongue—
Sixty koṭis of rays were emitted, and by those rays this trichiliocosm great thousandfold world system was pervaded with a magnificent radiance;
and by those rays, the hells, the animal realm, the world of Yama, the gods, and humans were all pervaded.

And those rays [of light] caused cool breezes to blow for those hell-beings whose bodies were being consumed by blazing fire; upon being touched by them, a pleasant sensation arose in them for that moment. And before each individual hell-being stood a manifestation of the Buddha, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and his form resplendent with the eighty secondary characteristics; seeing him, those hell-beings were filled with bliss.
Their bodies nourished by the sight of the Buddha, they thought upon seeing him: "It is through the power of this being that we have obtained pleasant sensations.
They then conceived love, serene faith, and reverence toward the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said to them, "O beings, speak these words:
'Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Saṅgha.
In this way, you will always be endowed with happiness."
Then those beings in the hells, having joined their palms in reverence, uttered these words:
"Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṅgha!
Thereupon, by that root of merit and by that clarity of mind, those beings in the hells passed away from there; some were reborn among the gods.
Some among them are reborn among humans;
and for those beings who have been born in the cold hells, warm winds blow.
As before, up until they are reborn among humans;
likewise, for the hungry ghosts (*preta*) and *piśācas* whose bodies are ablaze with hunger and thirst, those rays extinguish the fire of their hunger and produce a feeling of happiness.
Before each and every preta, a manifested form of the Buddha stands, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and his body radiant with the eighty minor characteristics.
Upon seeing him, those pretas experience joy and physical well-being from the sight of the Buddha, and they think:
"By the power of this being, we have obtained a pleasant sensation."
They conceived faith, love, and reverence toward the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said to them: "Come, you beings, utter these words:"
“Homage to the Buddha, homage to the Dharma, homage to the Saṅgha! By this, you shall always be endowed with happiness.
Then those hungry ghosts, having raised their joined palms, uttered these words:
“Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṅgha!
Then, by that root of merit, those beings who were hungry ghosts passed away from there; some were reborn among the gods, and others among humans.
In this way they exhorted the animals, and in this way they exhorted the humans.

Innumerable gods and humans approached the Blessed One, bowed their heads at his feet, and sat down to listen to the Dharma. At that time, innumerable hosts of gods and humans resolved their minds upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
And there, bodhisattvas beyond counting attained samādhi, kṣānti, and dhāraṇī.
Thus ends the second chapter, "The Gateway to Dhāraṇīs," in the *Śrīkaruṇāpuṇḍarīka*, a Mahāyāna sūtra. //2//
(KpSū 51) III.
The Third Chapter on the Bestowal of Gifts.
Then, when the Blessed One had withdrawn his own miraculous display, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śāntimati addressed the Blessed One as follows:

“Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, that the buddha-fields of other Blessed Buddhas are completely pure, free from defilement, free from the five corruptions, and adorned with various arrays of qualities;
and that all the bodhisattvas mahāsattvas therein are filled with various kinds of virtues and endowed with various forms of happiness,
while even the name of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas is not found there?”

Furthermore, from where does this arise? O Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, that the Blessed One has been born in a Buddha-field of five corruptions— having attained unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment while the corruption of lifespan, the corruption of the eon, the corruption of sentient beings, the corruption of views, and the corruption of afflictions were prevailing?

“And why does he teach the Dharma by taking as his basis the four assemblies and the three vehicles? Why has the Blessed One not taken hold of a completely pure buddha-field, one free from the five corruptions?
The Blessed One said:
“By the power of their vows, noble son, bodhisattvas take hold of a completely pure buddha-field; by the power of their vows, they take hold of an impure buddha-field.”
"O son of good family, because they are endowed with great compassion, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas take possession of impure Buddha-fields.
For what reason?
Because I made such a vow that I have now been born in a Buddha-field as wretched as this one, characterized by the five corruptions."
“Listen to that, Śāntimati, and attend to it well and thoroughly; I shall speak it to you.
“Very well, Blessed One,” the Bodhisattva Śāntimati replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this to them:
"Long ago, noble son, after incalculable eons equal to the sands of a single Ganges River had passed, there occurred in this buddha-field a great eon named Dhāraṇa.
And during that great eon, in that buddha-field, within that system of four continents, there was a universal monarch named Araṇemī, the ruler of the four continents."
Now, that Āraṇemin had a brahmin named Samudrareṇu who served as his domestic priest.

To him was born a son endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man, adorned with the eighty minor characteristics, possessing the signs of a hundred merits, radiating a fathom-wide halo, having the proportions of a banyan tree, and of such a lovely appearance that one could never tire of beholding him.
As soon as he was born, hundreds of thousands of gods performed worship and established his name as Samudragarbha.
At a later time, having gone forth, shaved off his hair and beard, and donned saffron-colored robes, he realized unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
A Tathāgata named Ratnagarbha appeared;
by turning the wheel of Dharma, that Blessed One established many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of living beings in the fruit of heaven and liberation.

At another time, surrounded and honored by many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of śrāvakas, he wandered on his tour through villages, towns, market towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals.
Traveling by stages, he arrived at a certain city where that universal monarch resided.
There, not far outside the city, in a grove named Jambūvana, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha was dwelling together with many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of disciples.

Thus King Araṇemin heard: "The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha has arrived in our realm and is dwelling in the Jambūvana Grove together with many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of śrāvakas."
"What if I were now to go forth?
Having approached him, I shall honor, revere, and respect that Tathāgata.
Then King Araṇemin, with the royal majesty of a king and great royal power, surrounded and escorted by many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of living beings, went out from the city.

He went toward the Jambūvana grove; having arrived there, he proceeded by vehicle as far as the ground was accessible to a vehicle, and then entered the park on foot, approaching the place where the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha was.
Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, circumambulated him three times, and sat down to one side.
To King Araṇemin, as he sat to one side, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the Dharma.
Having instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened him in many ways with a discourse on the Dharma, he became silent.

Then King Araṇemin, rising from his seat, draping his upper robe over one shoulder, and prostrating at the feet [of the Buddha], bowed with palms joined toward the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and addressed the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha:
"May the Blessed One consent to dwell with me for these three months together with the community of monks."
“I shall attend upon the Blessed One with robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick, as well as the community of monks.

O son of good family, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha signified his assent to King Araṇemin by remaining silent. Then, King Araṇemin, understanding the Blessed One’s assent through his silence, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and [departed] from the Blessed One...
...departed from his presence.
(KpSū 55) Then King Araṇemin summoned the provincial kings, the ministers, the high officials, the military commanders, the citizens, the country folk, and the servants.

Having addressed them, he said: "Village chiefs, let it be known that I have invited the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha, together with the community of monks, for these three months with all necessary provisions.
Therefore, whatever articles of enjoyment, requisites, attendants, services, or harem women I possess, I offer all of them with reverence to the Blessed One and the community of monks."

"Whatever personal articles you have—enjoyments, luxuries, attendants, services, and even the inner apartments—all of that you should respectfully offer to the Blessed One and the community of monks. They, too, offered it all.
Furthermore, the Householder Jewel, having made the entire auspicious garden out of Jāmbūnada gold, [offered it].

In that very garden, he had a gabled pavilion constructed for the sake of the Blessed One, made of the seven precious gems; and here, on all four sides, he had doors made of the seven precious gems constructed. The entire garden was adorned with trees made of the seven precious gems.

And those trees were decorated with various kinds of garments, various fine cloths, various parasols, various types of pearl necklaces, various kinds of ornaments, and various ornaments made of diverse precious gems.
He adorned those trees with fragrant scents and with flowers and fruits made of every kind of jewel.
And that entire park was adorned with many kinds of jewels,
strewn with various flowers, and seats were arranged there, covered with various silk cloths, fine fabrics, and upper garments.
That wheel-treasure also blazed in the sky above at a height of one man’s length, positioned outside the gabled hall and facing toward the Blessed One.
The elephant-treasure, entirely white, with seven limbs well-proportioned and firmly established, stood behind the Blessed One and held a jewel-tree over the Blessed One’s head.
And that tree was adorned with the seven precious gems, with various kinds of pearl necklaces, with diverse ornaments, with various garlands, and with silken cloths of many colors;
and a parasol made of the seven precious gems was placed over that tree.
