Behold, Great King, in the western direction, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddha-fields, there is a world-system named Indrasuvirājitā.
Therein dwells, remains, and maintains himself a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Indraghoṣeśvararāja, who teaches the Dharma to pure beings.
And in that Buddha-field, there are no Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
There is even a conventional designation;
however, no discourse concerning the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas is made there,
for only pure Mahāyāna discourse is found therein.
All beings there are born spontaneously,
and even the name of a woman is not known there.
All these qualities exist in that buddha-field, just as the Great King made an immeasurable vow regarding the array of qualities of a buddha-field.

"Beings of immeasurable intention have been made ready and accepted as those to be converted by him. Therefore, Great King, when the Tathāgata Indraghoṣeśvararāja has passed into parinirvāṇa and his True Dharma has disappeared, after the passing of sixty intermediate kalpas, that world-system will be named Meruprabhā.
There, a Tathāgata named Acintyamatiguṇarāja will appear—an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha."

Just as was the array of the qualities of the Buddha-field in the world-system Indrasuvirājitā of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Indraghoṣeśvararāja, even so shall be the array of qualities in the world-system Meruprabhā of the Tathāgata Acintyamatiguṇarāja.
The lifespan of that Tathāgata Acintyamatiguṇarāja will be sixty intermediate kalpas.
When the Tathāgata Acintyamatiguṇarāja passes into parinirvāṇa, his True Dharma will remain for sixteen intermediate kalpas.
Once that True Dharma has disappeared, after the passing of a thousand intermediate kalpas, that world-system will be named Virati.
There, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Raśmi—
[the rest] as before— is equal to them in lifespan, and their world-system is equal.
When those who have thus attained parinirvāṇa have passed away and the true Dharma has disappeared, there will be another world-system called Aparā.
There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ratneśvaraghoṣa will appear.
His array of qualities of the Buddha-field will be equal [to that of others], he will remain for an equal number of intermediate kalpas, and he will sustain his life and teach the Dharma.
After he has passed into parinirvāṇa, his True Dharma will remain for seven intermediate kalpas;
and when that True Dharma has disappeared,
[the rest] is as described before.
In this way, I see immeasurable and infinite Tathāgatas born in that buddha-field and also entering parinirvāṇa;
yet that world-system neither undergoes destruction nor does it evolve.

There, in the future time, after one incalculable eon equal to the sands of the Ganges has passed and when the second incalculable eon equal to the sands of the river Ganges has begun, that world-system will be named Sukhāvatī.
"It shall come to pass,
O Great King, that you will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; you will become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Amitāyus."
King Araṇemi asked: "Venerable Blessed One, where are those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who will attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in that buddha-field before us?
The Blessed One said: "Great King, these are those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, from the ten directions by immeasurable, incalculable, incomparable, and infinite [beings]..."
They have come from those various world-systems in all directions to pay me homage, to attend upon me, and to hear the Dharma;

these sons of noble family who are seated before me have been prophesied for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by past Buddhas, and they have also been prophesied for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by the present Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
"O Great King, those who shall first attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in that buddha-field—

each one of these bodhisattvas, O Great King, has performed services in the presence of many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of Buddhas, has planted roots of merit, and has cultivated wisdom; these, O Great King, are the sons of noble family who will become the Buddhas there in that buddha-field first of all."

King Araṇemi said, "Venerable Blessed One, after how much time will this brahmin Samudrareṇu— who has inspired me along with my assembly toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment— attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment? The Blessed One replied, "This brahmin Samudrareṇu is one of great compassion."
“You shall hear how he will roar this lion’s roar.
The king said, “If this aspiration of mine is fulfilled, just as I have been prophesied by the Blessed One,”
“Just as I perform this prostration at the feet of the Blessed One with the five-fold salutation (*pañcamaṇḍala*), may world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā tremble and shake;
and may those Buddhas who abide, dwell, and maintain themselves in those Buddha-fields grant me a prophecy.
Then, noble son, King Araṇemin fell at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha with the five-fold salutation.
At the very moment the king’s head touched the earth, Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā shook, trembled, quaked, were agitated, and were thoroughly convulsed;
Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā made this prophecy:

"In the eon called Dhāraṇa, in the Buddha-field called Santīraṇa, when the lifespan of beings is eighty thousand years, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnagarbha will prophesy for King Araṇemin."

"In a future time, after an incalculable eon equal to the sands of the river Ganges has passed and the second incalculable eon has begun, you will become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Amitāyus in the world-system Sukhāvatī, which is infinitely pure;
you will illuminate world-systems equal to the sands of the river Ganges in all ten directions."
The Blessed One said:
"Arise, O supreme being, knower of the ritual; you have been prophesied by those who possess the ten powers."
Like the Ganges, you shall cause the earth, together with its mountains, to tremble; you will become a charioteer for those to be tamed, the best among men.”
Then, noble son, King Araṇemi— satisfied, elated, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness— approached and sat down to one side, not very far away, in order to hear the Dharma.
Then, noble son, the brahmin Samudrareṇu addressed the king Araṇemin’s eldest son, the prince named Animiṣa. Animiṣa replied:
[the rest as before].
“I have surveyed the states of woe and the beings born therein who experience fierce and terrible suffering.

I have surveyed the heavens and the beings born therein whose defiled minds cause them to fall once again into the states of woe. And I have surveyed all beings as they dwell in association with unwholesome friends.”
"In the darkness of a famine of Dharma, with their roots of merit completely exhausted, seized by the grasp of false views, they are afflicted by evil paths.
O Blessed One, with my voice I shall inform those beings."
And I dedicate all merit toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

While I practice the conduct of a bodhisattva, may whatever sentient beings are oppressed by suffering, threatened by fear, entered into the darkness of a famine of Dharma, despondent, wretched, without protection, without refuge, and without resort, proclaim my name.
If I were to hear with the divine ear and see with the divine eye,
yet did not liberate those beings from their misfortunes,
I would not awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

"Venerable Blessed One, when I, for the sake of sentient beings, shall practice the conduct of a bodhisattva for a long time through the excellence of my long-standing vows, may my aspiration then be fulfilled. Venerable Blessed One, when I, as the great king Araṇemin, after one incalculable eon equal to the sands of the river Gaṅgā has passed, shall be established in the second [eon], I will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Amitāyus in the world-system Sukhāvatī."
In a completely pure Buddha-field, he will perform the work of a Buddha for completely pure beings;

for as long as the Tathāgata Amitāyus performs the work of a Buddha for immeasurable eons, having completed that work of a Buddha, he will enter the realm of nirvana without remainder, and once he has entered it, his True Dharma will remain.
For that long I shall practice the conduct of a bodhisattva;
having become a bodhisattva, I shall perform the work of a Buddha.

When the true Dharma of the Tathāgata Amitāyus, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, disappears during the first watch of the night, on that very same night, during the final watch, may I realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
May the Blessed One grant me the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

In this very way, I address by means of my voice those Blessed Buddhas who reside, stay, and maintain themselves in world-systems throughout the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges; may those Blessed Buddhas also grant me the prediction.
"Those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, have prophesied [you] for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. "Noble son, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha has prophesied Prince Animiṣa, and he spoke thus:

'Noble son, since you have surveyed the lower realms, surveyed the heavens, and surveyed the suffering of all sentient beings, you have generated a mind of compassion for the sake of liberating sentient beings from suffering.'"
"Therefore, noble son, you shall be named Avalokiteśvara.
As Avalokiteśvara, you shall be the liberator from suffering for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings.
Noble son, while being a bodhisattva, you shall perform the work of a Buddha."
When the Tathāgata Amitābha has entered final nirvāṇa, during the second incalculable aeon equal in duration to the sands of the river Gaṅgā—

specifically on the very night when the True Dharma shall disappear in the first watch of that night— on that same night, in the last watch, you, noble son, seated upon the diamond throne at the foot of the Bodhi tree in the world-system Anekavyūha, shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"You shall become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Samantaraśmyabhyudgataśrīkūṭarāja.
Your lifespan shall be ninety-six hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of kalpas.
After you have entered parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain for sixty-three koṭis of kalpas."

Avalokiteśvara said: "If, Blessed One, this aspiration of mine is fulfilled, then when I prostrate at the feet of the Blessed One, may all those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who dwell, remain, and sustain themselves in world-systems in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, grant me their prophecy."
“May the earth tremble throughout the world-systems in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of all the Ganges rivers;
may the sound of five-fold musical instruments issue forth from all mountains, rocks, peaks, and trees;
and may all sentient beings attain a mind free from passion.”

And when the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had paid homage to the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha with the five-fold prostration, the earth trembled in as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā; and those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, bestowed prophecies upon him— as described at length previously.
From the peaks of all the mountain rocks, the sound of five-fold musical instruments issued forth,
and all sentient beings remained with minds free from passion.
The Blessed One said:
“Arise, O you whose mind is joyful through compassion and merit! You have been prophesied as one who shall bear a sublime body throughout the ten directions.
The earth and its realms have trembled in six ways; you shall become a Great Sage, the foremost person among the Victors.”
Then the brahmin Samudrareṇu, the chief priest, addressed the second prince named Nimi:
"Noble son, rejoice in this great renunciation;
and whatever merit you have acquired, dedicate it all toward omniscience for the sake of all sentient beings."
“Generate the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Then Prince Nimi, having sat down before the Blessed One, said this: “Whatever service I have rendered to the Blessed One with all necessary provisions, together with an immeasurable community of monks, and whatever joy has arisen from that [merit]—”
This is a mass of merit: whatever merit consists of the good conduct of body, speech, and mind, I dedicate toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
May I not touch awakening in this defiled buddha-field alone;

There, the youth Avalokiteśvara, seated beneath a bodhi tree adorned with many jewels in the world-system Sarvaratnasannicayā, shall attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment and become the Tathāgata named Samantaraśmyabhyudgataśrīkūṭarāja.
I would entreat him to teach the Dharma; and for as long as that Tathāgata teaches the Dharma, for that long I would practice the conduct of a bodhisattva.
When that Tathāgata has passed away and his true Dharma has disappeared, immediately thereafter I would attain perfect awakening.
May my buddha-field be such in its array of qualities.

In this very way may I perform the work of a Buddha; in this very way may I lead [beings] to final nirvana; and in this very way, once I have entered final nirvana, may the True Dharma endure for a long time.
“The entire array of qualities shall be exactly like that of the Tathāgata Samantaraśmyabhyudgataśrīkūṭarāja.
The Blessed One said, “O Mahāsthāmaprāpta, noble son, you have made this aspiration;
noble son, you shall attain such a state as you yourself have taken hold of.”
“Son of good family, you shall attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in that buddha-field;
you will become a Tathāgata named Supratiṣṭhitaguṇamaṇikūṭarāja, with power such as yours.”
“Noble son, you have grasped the great station; therefore, noble son, become one who has attained great power.
He said, “If, Blessed One, this aspiration of mine is fulfilled, [then let it be so].”

"Therefore, when I bow at the feet of the Blessed One with my body in the five-pointed prostration, may the Buddha-Blessed Ones in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, grant me their prophecy, and may a rain of *sumanā* flowers fall. When, noble son, the true person Mahāsthāmaprāpta performed this prostration at the feet of Ratnagarbha with the five-pointed salutation, [the prophecy was given].
Then, that was prophesied by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the ten directions— each as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—
and the great earth shook in six ways,
and a rain of *sumana* flowers fell.
The Blessed One said:
"Arise, O Dṛḍhasthāmavegapuṇya! You have been prophesied by the Lords of the World in the ten directions.
The great earth has trembled and a rain of *sumanā* flowers has fallen; you shall become one who is like a Brahmā among gods and men."
(KpSū 124) Then the brahmin Samudrareṇu addressed the third prince, named Indragaṇa;
the details are as before.
Having joined his palms in reverence, Ratnagarbha addressed the Tathāgata as follows: "Whatever service I have rendered to the Blessed One and the community of monks with all necessary provisions,
whatever good conduct of body, speech, and mind I have performed, and this mass of merit accompanied by rejoicing— [all these I dedicate]."
I dedicate all this toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; may I not awaken to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in a defiled buddha-field,
nor may I attain it too quickly.

And as long as I have not fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, while practicing the conduct of awakening, may I behold the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in other world-systems throughout the infinite and boundless ten directions—
those whom I first inspired toward awakening, those for whom I first generated the thought of awakening, and those whom I established in the thought of awakening.
And those whom I have encouraged, introduced to, and established in the perfections while practicing the conduct of awakening—

may I, with my divine eye, behold those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, as they teach the Dharma in Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, in Buddha-fields as numerous as atoms of dust, all those whom I have encouraged toward awakening.
Thus, while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, may I perform the work of a Buddha;

may I practice the conduct of a bodhisattva for as long as it takes to purify the intentions of sentient beings, so that whatever beings are born in my buddha-field shall be of such a nature as the gods of the Brahma-realm.
And furthermore, may I purify the array of qualities of the Buddha-field such that this single Buddha-field would be as vast as a great trichiliocosm equal in extent to the sands of the river Ganges;
and may the walls of that Buddha-field reach as far as the peak of existence (*bhavāgra*), composed of many jewels and inlaid with various gems;
and may the entire ground of that Buddha-field consist of pure lapis lazuli.
The earth would be free from dust, stones, and pebbles, and devoid of any contact with impurities; therein,
even the designation of the name "woman" would not exist,
and all beings would be of miraculous birth (*upapāduka*), and no beings there would subsist on solid food.
And all beings there would have joy as their sustenance and the Dharma as their sustenance.
In that buddha-field, there would be no designation for śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas;
rather, that buddha-field would be completely pure, consisting of pure bodhisattvas who are free from stubbornness, stains, hatred, and hypocrisy, and who lead a pure holy life.
All the bodhisattvas there would appear with shaven heads and wearing saffron robes; as soon as they appeared, a great radiance would arise,
and in their right hands, bowls made of jewels filled with various kinds of food would appear.
"Immediately upon their appearance, may they obtain such a recollection as this: 'It is not fitting for us to consume solid food;

what if we were to go to other world-systems and honor the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are currently dwelling and maintaining themselves there with this food, and likewise honor the disciples of the Buddha and suffering people?
And having gone to the realms of the hungry ghosts, may we honor those beings whose bodies are ablaze with hunger and thirst with this food.'"
Simultaneously with the arising of that thought, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas would attain the samādhi called "Possessing Inconceivable Conduct.

By the attainment of that samādhi, they would go to immeasurable other buddha-fields in the ten directions to honor the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, as they dwell and maintain their lives, by providing them with food, as well as their śrāvakas and other sentient beings.
Having honored them with joy and delivered a teaching of the Dharma, they would return to their own Buddha-field by means of that very same morning meal.
Likewise, regarding robes and jewels,
up until returning to their own Buddha-field by means of that very same morning meal, they would clothe one another with robes.

Whatever enjoyments and possessions those bodhisattvas in that buddha-field may have, they shall first share them all in common with all the Buddhas, the śrāvakas, and other beings, and only afterwards enjoy them themselves;
and that buddha-field shall be free from the eight inopportune states.
And there would be no word for suffering,
nor any word for undertaking the training,
nor even any word for the emergence from an offense.
That buddha-field would be accumulated with hundreds of thousands of various jewels;
it would be inlaid with many gems and resemble the *maṇisandarśana*.
Those jewel-gems which had never been seen before in the ten directions and had never been heard of before would circulate there.
Even if tens of millions of years were spent enumerating the names of those jewel-gems, they would not be exhausted.
Furthermore, if a bodhisattva should desire to see the buddha-field as consisting solely of gold, it would remain for him as consisting solely of gold;
if one should desire it to consist of silver, he would see it as consisting of silver.
And this golden nature of it would not diminish—
*peyāla*, as before.
Whoever should desire to see that buddha-field as consisting of crystal, of beryl, of emerald, of ruby, of pearl, or of musāragalva, such a buddha-field they would behold.
They might desire this:

whatever Bodhisattva should desire to see that buddha-field as consisting of agalloch, tagara, or tamāla leaves, or as consisting of uragasāra sandalwood or goṣīrṣa sandalwood, for him it would be exactly so.
In whatever way and in whatever manner they may desire it, it shall become exactly so;
yet one person's vow shall not obstruct another's,
for the vow of every single one is fulfilled.
Furthermore, in that buddha-field, the sun and moon would not be perceived,
and the bodhisattvas born there would be self-luminous.
Whatever kind of radiance they might desire, they could emit such,
even throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddha-fields;
and in that Buddha-field, even the name "night and day" is not known.
Except for the blooming of flowers,
neither cold nor heat is known in that buddha-field, nor is there illness, nor infirmity, nor old age and death; however,
any bodhisattva who desires to fully awaken to enlightenment must dwell in another world-system and exhaust his lifespan there.
He would fully awaken to enlightenment;
in that buddha-field there would be no death,
and the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata would occur in the sky above through supreme parinirvāṇa.
Whatever kind of enjoyments and possessions the bodhisattvas might desire, those very kinds would be manifested.
And in every buddha-field, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of musical instruments would play in the expanse of the sky;
yet from those instruments, no sounds associated with sensual desires would issue forth.
Otherwise, the sounds of the *pāramitās* would issue forth;
the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," the sound of "Saṅgha," and the sound of the Dharma-discourses of the Bodhisattva-piṭaka would issue forth.
Bodhisattvas, according to their respective inclinations, would hear such kinds of sounds.

“Blessed One, while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, I have seen the arrays of qualities of buddha-fields, those arrays, those ornaments, those marks, those signs, those locations, and those vows within immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddhas; may all of these enter my own buddha-field.”
Setting aside the arrays of the disciples and solitary buddhas, as well as the arrays of qualities of a buddha-field during the five degenerations,

there would be no perception of hells, animals, or hungry ghosts in that buddha-field; nor would Mount Sumeru, the Cakravāḍa or Mahācakravāḍa mountains, mountains of rock or dust, or great oceans be perceived.
Nor would there be other ordinary wooden trees; rather, that buddha-field would be filled with various divine trees that transcend the mundane.
Except for divine flowers—*māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava*—there would be no foul odor there; instead, that buddha-field would be suffused with various most sublime fragrances.
Furthermore, all the bodhisattvas born there would be bound to only one more birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*).

"Venerable Blessed One, may there not be even a single sentient being therein who, having passed away from that place, would be reborn elsewhere—except for those in Tuṣita; and having passed away from Tuṣita, they would attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Venerable Blessed One, I shall practice the conduct of a bodhisattva until I have accomplished such a great feat of a superior person."
"I shall establish a buddha-field of such a form;
together with beings of such pure intentions and bodhisattvas bound to only one more birth, I shall establish that buddha-field as being filled [with them]."
There shall be no bodhisattva there who was not first inspired by me toward awakening;
all those bodhisattvas whom I first inspired toward awakening and established in the perfections shall be reborn there.
I shall cause this very buddha-field to be included within that [world-system], and I shall pacify all these sufferings.
"O Venerable Blessed One, while I am a bodhisattva, may I accomplish such human effort that thereafter I might awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in that buddha-field;
and may my bodhi-tree have a circumference equal to ten thousand sets of four continents."

It shall be named Saptaratnavicitrasandarśana (Display of the Various Seven Jewels), measuring ten trichiliocosms in circumference; and by the fragrance and radiance of that Bodhi tree, the entire Buddha-field shall be pervaded.
At its base, may there be for me a vajra-throne, variegated with various jewels and measuring five times the size of a four-continent world-system;
let it be named "The Convergence of the Fragrance of Peaceful, Patient, and Exquisitely Varied Wisdom," and eighty-four yojanas in height;
upon that vajra-throne at the foot of that Bodhi-tree, may I sit.

Having assumed the cross-legged posture, may I realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening in that very moment; until the time of my final nirvāṇa, may I not break that cross-legged posture, nor release it, nor rise from the foot of that Bodhi tree.
Remaining right there at the foot of the Bodhi tree, seated upon the diamond throne, may I dispatch emanated Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to other incalculable Buddha-fields.
If each individual Buddha were to teach the Dharma to sentient beings during a single morning meal,
and by means of that very same morning meal were to cause immeasurable sentient beings to undertake, establish, and become irreversible in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
then emanated bodhisattvas would perform such bodhisattva activities.
When I have attained awakening, may my body be visible in worlds throughout the ten directions beyond all calculation;

and for those beings whose eyes perceive my body adorned with the primary marks, may they all become destined for unexcelled, perfect awakening, and until their final nirvana at awakening, may those beings never be separated from the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

Therein, no one shall be deficient in their faculties. And whichever Bodhisattvas there may be who wish to see me, wherever they go, turn, walk to and fro, sit, or stand, all those Bodhisattvas, by the mere arising of a thought of homage to the Buddha, shall behold me seated at the foot of the Bodhi tree. Having seen me, whatever doubt regarding the Dharma they may have shall vanish at that very sight; their anxieties shall be dispelled, and they shall understand the meaning of the Dharma-words even without them being taught.
May my lifespan be immeasurable, such that it cannot be calculated by anyone except through omniscient knowledge;
and may there be immeasurable bodhisattvas therein.

"And at the very moment that I should awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in that buddha-field, at that moment, may the bodhisattvas in that buddha-field have shaven heads and wear saffron robes,

and until my final nirvana, may not even a single being in this buddha-field have long hair or wear white garments; rather, may they all possess the appearance of ascetics and abide in the likeness of ascetics."
The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, O noble man!
You too are learned, discerning, and wise; you have made a most beautiful vow; you are exceedingly virtuous and possessed of great knowledge."
Since you, noble son, for the sake of all sentient beings, have formed such a supreme and praiseworthy intention and have embraced this magnificent array of qualities of a Buddha-field,
therefore, noble son, let your name be Mañjuśrī.
Mañjuśrī, in a future time, after two incalculable eons as numerous as the sands of the Ganges have passed, you shall become...
And when the third incalculable eon has entered, there will be a world-system in the southern direction named Śuddhavirajasannicaya;
therein the Sahā world-system will be contained, and having entered it, that buddha-field will manifest with such an array of qualities.
There, Mañjuśrī, you shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening;
you will become a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha named Samantadarśin.
Your assembly of bodhisattvas will be of such a nature, and all these vows of yours shall be fulfilled exactly as you have made them.
Then, having become a bodhisattva, you will have planted roots of merit under many millions of buddhas; you will be one who purifies intentions and crushes the afflictions.
And, Mañjuśrī, those beings who hear your name will experience the destruction of all karmic obstructions.
"And you shall be one who increases the wholesome.

Mañjuśrī said, "If, O Blessed One, such a fulfillment of my aspiration should come to pass, just as the vow I have made, then may the Buddha-Blessed Ones in the ten directions— in immeasurable and incalculable [worlds]— grant me their prophecy accordingly."
They abide, remain, and maintain themselves in the world-systems, and they teach the Dharma to sentient beings.
Likewise, may immeasurable and incalculable Buddha-fields tremble,
and may all sentient beings be endowed with such happiness.
It is, for example, like that of a Bodhisattva who has entered the meditative absorption of the "Array of Play" of the second dhyāna.

Likewise, may divine māndārava flowers rain down from immeasurable and incalculable Buddha-fields, and from those very māndārava flowers may such sounds issue forth as these: the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," and the sound of "Saṅgha."
“May the sound of the word ‘perfection’ (pāramitā) and the sound of the words ‘powers’ (bala) and ‘fearlessnesses’ (vaiśāradya) issue forth;
and when I bow at the feet of the Blessed One with the five-fold prostration (pañcamaṇḍala), may such a sign appear.
And when Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta had performed his prostration at the feet of the Blessed One, at that very moment immeasurable and incalculable Buddha-fields trembled.
Divine *māndārava* flowers rained down,
and all sentient beings were endowed with such happiness as they had previously vowed.
And those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who heard the Dharma from those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, questioned those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
“What is the cause, what is the condition for the manifestation of such signs as these?
And those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, prophesy Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta’s attainment of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
The Blessed One said:
“Arise, O one of supreme intelligence and vast wisdom! You have been prophesied by the Lords of the World in the ten directions.
The earth has trembled, sentient beings have been gratified with happiness, and flowers have rained down; you shall become a Buddha in the world. Thus it was said.
(KpSū 135) Then, noble son, the brahmin Samudrareṇu addressed the fourth prince, named Ānaṅgaṇa;
[the rest is] as in the elaboration regarding the vow made by Mañjuśrī.
The Blessed One gave him his approval, saying: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!
As a bodhisattva, noble son, you shall shatter the mountains of afflictions of immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings."
And you shall perform the work of a Buddha;
thereafter, you will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Therefore, noble son, become a bodhisattva named Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsaśrī.

In a future time, after one incalculable eon as numerous as the sands of a single Ganges River has passed and when a second incalculable eon as numerous as the sands of a Ganges River has begun, you will become the Buddha Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsa. In the eastern direction,
beyond as many world systems as there are atoms in ten times the sands of a Ganges River of Buddha-fields, there will be a world system named Animiṣā.
"There, noble son, you shall attain perfect awakening; you will become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Buddha, a Blessed One named Samantabhadra.
And your buddha-field shall be adorned with many such qualities, just as you have made your vow."
(KpSū 136) And as soon as the Bodhisattva Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsa had been prophesied for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, O son of good family,

many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of deities dwelling in the expanse of the sky uttered cries of "Excellent! and rained down powders of gośīrṣa, uragasāra, candana, agaru, and tamāla.

He said, "Venerable Blessed One, if such a wish of mine may be fulfilled, then whenever I pay homage to the Blessed One with the five-fold prostration, may world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā be filled with a sublime and divine fragrance that transcends the human."
"And whatever beings might be born in those world-systems—whether they be denizens of hell, animals, inhabitants of the world of Yama, gods, or humans—all of them shall smell that fragrance;
and for all of them, physical illness and physical suffering, as well as mental illness and mental suffering, shall remain pacified for as long as I keep my head touching the earth.
Then, noble son, the Bodhisattva Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsa prostrated with his five limbs at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.
Then, at that very moment, world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā became suffused with a sublime fragrance surpassing that of the divine;
and for all sentient beings, physical illness and mental illness, as well as physical suffering and mental suffering, were pacified and calmed.
The Blessed One said:
"Arise, O breaker of the vajra! Many realms are suffused with your fragrance;
you shall become a father to the excellent world, bringing happiness and joy to sentient beings."
Then, noble son, the brahmin Samudrareṇu addressed the fifth prince, named Abhaya.

[The same as before: “And not only in this defiled buddha-field, O Venerable Blessed One, would I awaken to enlightenment, but in a place where there would be no hells, no animal births, and no worlds of Yama.”

In that place, the ground consists of blue *vaiḍūrya* stone; its array of qualities (*guṇavyūha*) should be described in detail just as it is in the lotus world-system (*padmā lokadhātu*), the Buddha-field.
Then Prince Abhaya, having placed a lotus before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, said:
"Venerable Blessed One, if such a wish of mine should be fulfilled, then by the power of the Blessed One, may I attain the *samādhi* called 'Array of Vision'."

"By means of this, may a rain of flowers fall before the Blessed One from lotuses the size of chariot wheels— numbering as many as the atoms in a buddha-field, filling world-systems in the ten directions equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges— and may we behold it. As soon as these words were uttered, through the power of the Buddha, he attained the samādhi called *Darśanavyūha* (The Array of Vision).
In world-systems in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, a rain of lotuses fell, equal in number to the atoms of a buddha-field and the size of chariot wheels;
seeing this, Prince Abhaya was filled with supreme joy and gladness.
The Blessed One said, "Excellent indeed, noble son, is the vow you have made."
"A beautiful buddha-field has been taken hold of by you, this samādhi has been attained by you very swiftly,
and by your word of truth, a rain of lotuses has been made to fall."
He said, "If my aspiration for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment is to be fulfilled, then let these lotuses remain in the sky, and remaining thus in the sky, let them rain down.
The Blessed One said, "The surface of the sky has been sealed with lotuses, son of good family;
therefore, son of good family, you shall be known by the name Gaganamudra (Seal of the Sky)."
In a future time, after one incalculable eon equal to the sands of a single Ganges River has passed and the second has begun, you will become the Buddha Gaganamudra.
In the southeastern direction, after traversing as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of millions of Ganges Rivers, there will be a world-system named Padmā.

There you shall attain awakening; you shall become the Tathāgata named Padmottara, an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, and so forth, up to a Buddha, a Blessed One, together with an immeasurable and pure assembly of Bodhisattvas,
and your lifespan shall be incalculable.
“You shall obtain this very vow, endowed with all these qualities.
The Bodhisattva Gaganamudra prostrated his head at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha,
and the Blessed One said:
“You shall become a benefactor in the world, a pacifier of the turbidity of afflictions;
possessing virtues equal to the atoms of a buddha-field, you will attain awakening just as the previous Victors did.”
Then, noble son, the brahmin Samudrareṇu addressed the sixth prince, named Ambara.
[The text continues as follows: "And it is not only in this defiled buddha-field," up to the point where the bodhisattva Gaganamudra made his vow.

“Blessed One, if such a wish of mine should be fulfilled, then may parasols made of the seven precious gems appear in the skies throughout all the world-systems in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—covered with nets of gold and adorned with bells made of the seven precious gems.

From those very parasols, bells, and nets, may this kind of sound issue forth: namely, the sound of the Buddha, the sound of the Dharma, the sound of the Saṅgha, the sound of the perfections, the sound of the powers, the sound of the superknowledges, and the sound of the fearlessnesses.”
And may all those beings hear such a sound; having heard it, may they all resolve their minds upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
And those beings here who have previously resolved their minds upon enlightenment, may they become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
As soon as these words were spoken, then from the entire expanse of space in world-systems throughout the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, sounds of this kind resounded.

Through the power of the Blessed One, he saw it for himself and spoke again as follows: "Venerable Blessed One, if such a hope of mine may be fulfilled according to the vow I have made, then, in the presence of the Blessed One, I shall enter the *jñānavairocana* (Wisdom-Illumination) samādhi, by which my wholesome qualities may be brought forth."
"And once I have attained this samādhi, may the Blessed One grant me a prophecy.
Through the power of the Blessed One, the Jñānavairocana-samādhi was attained.
The Blessed One said, "Excellent, excellent, O noble person!"
A sublime vow has been made by you;
by that outflow of merit, many Buddha-fields in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, shall all become equal in measure.
The Buddha-field is stirred by a hundred thousand pleasing sounds;
therefore, noble son, go forth with the name Vegavairocana!
In a future time, after an incalculable eon equal to the sands of a single Ganges River has passed, you will become [a Buddha].
"When the second [eon] has entered, after passing through world-systems in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges,
there is a world-system named Ādityasoma; there you shall attain perfect awakening,
and you shall become a Tathāgata named Dharmavaśavartīśvararāja— an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, and so forth, up to a Buddha, a Blessed One."
Then that Bodhisattva Vegavairocana paid homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, with the five-fold prostration and said:
"Arise, O you of excellent vows, gentle one whose mind is subdued! Great and intense compassion for sentient beings has arisen within you."
"O Tārā, establish sentient beings on the shore of the ocean of suffering until you awaken to unsurpassed, perfect buddha-enlightenment."
(KpSū 142) Then, noble son, the brahmin Samudrareṇu addressed the seventh prince, Aṅgaja:
[and so on]... "I would not attain awakening in this defiled buddha-field."

And where neither hells, nor the animal realm, nor the world of Yama are known; where there is no female sex, nor the dwelling of beings in a womb; where there is no Sumeru, no Cakravāḍa or Mahācakravāḍa mountains, no earth, stone, mountain, or rocky peaks, no saline soil, gravel, potsherds, thorns, or thickets, no wooden trees, and no great oceans.

And there, neither sun nor moon exists, nor the forms of stars, nor night and day, nor masses of darkness; nor do there exist for sentient beings excrement, urine, spittle, or nasal mucus, nor the foul odor of bodily fatigue; nor shall there be for sentient beings exhaustion of body or exhaustion of mind.
And there shall be no ground of dust;
the entire ground there shall consist of emerald, adorned with many hundreds of thousands of jewels,
and that buddha-field shall be strewn with māndārava and mahāmāndārava flowers and adorned with various jewel-trees.

And those jewel-trees would be adorned with various nets of jewels; they would be adorned with various jeweled cloths, various jeweled garments, various jeweled garlands, and various ornaments of jeweled decorations; and those jewel-trees would be further adorned with various wreaths, various musical instruments, various jeweled vessels, and various flowers.
They would exist; night would not be perceived there, except when the flowers close and musical instruments are played.
And from those closing flowers, bodhisattvas would be reborn.

And while absorbed therein, the bodhisattvas would attain the samādhi called "Array of Vision," by means of which samādhi, once attained, they would see the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, abiding and maintaining their lives in other world-systems throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field; and at that very moment, they would likewise attain such a pure divine ear.
By means of which they might hear the Dharma teachings of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in other world-systems in the ten directions—in Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field;
and may all those beings, upon being born, possess the recollection of their past lives and remember kalpas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field;
and may all those beings, upon being born, likewise attain such a divine eye.
May they behold, all around in the ten directions, the magnificent arrays of qualities of Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within those Buddha-fields.

And may all those beings, upon their birth, be endowed with such skill in knowing the minds of others that, in a single moment, they discern the mental activities of all sentient beings in Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within those Buddha-fields, continuing until their awakening and final nirvana.
Those beings would be directed toward that samādhi;
and at the time of dawn, fragrant, delightful, and soft breezes with pleasant touch would blow from the four directions,
which would cause those flowers to bloom.
And those bodhisattvas, having emerged from those eight samādhis, would rise up from those flower filaments;
they would attain such a range of supernatural power (*ṛddhiviṣaya*) that in a single moment of thought they would go in each direction as many times as there are atoms in a buddha-field,
and having paid homage to and attended upon the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, as they remain and maintain their lives, they would then return.
And there, having formed a cross-legged posture upon the filaments of the *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava* flowers, they should sit;

with their minds focused on the bliss of the Dharma, they should gaze upon the Tathāgata. In whichever direction they sit or turn, they should see me alone in every quarter. And whatever kind of doubt, perplexity, or uncertainty regarding the teachings may arise for those bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas there, all of that shall vanish by the mere sight and observation of me.
And whatever kind of Dharma teaching those bodhisattva mahāsattvas might desire, they would understand such a Dharma teaching by my mere glance; furthermore,
the beings there would be without "mine-ness" and without possessiveness.
They would be indifferent even to their own bodies and lives;
and all the bodhisattvas there would be irreversible.
There, even the name of the unwholesome would not exist.
And in that buddha-field, there would not even be the name of "undertaking training," nor any talk of rising from an offense,
so that all sentient beings would be endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man.
And may all beings possess the strength of Nārāyaṇa; and may not even a single being there have impaired faculties until their awakening and final nirvāṇa;
and may all beings there be born with shaven heads, clothed in new saffron robes.
May they attain well-distinguished meditative concentration and continue it until the very limit of enlightenment;
and may they all therein possess roots of merit that are perfectly harmonized.
Furthermore, in that buddha-field, the suffering of old age and illness would not be known among sentient beings.
Those sentient beings whose lifespan comes to an end would all pass away while sitting cross-legged,
and from their own bodies they would emit the fire element by which they would consume their own bodies.
And winds might come from the four directions that would carry those relics of the Bodhisattvas to empty Buddha-fields.
And such great precious jewels might appear— just like the radiant jewel-gem of a universal monarch (cakravartin)—

such that whatever beings there were who saw the radiance of that jewel-gem, or saw that jewel-gem, or touched it, they would all [be freed] from the sufferings of the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama, until their awakening and parinirvāṇa.
May they not experience [suffering];
and having passed away from there, may they be reborn in those places where the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, remain and dwell, teaching the Dharma to sentient beings.
And those beings born there shall hear the Dharma from the presence of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and they shall generate the mind of awakening (bodhicitta);
and as soon as the mind of awakening has been generated, they shall become irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
Not a single being in my Buddha-field shall pass away while not in a state of meditative concentration (asamāhita).
May they not experience painful sensations, nor die with minds distracted by mutual hostility; and may they not, because of that, be reborn in the realms of Māra or the inopportune states (*akṣaṇa*).
Until the limit of enlightenment, may they never be separated from the sight of the Buddhas, and may they never be separated from hearing the Dharma or serving the Saṅgha.
And may all sentient beings therein be free from stubbornness, hatred, hypocrisy, envy, and avarice.

And that buddha-field would be devoid of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; it would be filled with pure bodhisattvas. Furthermore, the beings who are born there would possess hearts that are gentle, soft, free from enmity, free from defilement, peaceful, and composed.
May that buddha-field of mine be luminous,
and may that buddha-field of mine be arrayed with great qualities;
may it be visible in the ten directions through as many world-systems as there are atoms in a buddha-field, and may it pervade them with its fragrance.
And may the beings there be endowed with eternal happiness;
nor shall even the sound of suffering be heard in that buddha-field.

I shall practice the conduct of a bodhisattva for as long as it takes until, while still a bodhisattva, I have purified a buddha-field with such perfections of the array of qualities of a buddha-field.
I shall establish that buddha-field filled with beings whose intentions are purified in such a manner;
thereafter, I would manifest full awakening to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in that buddha-field.
And once I have attained awakening, my radiance would be immeasurable.
"May my body, adorned with the primary marks, be visible in other buddhafields throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within a thousand buddhafields.
And may the passion of those beings who see me there be pacified;
may their hatred, delusion, envy, pride, hypocrisy, and all afflictions and secondary afflictions be pacified."
May all generate the mind of awakening (bodhicitta); and whatever kinds of meditative absorptions (samādhi) and dhāraṇīs they might desire, may they obtain them upon seeing me.
Furthermore, for those beings who have been reborn there in the cold hells, may a sensation of bliss arise for them upon seeing me.

And may they obtain such pleasant sensations as those of a monk who has entered the second dhyāna; and upon seeing me, may they all become endowed with the highest physical and mental happiness, [dedicating it] toward unexcelled [enlightenment].

May they generate the mind set on unexcelled perfect enlightenment, and having passed away from there, may they be reborn in my buddha-field, and there may they become irreversible from unexcelled perfect enlightenment.
And may those beings who have been reborn in the realms of hungry ghosts behold me.
...and so on, until they become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; in this way, those who have been born as animals should be addressed.
Likewise, O gods, may my radiance shine twice as bright.
May my lifespan be immeasurable,
such that it cannot be calculated by anyone except through the wisdom of the Omniscient One.

And when I have attained awakening, may the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the other immeasurable and infinite world-systems throughout the ten directions, proclaim my praise and cause it to be heard by others.
And those beings there who should hear my praise, let them dedicate their roots of merit toward that buddha-field of mine;

having passed away, they shall be reborn in my buddha-field, with the exception of those who have committed the acts of immediate retribution, those who reject the true Dharma, and those who revile the noble ones.
Furthermore, when I have attained awakening, those beings in immeasurable and incalculable world-systems who should hear my name and desire rebirth in my buddha-field—

At the time of their death, surrounded by many assemblies, having entered the *vitimira* concentration, may I satisfy those beings with such well-spoken words that all the suffering of those beings shall be pacified,
and through that very clarity, they may attain the definitive concentration.
May they attain the dharma-patience that delights the mind,
and having passed away, may they be reborn in my buddha-field;
and furthermore, may those beings in other buddha-fields who are destitute of the seven riches and have no interest in the three vehicles [likewise attain this].

May I stand before those who are indifferent to divine and human prosperities, who seek only the wholesome, who are stained by unrighteous passion for the three bases of meritorious action, who are overcome by improper greed, and who are enveloped by false teachings— at the time of their death, surrounded by a great multitude, may I teach them the Dharma through the *prabhāsa-samādhi*.
I would show them my own buddha-field and inspire them toward awakening;
those beings would attain supreme joy, serene faith, and gladness in my presence, and they would generate the resolve for awakening.
May all their painful sensations be pacified,
may they attain the *sūryapradīpa* concentration,
and may they be freed from the obstruction of delusion.
"And having passed away, may they be reborn in my buddha-field.
The Blessed One said, "Excellent, excellent, O noble man!
You have made a purifying vow."

He said: "Venerable Blessed One, if such a wish of mine may be fulfilled, then let a rain of uragasāra sandalwood powder fall in other buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within those buddha-fields;
and whatever sentient beings should smell that fragrance, may they all generate the mind set on awakening."
And now I have attained the samādhi named Praṇītadyuti, by which I may see it for myself.

And once that sublime radiance samādhi had been produced, noble son, he himself beheld in the other world-systems in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms of that buddha-field, the powder of uragasāra sandalwood; and in each of the ten directions, he saw beings beyond counting with palms joined together, who were generating the resolve for awakening.

The Blessed One said, “Noble son, a rain of fragrance has fallen with extreme swiftness, and beings beyond counting have been inspired toward enlightenment; therefore, noble son, you shall be named Siṃhagandha (Lion-Fragrance). Noble son Siṃhagandha, when one incalculable aeon, equal to the sands of a single Gaṅgā River, had passed and the second had begun, from this world in the upward direction...”

After passing through as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in forty-two Buddha-fields equal to the number of sands in the river Ganges, there will be a world-system named Nīlagandhaprabhāsaviraja;
there you, Siṃhagandhā, shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
“You shall become a Tathāgata named Prabhāsaviraja-samucchrayagandheśvararāja, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, and so forth, up to a Buddha, a Blessed One.
Then, noble son, the Bodhisattva Siṃhagandha prostrated at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha with the fivefold limb-bowing.
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said to him:
"Arise, O you who are worshipped by asuras, humans, and gods! Deliver the world of sentient beings who are suffering, O Blessed One!
Having severed the bonds of the afflictions and the suffering of existence, you shall become a Victor among men, a noble person."
Then, noble son, the brahmin Samudrareṇu addressed the eighth prince, named Amīgha:

[peyālam] “O Blessed One, I shall practice the conduct of a bodhisattva as a bodhisattva in a defiled buddha-field for as long as it takes me to establish ten thousand such defiled buddha-fields as completely pure.”

Just as the Buddha-field Nīlagandhaprabhāsaviraja is, so shall it become. With such bodhisattvas— who have planted roots of merit, possess purified intentions, and have set out upon the Mahāyāna— I shall cause that Buddha-field to be filled.
"Afterwards, I shall realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Venerable Blessed One, I shall practice the conduct of a bodhisattva in such a way that other bodhisattvas do not practice it.

Venerable Blessed One, during these seven years, while staying alone in seclusion, I have been reflecting upon the purity of the qualities of a Buddha, the purity of the qualities of a bodhisattva, and the purity of the qualities of a buddha-field."
Preceded by the *darśanavyūha* samādhi, eleven thousand bodhisattva samādhis— which have been produced, attained, and cultivated by me here—
constitute, O Venerable Blessed One, my conduct as a bodhisattva while I was a bodhisattva.

Furthermore, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside and maintain themselves in other infinite and boundless world-systems in the ten directions for the benefit and happiness of sentient beings, and who teach the Dharma—
May I behold those Buddha-fields, such as Dhvajāgrakeyūra, which have transcended the three times, and may I turn [the wheel of Dharma] there, filled with Jinas.
By means of that samādhi, O Venerable Blessed One, may I behold Buddhas, Blessed Ones, equal in number to atoms, surrounded by hosts of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas.
By the power of the *aniśritāsamādhi*, may I pay homage to each one with bodies as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field.

With each single body, I would worship each [Buddha] with unsurpassed, diverse jewels, flowers, unsurpassed, diverse perfumes, garlands, powders, ointments, and musical instruments, and with all unsurpassed arrays. And in a single field, I would practice for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the ocean.
And when, through the concentration of the dissolution of the entire body, I may in a single instant comprehend the spheres of activity of each Buddha, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field;
and when, O Venerable Blessed One, through the concentration that is a mine of qualities, I may praise each [Buddha] with supreme praises as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field;
and when, O Venerable Blessed One, through the unwinking concentration, I may see all Buddha-fields filled with Victors, in a measure equal to the number of waking thoughts in a single moment.

"Furthermore, O Venerable Blessed One, by means of the concentration of non-affliction (*araṇā-samādhi*), may I, in a single moment of thought, behold the bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present in all Buddha-fields, as well as the magnificent arrays of qualities of those Buddha-fields.
And furthermore, O Venerable Blessed One, by means of the Śūraṅgama concentration, may I enter into the hells, manifest a hellish body, and teach the Dharma to the beings dwelling in the hells."
And I would encourage them toward awakening; then, having generated the mind set on awakening, those beings,
after passing away from there, would be reborn in the company of human beings.
Wherever the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, reside, may they hear the Dharma from those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones,
and may I establish them on the stage of non-retrogression;
likewise for those among the animals.
Thus it is with the pretas, thus it is with the yakṣas,
and thus it is with the rākṣasas.
Thus among the asuras, thus among the nāgas, and thus among the kinnaras and mahoragas.
Likewise among the piśācas, pūtanās, and kaṭapūtanas; likewise among human outcasts (caṇḍālas);
likewise among merchants and courtesans.
And, Blessed One, in whatever kind of families sentient beings are born,
in whatever manner they obtain their physical bodies,
and in whatever way sentient beings experience pleasant or painful sensations through the condition of karma—
And in whatever kinds of crafts or occupations they are engaged, having manifested a physical form of that same kind, I would demonstrate diligence in those very same crafts and occupations,
and I would satisfy the minds of sentient beings through such visual communication.
And I would teach the Dharma, and I would exhort, establish, and settle them in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and I would establish them as irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

"O Venerable Blessed One, I shall practice the conduct of a bodhisattva for as long as it takes to purify the mental continuums of all sentient beings in ten thousand buddha-fields in such a way that they do not produce prior karmic afflictions,
even in the case of a single sentient being."
May the four Māras not know the path of my mental continuum;

may I establish ten thousand Buddha-fields as pure in this manner, so that the magnificent array of qualities of those Buddha-fields may be exactly like those of the Nīlagandhaprabhāsaviraja Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Prabhāsavirajasamucchrayagandheśvararājajyotis.
Thus, I [shall fulfill] my own buddha-field and my own assembly, just as the bodhisattva Siṃhagandha has made his vow:
"Venerable Blessed One, if such a hope of mine should be fulfilled, then likewise may all the sufferings of sentient beings in ten thousand buddha-fields be pacified,
and may they all become gentle-minded."
May their minds become pliable;
while remaining in their respective four-continent worlds, may they behold the Buddhas.
And for those beings, may various jewels, various flowers, perfumes, ointments, powders, parasols, banners, and flags appear.
By means of which those beings might worship those Buddhas and generate the resolve for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
and may I myself, Blessed One, behold them through the power of the meditative absorption of the array of visions.
"As soon as these words were spoken, he himself saw it exactly as his vow had been made.
The Blessed One said, "Excellent, excellent, noble son!
You, noble son, shall establish ten thousand pure Buddha-fields, both in the vicinity and within your own Buddha-field."
You will purify the mental continuums of immeasurable and incalculable sentient beings;
likewise, you will apply yourself with zeal to the immeasurable and incalculable worship of immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

"Therefore, noble son, you shall be named Samantabhadra. In a future time, after one incalculable eon equal to the sands of the river Gaṅgā has passed, and when the second incalculable eon remains, in the northern direction, sixty times as many worlds as there are sands in the river Gaṅgā away from this buddha-field, you will become [a Buddha]."
“Having transcended [many] buddha-fields, there will be a world-system named Jñānatāpasuviśuddhaguṇa;

there you, Samantabhadra, will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, and you will become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, [and so on] up to a Buddha, a Blessed One, named Jñānavajravijṛmbhiteśvaraketu.”
Then, noble son, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra prostrated his head at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha with the fivefold circle of limbs.
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:
"Arise, O Surata, O Suvrata! Having purified the mental continuums of sentient beings with a disciplined mind, you have established yourself in firm resolve."
"Save sentient beings from the most terrible river of afflictions; O bearer of the torch of wisdom, you shall become a Buddha in the world."
Furthermore, noble son, at that time ten thousand lazy beings spoke with one voice:
"Venerable Blessed One, we shall become Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in those purified Buddha-fields—
those very pure intentions which the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, establishes as purified."
"In this way, having fulfilled the six perfections, may we be reborn in that buddha-field.
Thus, noble son, ten thousand living beings were prophesied by the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha:
"When Samantabhadra awakens to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, then you shall all awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in those surrounding world-systems."

"You shall become Tathāgatas with names consisting of one thousand [elements]; that is to say, you shall become one thousand Tathāgatas named Jvālakuṇḍeśvaraghoṣa; another thousand shall be named Saṃvṛtīśvaraghoṣa;
and another thousand shall be Tathāgatas named Suvimalaghoṣeśvararāja."
Furthermore, there will be another thousand Tathāgatas named Bhayaghoṣeśvararāja; another thousand will be named Vimalaghoṣatejeśvararāja;
and five hundred will have a single name, namely, Sūryaghoṣa.
Likewise, there were two kings: Vigatabhayakīrti and Vigataraśmi;
and Vigataraśmighoṣakīrtīśvaraghoṣa and Viparadharmakīrtighoṣa.
Garbhakīrtirājaratnadhvaja,
Jyotīśvara, and Uttaptamunijñāneśvara;
Ketacīvarasaṃbhṛtarāja, Acintyamatijñānagarbha,
and Jñānamerudhvaja.
Jñānasāgararāja, Mahāvīryaghoṣeśvara, Meruśrīkalpa,
Jñānavirajavega, Kimīśvarabīja,
and Jñānasuvimalagarjiteśvara.
King Abhibhūtaguṇasāgara,
King Jñānasaṃbhavabala,
and King Virajavīreśvara.
Muniśrīkūṭavegasaṃkusuma, Śrīkūṭajñānabuddhi, and Vajrasiṃha.
Śīlaprabhāsvara,
Bhadrottama, Anantaraśmi,
Siṃhanandi,
Akṣayajñānakūṭa, and Ratnāvabhāsa.
Jñānavimala, Jñānapravāḍa, and Siṃhakīrti.
Abhijñāguṇarāja (King of the Qualities of Supernormal Knowledge), Dharmasumanāvarṣin (Rainer of the Flowers of Dharma), and Prabhākara (Light-Maker).
Abhyudgatameru, Dharmasamudgatarājavimala, and Gandheśvara.
Vimalanetra, Mahāprasannaya, and Asaṅgabalarāja.
Possessing the power of his own knowledge and merit,
clothed in wisdom,
he is a master of all things.
One who seeks what is not clung to,
the source of primordial wisdom,
the great Meru.
Balagarbha, Guṇākara, and Latākusumadhvaja.
Gaṇaprabhāsa, Viguṇamoharāja, and Vajrottama.
Dharmaketu, Ghoṣendrarāja, and Svagupta.
Vajradhvaja, Ratneśvara, and Abhyudgatadhvaja.
Śailakalpa, Ratimegha, and Dharmakārisālarāja.
Samantaguptasāgararāja,
Jñānasaṃnicaya, and Jñānārci.
Kusumagaṇi, Gajendreśvara, and Udumbarapuṣpa.
Kāñcanadhvaja, Dharmadhvaja, and Vinarditarāja.
Candana,
Supratiṣṭhitasthāmavikrama, and Dhvajāgrapradīpa.
Jñānakrama,
Sāgaradhvaja,
and Vyayadharmakīrti.
Māravinardita,
Guṇārcis, and Jñānaprabha.
Jñānapradīpa, Kṣemarāja, and Jñānaghoṣa.
The Collection of Banners,
the Vajra Lamp,
and the King of Arrays.
Jayasaṃkhyā,
Supratiṣṭhita, and King Maticandra.
He whose roar resounds in succession like a king,
whose body has the majesty of a lion of the Sāla tree,
and whose inner strength surpasses that of Nārāyaṇa.
Ratnaguṇasaṃnicaya, Jyotigarbha, and Nakṣatravibhavakīrti.
Puṇyabalasālarāja, Jñānaghoṣa, and Brahmottara.
Dhṛtarāṣṭra;
furthermore, there will be another thousand kings named Gandhapadmavijitakīrtirāja,
and Raśmimaṇḍalajyotiprabhāsarāja.
Gandhapadmottaravega,
Anantaguṇasāgarajñānottara, and Jambucchāya.
Guṇaśailadhvaja, Siṃhaketu,
and Nāgavivarjitakusumatejarāja;
With fragrant seeds as its essence,
it will become like the King of the Splendor of the Qualities of Immortality.
Furthermore, another thousand Dharma-kings will become Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas named Nāgendra-vimukti, Buddhaloka-sāgaralocana, and Śaila.
At one time, on a single day, they will all fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment;
their lifespan in their respective world-systems will be ten intermediate kalpas.”
Those ten thousand beings also prostrated with their heads at the feet of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha by touching them with the five parts of their bodies.
The Tathāgata Ratnagarbha said:
"Arise and roar like mighty elephants; gather a store of auspicious provisions.
Diligent in the perfections and possessing great speed, you shall become leaders of the worlds of asuras and men."
Then, noble son, the brahmin Samudrareṇu addressed the ninth prince, named Amigha.

[The same as before. He said: "I shall practice the conduct of a bodhisattva in such a way that in world-systems in the ten directions equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, those who are staying and maintaining themselves, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā..."
The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, will serve as witnesses for me while I practice the conduct of awakening and throughout my career as a bodhisattva,
from the moment I generate the mind set on awakening in your presence, O Venerable Blessed One, until I fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
In this interval, while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, may no thought of regret arise in me;
until reaching the limit of enlightenment, may I be firm in my vow, acting exactly as I speak, and may there be no agitation of mind in any other sentient being. (KpSū 162)
May no thought for the vehicle of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas arise in me;
may thoughts and mental factors of sensual desire not arise; may they not be accompanied by sloth and torpor, nor by restlessness, nor by remorse, nor by doubt.

There is no taking of life, no taking of what is not given, no unchastity, no false speech, no slander, no harsh speech, no covetousness, no malice, no wrong view, no frivolous chatter, no mind accompanied by stinginess, no lack of respect for the Dharma, and no mind of deception.
Until the very limit of enlightenment, while I am practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, may these qualities never be absent from me.
From the moment of my taking up [the path] until the limit of enlightenment, may mindfulness of the Buddha always proceed within my mind and mental factors, even as I take a single step.
Until the limit of enlightenment, may I never be separated from the vision of the Buddhas, nor from hearing the Dharma, nor from attending upon the Saṅgha.
May I obtain the going forth in all births;
in all births may I be a wearer of rag-robes,

one who possesses only the three robes, a dweller at the foot of trees, one who remains in the sitting posture, a forest-dweller, an eater of alms-food, one of few desires, contented, a teacher of the Dharma, one whose speech is authoritative, and one endowed with immeasurable eloquence.
May I not incur a root downfall;
may I not subdue the proponents of other doctrines with mantras associated with falsehood;
and may I teach the Dharma to women in connection with emptiness.
With a mind focused on emptiness, I shall not show my teeth to women, nor shall I teach the Dharma with gestures of the hands;
and I shall always conceive the notion of the Teacher toward those bodhisattvas who have set out in the Mahāyāna.
And toward whichever Dharma-preacher from whom I might hear the Dharma, I shall produce the perception of him as the Teacher;

and I shall honor that Dharma-preacher with respect, honoring, respecting, revering, and worshiping him just as I would a Tathāgata, even serving the Dharma-preacher with my own flesh; and I shall not give gifts while discriminating between those who are worthy recipients and those who are not.
May no thoughts or mental factors of stinginess regarding the gift of Dharma arise in me.
May I protect beings who seek awakening by giving even my own life,
and may I liberate beings fallen into calamity from their misfortunes by means of wealth acquired through my own vigor, power, and vows.
I shall not reproach one who bears the marks of a renunciant or one who bears the marks of a householder, whether for an actual offense or a non-offense.
And I shall always conceive of gain, honor, and fame as being like fire, poison, or a weapon.
O Venerable Blessed One, if these aspirations of mine, made in the presence of the Blessed One, should be fulfilled until the very limit of enlightenment, [then may my head split into seven pieces].

“May divine wheel-treasures appear from both my hands— possessing a thousand spokes, hubs, and rims, and radiant with a splendor like the color of the sun. As soon as these words were spoken by Prince Amitābha, such wheels appeared from both his hands, exactly as he had requested.

He spoke again: "Venerable Blessed One, if such a wish of mine should be fulfilled until the very limit of enlightenment, then let these wheels go to those empty Buddha-fields of the five corruptions;

and with such a loud sound, as the nāga kings Nanda and Upananda travel, let them make the entire Buddha-field known by their voice [proclaiming] the range of the Buddhas—the practice of the cultivation of emptiness, the vision of knowledge that does not forget the predictions for bodhisattvas."
May this Dharma-discourse be circulated;
and may this Dharma-discourse appear to the sense of hearing of all those beings who have been reborn there, and as soon as it falls upon them, may their passion be pacified.
"May hatred, delusion, pride, envy, and avarice be pacified;
through the mental application of recollecting all the Buddhas, may they generate the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
And those two wheel-treasures were dispatched by the noble son Prince Amīkṣṇa, and they proceeded with such speed that it was just as the Blessed Buddhas travel with the speed of a Buddha.

In this very way, those two wheel-treasures proceed, traveling through immeasurable and incalculable Buddha-fields in the ten directions—fields characterized by the five corruptions—and there they cause beings to practice the Dharma-discourses of the Buddhas, which consist of the cultivation and application of the knowledge that includes the Bodhisattva’s prophecy and the non-forgetfulness of mindfulness.
And for those beings, this [is what occurs]: (KpSū 165)

When this Dharma discourse came within the range of their faculty of hearing, the passion of all those beings, as well as their stinginess and all mental factors associated with the mind, were pacified; and through mental attention, they all directed their minds toward unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, taking the domain of a Buddha’s wisdom as their object.
In just a moment, those wheels turned back and stood before Prince Amīta.
Then, noble son, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha gave his approval to Prince Amīta, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son!"
An exceedingly sublime vow has been made by you;
these divine wheel-treasures have been dispatched to empty Buddha-fields of the five corruptions,
and many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings have been established in minds free from defilement.
And they have been encouraged toward enlightenment.
Therefore, noble son, you shall be named Akṣobhya;
you will become the unshakable leader of the world.
“Take up, Akṣobhya, the arrays of qualities of a buddha-field, however you desire them.

Akṣobhya said: “Venerable Blessed One, I desire such an array of qualities of a buddha-field as this: that the ground of the entire world be made of gold, level like the palm of a hand, strewn with divine jewels and gems, free from pebbles and gravel, free from stones, pillars, rocks, and mountains; soft, with a pleasant touch like *kācalindika* cloth.”
When the soles of his feet are set down, the earth would sink; when the soles of his feet are lifted, it would rise again.
And therein, the realms of hell-beings, animals, the world of Yama, and hungry ghosts would not be perceived.
Furthermore, in that buddha-field there would be no foul-smelling things;
that buddha-field would be suffused with a fragrance surpassing that of the divine, and it would be strewn with divine *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava* flowers.
Furthermore, there would be no aging, sickness, or death for the beings there;
nor would there be mutual fear, nor mutual harm, nor untimely death, nor death with regret, nor death in a state of non-concentration for those beings.
There, the beings would exist through mental attention focused on the recollection of the Buddha.

May they not be reborn in the miserable realms, nor may they be reborn in empty buddha-fields characterized by the five corruptions until their final nirvana at enlightenment; may they never be separated from the sight of the Buddha, never be separated from hearing the Dharma and attending upon the Saṅgha,
and may the sentient beings therein have little passion, little hatred, and little delusion.
And may all there abide having undertaken the ten paths of wholesome action;
and in that buddha-field, there should be no grasping at moral precepts by sentient beings, nor any concern for names and signs.
And there, no Māras shall have access to sentient beings by way of the path;
nor shall the sentient beings there be of ugly appearance,
nor shall the sentient beings there be of discordant proportions.
That is to say, whether noble ones or slaves,
the beings there would be without "mine-ness" and without possessions;
and therein there would be no white liberation for either śrāvakas or bodhisattvas.
Even for those who have entered into dreams, ultimately all beings therein shall be desirous of the Dharma and intent upon seeking the Dharma. Furthermore,
not even a single being in that Buddha-field shall possess perverted views, nor shall there be any belonging to other sects.
And there, among those beings, there would be no physical exhaustion nor mental exhaustion;
and all those beings there would possess the five superknowledges.
Furthermore, neither thirst nor hunger would afflict those beings there.
Whatever kind of food they might desire, that very same shall appear before them in jeweled vessels, just as it does for the gods of the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*).
Furthermore, there shall be no excrement, urine, phlegm, nasal mucus, or tears upon their bodies, nor shall there be sweat;
and there shall be neither cold nor heat in that place.
It would be fragrant and delightful, and soft-touching breezes would blow;
and those [breezes] would perform the function of fragrance for the gods and humans there, according to what they desired, and in whatever manner they might desire it.
Suppose one person should desire cool air, a second warm air, and another should desire the fragrance of a blue lotus.
Others [smelled] the scent of uragasāra sandalwood, others the scent of kālānusāri,
and others the scent of tagara.
Others might desire no foul odor, and others might desire the wind to be entirely absent; for them, it would be accomplished exactly as projected by their arising of thought.
In this way, the world-system would become free from the five corruptions;
and there, for sentient beings, there would be gabled palaces made of the seven precious gems,
and within those gabled palaces, couches made of the seven precious gems would be arranged.
Where those humans dwell, there may appear beds with pillows, having the soft touch of kācalindika cloth;
and all around the gabled pavilions, lotus ponds filled with water endowed with the eight qualities may appear,
wherein those beings may perform their needs for water.
Or let rows of trees of *sumana* and palm trees be adorned;
let those trees be decorated with various flowers, various fruits, various fragrances, various garments, various parasols, various pearl necklaces, and various ornaments.
And whatever kind of clothing or ornament the beings there might desire, they shall take them from those wish-fulfilling trees (*kalpavṛkṣa*) and wear them.
In this manner, having taken flowers up to ornaments, they should bind them [to the tree].

And may my Bodhi tree be composed of the seven precious gems, one thousand yojanas in height, one yojana in the circumference of its trunk, and one thousand yojanas in the circumference of its branches.

Then, stirred by the wind, from that Bodhi tree there shall issue forth a sound surpassing the divine, smooth and pleasing—the sound of the perfections, the superknowledges, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment.
And those beings who hear that sound shall attain minds free from passion and recover their mindfulness.
Furthermore, the women in that Buddha-field shall be endowed with all virtues, just like the celestial nymphs in the Tuṣita heaven.
And there the womenfolk shall not be foul-smelling,
nor shall they be double-tongued or habituated to envy and stinginess;
and there men shall not [be afflicted] by the womenfolk.

They might engage in sexual intercourse and physical contact with them. And if a man there should give rise to a mind imbued with passion, and having approached a woman, he gazes upon her with a passionate mind, in a mere moment that man's passion would be stilled.
They should proceed with great urgency and attain the auspicious, stainless samādhi;
by means of that samādhi, they shall be completely liberated from the snares of Māra.
Furthermore, they would not give rise to a mind of passion again.
And if a woman there were to look at a man with lustful intent, she would become pregnant;
yet, by the mere act of looking, the passion of both would be pacified.
May the boys and girls dwelling in the womb experience such physical and mental happiness as the gods of the Thirty-three rejoice and delight in, experiencing physical and mental happiness;
