for that long may I remain in saṃsāra, having attended upon Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, and for each and every Buddha, may I perform worship as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field.
And from the presence of each individual Buddha, may I attain virtues equal in number to the atoms within a buddha-field,
and may I inspire as many sentient beings as there are atoms in a buddha-field toward awakening.
Likewise, for those belonging to the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas and those belonging to the vehicle of the śrāvakas, I would inspire sentient beings according to their respective inclinations.

In the absence of the arising of a Buddha, I would establish beings in the ten paths of wholesome action through the vow of a world-rishi (*ṛṣi*), and I would establish them in meditative concentration and the supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
To those who are devoted to Maheśvara due to their addiction to false views, I would, in the form of Maheśvara, establish beings in wholesome states;
and to those devoted to Nārāyaṇa, those devoted to the moon and sun, up to those devoted to Brahmā, I would, in the form of Brahmā, establish beings in wholesome dharmas.
In this way, in the form of a garuḍa, I would engage the garuḍa birds in virtuous practices, and so on,
up to the form of Śakra;
and I would satisfy hungry beings with my own flesh and blood.

May I protect beings who have fallen into calamity with my own body and even my life. O Venerable Blessed One, for that long may I wander on my journey with exceedingly great vigor for the sake of those whose mental continuums are scorched and who are deprived of roots of virtue;
and for that long may I endure within saṃsāra, for the sake of sentient beings, various kinds of fierce, terrible, and harsh sufferings.
When many incalculable eons, equal to the sands of more than one Ganges River, have passed away, and when the second incalculable eon,

equal to the sands of the Ganges River, has entered— during the Bhadraka Great Eon— at that time, when the young brahmin Jyotipāla awakens to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment and becomes the Tathāgata named Krakucchanda, then I...

At that time, with the noble eye of wisdom, may I behold the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are currently residing and maintaining their lives in world-systems in the ten directions as numerous as the atoms in a thousand Buddha-fields, turning the wheel of Dharma in accordance with the truth— those Buddhas by whom my own mental continuum was scorched and my roots of unwholesomeness were gathered together.

Those who were devoid of the seven riches, abandoned by all empty buddha-fields, perpetrators of the immediate transgressions, rejecters of the true Dharma, revilers of the noble ones, and even those who were perishing on evil paths— having fallen into such peril— I first inspired them toward, introduced them to, and established them in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

May those beings first be encouraged by me in the perfection of generosity, up until being established in the perfection of wisdom; and may that seed of their roots of merit be cast by me into unsurpassed nirvāṇa,
and may they be fully liberated from the miserable states.

May they be engaged in the accumulations of wisdom and merit while remaining and living in those Buddha-fields; may they be brought into the presence of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, so that they may receive the prophecy of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, attain the meditative concentrations, the dhāraṇīs, and the patient acceptances, and enter the stages; and may those beings [be shown] by me the magnificent arrays of qualities of the Buddha-fields.

They shall be encouraged to take up their vows and instructed accordingly so that they may each grasp for themselves the magnificent arrays of qualities of their respective Buddha-fields; and at that time, when the Fortunate Aeon has entered and the Sun-like Victor Krakucchanda has arisen, I shall [see] the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in as many Buddha-fields in the ten directions as there are atoms in a Buddha-field.
While he remains, sustains his life, and teaches the Dharma to sentient beings, may I behold him; then,
having approached the presence of the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha Krakucchanda, who has not long attained perfect enlightenment, may I perform various kinds of worship.
I would ask a question, I would go forth into homelessness, and I would apply myself to ethical discipline, learning, and meditative concentration.

May I become a teacher of the supreme Dharma; and at that time, for those beings whose mental continuums are scorched, who have fallen into the accumulation of unwholesome roots, who have entered upon the path of wrong views, who have committed the deeds of immediate retribution, and who are being obstructed by the false path— may I teach the Dharma to those beings who have fallen into such great peril.
And I would accept those who are to be trained;

when the Sun of the Jina has set, I would then perform the work of a Buddha effortlessly, until, among a population with a lifespan of a hundred years, I would establish sentient beings in the three bases of meritorious action.
And when that time has passed, having gone to the world of the gods, I would teach the Dharma to the gods.
And I would accept those beings who are to be disciplined as long as the lifespan of sentient beings reaches two thousand years; at that time,
sentient beings will be intoxicated with the pride of power, noble birth, and beauty, and they will be miserly.

Sentient beings cast into the darkness of the five corruptions—possessing intense passion, intense hatred, intense delusion, and intense pride; being intensely sinful, envious, and stingy; stained by an attachment to unrighteousness; seeking unrighteous enjoyments;
holding wrong views and perverted perspectives;
and being devoid of the seven noble riches.

They were disrespectful toward their mothers and disrespectful toward their fathers; they were not respectful toward śramaṇas and not respectful toward brāhmaṇas; they performed what should not be done and performed deeds that do not lead to merit; they saw no fear in the world beyond; they were not diligent regarding the three bases of meritorious action; they had no interest in the three vehicles and were not diligent in them;

they were not diligent in the three types of good conduct but were diligent in the three types of misconduct; they were not diligent in the ten paths of wholesome action but were diligent in the ten unwholesome paths of action.

Regarding the paths of action, sentient beings will be afflicted by the four perversions, established in the four calamities, fallen under the power of the four Māras, carried away by the four floods, and subject to the five hindrances;
they will be intoxicated with pride in their six sense faculties, engaged in the eightfold wrongness, fallen into the straits of sensual desire, and giving rise to latent tendencies.

They have no desire for the glory and prosperity of gods or humans; they hold perverted views and are ruined by following wrong paths; they commit the deeds of immediate retribution, reject the true Dharma, and revile the noble ones; they are deprived of all roots of merit, being like crows—chattering, ungrateful, and forgetful; they loathe what is wholesome, possess poor wisdom, have little learning, and are immoral; they are deceitful, stingy, and speak ill of one another.

They were disrespectful toward one another, indolent, with impaired faculties, weak, and lacking robes; they were influenced by evil friends, had lost the mindfulness regarding the womb, were afflicted by various diseases, distressed, ill-favored in appearance, devoid of modesty, shameless, and terrified of one another.
Those beings who, while eating only one meal a day, engage in much misconduct of body, speech, and mind, will become those who praise the view of eternalism.

Their minds will be attached to the five aggregates; their minds will be greedy for the five strands of sensual pleasure; they will have malicious minds, malevolent minds, hostile minds, harmful minds, turbid minds, harsh minds, agitated minds, untrained minds, harmful-mindedness, and arrogant minds.

Their minds were intent upon unrighteousness; their minds were unstable; their minds were characterized by mutual incitement; their minds were intent on killing one another; their minds were devoid of the Dharma; their minds were immature; their minds were contentious regarding the teachings; their minds had generated unwholesome states;
their minds did not seek peaceful nirvana; their minds were unworthy of offerings; and their minds were engaged in the accumulation of all fetters and bonds.
Their minds lack conviction regarding sickness, old age, and death; their minds are governed by all fetters; their minds embrace all hindrances;

their minds seek to cast down the banner of the Dharma; their minds raise up the banner of false views; their minds disparage one another; their minds are intent on devouring one another; their minds seek power through mutual oppression; their minds grasp at hatred; their minds harbor mutual malice; and their minds remain insatiable for sensual pleasures. (KpSū 236)

At that time, sentient beings will possess minds of grasping at all things and of stinginess, minds of ingratitude, minds of violating the wives of others, minds of malice and violence, and minds devoid of aspiration. Furthermore, they will hear these very words from one another.

The word "hell," the word "animal rebirth," the word "world of Yama," the word "disease," the word "old age," the word "death," the word "executioner," the word "unfavorable conditions," the word "eternal enemy," the word "imprisonment, shackles, bonds, and dungeons," the word "punishment and torture," the word "slander, abuse, and revilement," the word "housebreaking," the word "banditry," the word "theft," the word "foreign armies," and the word "famine."

The word "sexual misconduct," the word "false speech," the word "calamity," the word "slander," the word "harsh speech," the word "frivolous chatter," the word "envy and stinginess," the word "clinging and grasping," the word "the notions of ‘I’ and ‘mine,’" the word "the pleasant and the unpleasant," the word "the liked and the disliked," the word "separation from the beloved," the word "buying and selling," the word "mutual oppression as slaves," and the word "dwelling in the womb."

The sound of foul odors, the sound of cold, the sound of heat, the sound of hunger and thirst, the sound of the sensation of exhaustion and fatigue, the sound of agricultural labor, the sound of those exhausted by various crafts and skills, and the sound of those afflicted by various diseases.
And these beings will hear this from one another.
At that time, the Sahā world-system will be crowded with such beings who have fallen away from roots of merit, who have lost their virtuous friends, and who possess corrupt minds.

Those beings will be abandoned by the Omniscient Ones and by the empty buddha-fields, just as they are devoid of food, drink, self-control, restraint, the performance of wholesome deeds, and association with the virtuous.

Devoid of the noble eightfold path and destined for darkness upon darkness, those beings— by reason of the powerful condition of their karma— will at that time be reborn in this Fortunate Aeon (*bhadrakalpa*) during the period when the lifespan is one hundred and twenty years.
By reason of the karma of those beings, the Buddha-field will become inferior.
It will be abandoned by all sentient beings who have planted roots of merit;
the earth will become salty,
and the ground will consist of stones, gravel, dust, and sand, with mountains rising up in rugged elevations.
It will be infested with harsh gadflies, mosquitoes, venomous snakes, and fierce beasts and birds; winds will blow at improper times and be turbid;
and rains of thunderbolts, mixed with pungent, salty, and unpleasant substances, will fall out of season.

On earth, the grasses, herbs, weeds, trees, leaves, flowers, fruits, grains, and juices will become such that they are unsuitable for the food, drink, enjoyment, and use of sentient beings; they will be defiled, harsh, coarse, and mixed with poison.

Through consuming them, those sentient beings will, to a great degree, become coarse, wicked, fierce, violent, harsh, miserly, abusive, disrespectful toward one another, and possessed of minds full of malice and fear.

They will have murderous minds, consuming meat and drinking blood, wearing deer skins, intent upon weapons, and devoted to the slaughter of living beings; they will be preoccupied with physical beauty, lineage, family, power, treatises, scripts, horsemanship, archery,
and the equipment of arms, and they will be arrogant due to their greed.

At that time, people will be devoted to various harsh ascetic practices and vows. Then, descending from the Tuṣita heaven into an eminent Cakravartin lineage and a sovereign royal family, I shall enter the womb of the chief queen for the sake of ripening the roots of merit of those beings who are to be trained.
At that moment, I shall pervade the entire Sahā Buddha-field with a sublime radiance.
"May I pervade with a sublime radiance everything from above, as far as the limit of the Akaniṣṭha heaven, down to below, as far as the limit of the golden wheel.
And whatever beings at that time are born in this Sahā buddha-field— whether in the hells, or in the animal realm, or in the world of Yama, or among gods and humans—
may they all see, touch, and perceive that radiance."

As they reflect upon cyclic existence and become distressed by suffering, may I cause them to generate within their hearts a longing for nirvāṇa and minds that seek the pacification of the afflictions.
May I thus plant this first seed of the supreme path.

And while my mind is in meditative equipoise, may I dwell for ten months in my mother’s womb, teaching the single gateway of all phenomena—the exposition of all samādhis—which is the wisdom regarding the method of all dharmas, through an exposition that reaches to the furthest limit of time.

And for as long as I, having attained Buddhahood, might liberate beings exhausted by cyclic existence, may those beings see me while still within my mother’s womb for ten months, seated cross-legged with a mind concentrated on the manifestation of a jewel-treasury; and when the ten months have passed, through the accumulation of all merit and through meditative absorption, may I cause the entire world-system and the earth to tremble in six ways.
From above, as far as the limit of the Akaniṣṭha heaven, and from below, as far as the limit of the golden wheel, may I cause them to tremble in six ways.
And at that time, whatever beings have been born in this Sahā Buddha-field—whether in the hells or up to among humans—may I awaken them.
When I emerge from my mother’s right side, may I do so.
Furthermore, I would fill the entire Sahā buddha-field with a magnificent radiance;
at that time, I would also inspire all sentient beings in the Sahā buddha-field and plant the seed of nirvāṇa within the mental continuums of those beings who have not yet planted roots of virtue.

May I cause the sprout of meditative concentration to grow for those beings whose continuums have planted the seed of nirvāṇa. And when I touch the earth with the sole of my foot, at that moment may the entire Sahā buddha-field shake, tremble, and quiver in six ways,
as far as the limit of the golden wheel.

Then, at that time, I would awaken all those beings— those dwelling in water, those dwelling on land, those dwelling in the air, those included within the four modes of birth, and those residing in the five destinies—
and I would plant the unarisen sprout of meditative concentration within the mental continuums of those beings;
I would establish them as non-retrogressive through the three vehicles, possessing firm sprouts of meditative concentration.

And as soon as I am born, may all the Great Brahmās, Māras, Śakras, moons, suns, world-protectors, great nāga kings, lords of the asuras, those of miraculous birth, those of great supernatural power, or the yakṣas, rākṣasas, nāgas, and asuras in that Sahā buddha-field approach me for the purpose of making offerings.
And immediately upon being born, I would take seven steps;
by means of the samādhi called the Accumulation of All Merit, I would teach such a Dharma that the entire assembly would attain serene confidence through the three vehicles.
And those beings in that assembly who might belong to the vehicle of the śrāvakas shall be my disciples in their final existence;

and those beings there who might belong to the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas shall attain the patience known as Vairocanakusumā; and all those beings there who might belong to the unsurpassed Mahāyāna shall attain the samādhi called the "Contraction of the Ocean of Vajradharas."
By means of that samādhi, they would transcend the three stages.
Whenever I desire to bathe, those great nāga kings who are most distinguished there should bathe me;
and whatever sentient beings should see me being bathed, they shall all attain such qualities through the three vehicles as have been described.

And those beings who saw me mounting the chariot— in detail, he saw the various places for princely play, the sites of crafts and occupations, and the harem suitable for instruction; he saw the delight in the play of the five strands of sensual pleasure at midnight, his agitation and departure, the casting off of ornaments and finery,
his frequent wearing of red garments and seeking saffron robes, and his approach to the Bodhi tree.
And whatever beings should see me approaching,
for those beings I would teach such a Dharma through the concentration of the Accumulation of All Merit, so that those beings would apply themselves with intense aspiration to the three vehicles.
And whatever beings there may be who belong to the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas, may they all attain the patience of Vairocanakusuma;

and those by whom the seed of the Mahāyāna has been sown, may they all attain the samādhi called the "Contraction of the Ocean of Vajradharas," and by that samādhi may they transcend the three stages.
Furthermore, may I myself take a bed of grass, prepare the Vajrāsana at the foot of the Bodhi tree, and sit down, having assumed the cross-legged posture with my body held straight.
In such a manner, may I practice that Āsphānaka meditation,
may I bring the inhalations and exhalations to cessation,
and may I emerge from that meditation only once a day.
Having emerged from that state, I would take as my food only half a sesame seed, and I would give the other half to a recipient;
and for such a long time I would practice such a course of difficult austerities.
May all the gods, as far as the limit of the Akaniṣṭha heaven, who are included within this Sahā buddha-field, approach and perform worship to me,
and may they all be witnesses to my practice of austerities.

And for those who have planted the seed in the vehicle of the śrāvakas there, O Venerable Blessed One, may I exist within their mental continuums for the sake of the pacification of their afflictions.
May those who are in their final existence be my disciples to be trained;
those who belong to the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas,
and so forth, as previously described.

In this way, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, pretas, piśācas, and kumbhāṇḍas, as well as ṛṣis possessing the five superknowledges, might approach for the purpose of making offerings to me,
and all of them would become witnesses to my practice of austerities; and those belonging to the vehicle of the disciples (śrāvakayānika), and so forth, just as previously described.
And whatever non-Buddhist practitioners there may be in that four-continent world-system who perform ascetic penances, vows, and difficult austerities,
non-human beings should announce to them:
"You are not performers of difficult deeds."

Just as in this region the Bodhisattva in his final existence practices the course of austerities, so he meditates, fixes his attention in the heart, with his bodily formations calmed and his vocal formations calmed, and his inhalations and exhalations are tranquil;
and day by day, having arisen from meditation at one time, he takes food in the measure of half a sesame seed.
"That practice of austerities is of great supernatural power, it yields great fruit, and it is of vast extent;
before long, he will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. If you do not believe me, go and see for yourselves."
And having abandoned that practice of austerities and seen my own practice of austerities, those in whose mental continuum the sprout of the seed of the Śrāvaka-vehicle was established—
up to everything as previously stated—
those who were kings of men (KpSū 244).

Whether they be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, laymen, or laywomen— whether householders or renunciants— who are well-established in their homes, even they would come to me for the practice of austerities, as previously described for those belonging to the vehicle of the śrāvakas;
and whatever woman should come to see me,
that would be her final acquisition of a female body.
Those who belong to the Śrāvaka vehicle are as previously described.
As for those beasts and birds who might see me seated while practicing austerities, let this be their final rebirth in the animal realm.

And those beasts and birds by whom seeds have been sown in the Śrāvaka vehicle—let them be bound to only one more birth and become my own disciples. Those [bound to] the Pratyekabuddha vehicle are as previously described.

Such minor beings of the animal realm are to be described; likewise, the hungry ghosts (pretas) are to be described. Furthermore, for so long a time I would practice such difficult austerities (duṣkaracaryā) in a single cross-legged posture, until many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings become witnesses to my practice of austerities and are struck with wonder.
And in their continuums, I would plant the seeds of liberation for immeasurable and incalculable beings.

I would practice such difficult austerities that no being previously counted among sentient beings— whether a follower of another sect, one belonging to the vehicle of the Śrāvakas, one belonging to the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas, or one belonging to the unsurpassed Mahāyāna— had ever before performed such difficult austerities.
Furthermore, let no one counted among sentient beings— whether followers of other sects or others— be able to perform such a course of difficult practices as I shall perform.
Until I have attained unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, I will then exert my human effort and, with my host of forces, defeat Māra.
I shall take hold of the remaining fruits of my karma,
I shall conquer the Māra of the afflictions,
and I shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

Therefore, I would establish the state of arhatship within the continuum of one sentient being; likewise for a second, likewise for a third, and likewise for a fourth, I would teach the Dharma and establish the state of arhatship within their continua.
For the sake of each and every sentient being, I would display hundreds of thousands of miracles and establish right view within their mental continuum.
I would speak many thousands of words concerning the Dharma, its meaning, and its phrasing, and I would establish beings in the fruit according to their capacity.

I would shatter the mountains of afflictions within the mental continuums of sentient beings— which are as hard as adamant— with the vajra of primordial wisdom, and I would teach the Dharma by means of the formal arrangement of the three vehicles.

For the sake of even a single being, I would travel on foot for many hundreds of yojanas to teach the Dharma and establish them in the state of fearlessness. And there shall be no prohibition against going forth into homelessness within my teaching,
even for a woman who is weak, of impaired memory, distracted in mind, talkative and arrogant in mind, malevolent in mind, of poor wisdom, or whose mind is agitated by many afflictions.
May there be the going forth and full ordination within my teaching;
may I have four assemblies—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen;

may my teaching become widespread among many people; and may there be for the gods the vision of the truth, for the yakṣas, nāgas, and asuras the observance of the fast day endowed with the eight limbs of the noble ones.
"May the practice of celibacy prevail even among those born as animals.

And when I have attained awakening, O Venerable Blessed One, may those beings who, with malicious intent or murderous intent, approach me with weapons, fire, spears, or various other instruments of assault; who revile, abuse, or scold me with harsh and cruel words; or who spread reports of my ill repute in all directions and intermediate directions—"
Or they might offer me food and drink mixed with poison;
yet, having been sustained by such fruits of karma that are not exhausted, may I awaken to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Such that when I have attained awakening, sentient beings—driven by former enmity—might approach me with murderous intent, employing weapons, harsh words, and various blows, or even with food and drink mixed with poison, [and cause my] blood [to flow].

And should they give rise to [such thoughts], I would teach the Dharma to those beings with a voice cultivated by morality, learning, concentration, and great compassion— a voice like the sound of Brahmā’s tone or the roar of a celestial drum—
so that I might gladden their minds and establish them in what is wholesome.
So that those beings might confess their karmic obstructions and undertake restraint regarding their transgressions,
and so that for those beings there may be no obstructing karma with respect to heaven, the fruit of liberation, dispassion, or the destruction of the outflows.
And may my own [karmic debt] be exhausted here by the exhaustion of the fruits of my karma.

Furthermore, O Venerable Blessed One, once I have attained awakening, may I emanate as many forms of the Buddha’s body as there are pores on my skin for the duration of a single day— forms adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and the eighty secondary characteristics— and may I [sustain them].
I would dispatch emanations of the Buddha to empty buddha-fields,
and I would dispatch them to non-empty ones as well,
and I would dispatch them to buddha-fields of the five corruptions.

And furthermore, whatever beings there might be in those buddha-fields who have committed the acts of immediate retribution, who reject the true Dharma, who revile the noble ones, and so forth, up to those who are possessed of the roots of unwholesomeness;

and even those beings there who have set out in the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, or the Great Vehicle, yet who act with impurity regarding the training, who act with flaws, who have fallen into root downfalls, whose mental continuums are burnt, and who have lost their way on the path of virtue— [may they all attain supreme enlightenment].
There are beings who have set out into the wilderness of saṃsāra, being struck down by wrong paths and fallen into great peril;
for such beings, a single Buddha-form might teach the Dharma to hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings in a single day.
To those beings who are devoted to Maheśvara, I would teach the Dharma in the form of Maheśvara.
In the Sahā Buddha-field, they would proclaim my praises, and there I would inspire beings to make their vows.
Having heard my praises, those beings would then make their vows for my very own Buddha-field.
And they would desire rebirth. "O Venerable Blessed One, if at the time of death of those beings I were not to stand before them, were not to teach the Dharma, and were not to gladden their minds,
may I not attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

If, after passing away, sentient beings were to be reborn in the miserable realms and fail to obtain human birth in my buddha-field, all my teachings would fall into oblivion, they would not occur to me, and I would not be able to accomplish the entirety of the work of a Buddha.

Furthermore, if those sentient beings who are devoted to Nārāyaṇa— up to and including those sentient beings who, after passing away, were to fall into the miserable realms— were to do so, then I would not be able to accomplish the entirety of the work of a Buddha.

And when I have attained awakening, in all Buddha-fields, those beings who have committed the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*), up to those who are obstructed by wrong paths and have fallen into great peril— those beings who, having died, are reborn in my Buddha-field— shall, for that reason, become beings with the color of dust; they shall be Piśāca-faced, with lost mindfulness, foul-smelling, immoral, short-lived, afflicted by various diseases, and deprived of various necessities.
For the sake of those beings, as long as there may be four-continent world-systems in that Sahā world-realm,

I shall manifest a descent from the Tuṣita abode into every one of those four-continent systems, and my birth from the womb of a mother; and I shall extensively display the childhood play, the training in the arts and crafts, the practice of austerities, the subduing of Māra, the perfect awakening to enlightenment, and the turning of the wheel of Dharma.
And in all the four-continent worlds, may I manifest the entirety of the Buddha-activity, displaying everything from my final nirvana up to the distribution of my relics;
and having attained awakening, may I teach the Dharma with the utterance of a single word.
Those beings who belong to the vehicle of the disciples (śrāvakayānika) shall understand the Dharma taught as the scriptural collection of the discourse on the vehicle of the disciples;

those beings who are to be disciplined by the vehicle of the solitary buddhas (pratyekabuddha) shall understand the Dharma taught as the discourse on the vehicle of the solitary buddhas; and those beings who belong to the unsurpassed Great Vehicle (anuttaramahāyānika) shall understand the Dharma taught as the discourse on the unsurpassed Great Vehicle.

Those beings who are devoid of the accumulations of merit should understand the Dharma taught through discourses on generosity; those beings who are devoid of merit and long for happiness and heaven should understand the Dharma taught through discourses on ethical discipline;
and those whose minds are turbid with mutual fear and malice should understand the Dharma taught through discourses on the expression of loving-kindness.
Those who have committed the taking of life may understand the Dharma taught as compassion;

those who are overcome by envy and stinginess may understand the Dharma taught through discourse on sympathetic joy; and those whose minds are intoxicated with the pride of the form and formless realms may understand the Dharma taught through discourse on equanimity.
Those whose minds are intoxicated by the pride of sensual desire may understand the Dharma taught through discourse on the foul;
those beings who have fallen into a mind agitated by the restlessness of the Mahāyāna may understand the Dharma taught through discourse on mindfulness of breathing;
and those of poor wisdom may understand the Dharma taught through discourse on the lamp of dependent origination.

Those who speak with little learning should understand the Dharma taught through the discourse on the non-forgetting, the dhāraṇī of hearing, and its non-perishing; those fallen into the straits of wrong views should understand the Dharma taught through the discourse on emptiness;

those afflicted by the activity of discursive thought should understand the Dharma taught through the discourse on the signless; and those afflicted by the lack of purity regarding the wishless should understand the Dharma taught through the discourse on the wishless.
Those whose intentions are unpurified may understand the Dharma taught through the discourse on purified intention;
those impaired by mixed conduct may understand the Dharma taught through the discourse on the non-forgetfulness of the thought of awakening;
and those impaired by the heat of patient application [may understand it through the discourse on the perfection of patience].

Those with artificial speech should understand the Dharma taught through unartificial speech; those afflicted by a lack of resolute intention and pliancy should understand the Dharma taught through non-reliant speech; and those with defiled minds—[and so forth]—should [understand it] through speech that is pure in intent.
Those whose minds have forgotten what is wholesome [are taught] by means of the discourse on Vairocana;
those engaged in the deeds of Māra [are taught] by means of the discourse on emptiness;
those intent on the slaughter of others [are taught] by means of the discourse on the Exalted One.

Those whose minds are afflicted by various defilements [are to be understood] through the discourse on departure; those who have entered upon a perilous path [are to be understood] through the discourse on turning back; those whose minds are curious about the Mahāyāna [are to be understood] through the discourse on turning away.
For Bodhisattvas who are weary of saṃsāra, it is by means of discourse on delight; for those who have attained knowledge of the stages of virtue, it is by means of discourse on non-delusion;
for those whose roots of virtue are not mutually satisfied, it is by means of discourse on learning.
By means of the discourse on unimpeded rays for those whose minds are mutually unequal;
by means of the discourse on the introduction to action for those engaged in uneven karma;
and by means of the discourse on the lion-banner for those who have fallen into fear of assemblies.
For those whose minds have overcome the four Māras,
by means of the discourse on heroism;
for those beings who have gone to unilluminated Buddha-fields, by means of the discourse on the array of light.
For those with attachment and aversion, it is expressed by the term "mountain peak"; for those overwhelmed by the light of the Buddha-dharma, it is expressed by the term "banner-top ornament";
for those lacking great wisdom, it is expressed by the term "falling meteor."

For those fallen into the darkness of delusion, by means of the discourse on the lamp of the sun; for those engaged in the ineffability of exhaustion, by means of the discourse on the mine of virtues; for those desiring a self comparable to a mass of foam, by means of the discourse on Nārāyaṇa.
For those of unstable intellect, by means of discourse following the essence;
for those whose heads have been looked upon [by the Buddha], by means of the discourse of Merudhvaja;
for those who have relinquished their former vows, by means of the discourse of Sāravatī.
For those who have fallen away from the superknowledges, by means of the expression "vajra-word";
for those who long for the seat of enlightenment, by means of the expression "vajra-maṇḍala";
for those who loathe all phenomena, by means of the expression "vajra-like."
[It is taught] by means of discourse on conduct for those who do not understand the behavior of sentient beings;
by means of discourse on the lamp of wisdom for those who do not know the superior and inferior faculties [of others];
and for those who do not understand the cries of one another... [KpSū 253]
By means of discourse on the entry into sounds;

by means of discourse on the manifestation of the body of the true Dharma for those who have not yet attained the Dharma-body; and by means of discourse on the unblinking gaze for those who are deprived of the vision of the Tathāgata.
For those obscured by all objects of perception, [he speaks] with the discourse of the forest;

for those longing for the turning of the wheel of Dharma, with the discourse of the stainless wheel; for those who have set out upon the science of non-causality, with the discourse on the conformity of dependent origination.

For those who hold the view that a single buddha-field is eternal, [he teaches] by means of discourse on the discernment of well-performed deeds; for those who have not planted the seeds for the primary and secondary marks, [he teaches] by means of discourse on the possession of ornaments;
for those incapable of the distinctions of beautiful speech, [he teaches] by means of discourse on accomplishment.

For those who long for the wisdom of omniscience, by means of discourse that does not disturb the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); for those whose phenomena revolve in the present, by means of firm discourse;
and for those who do not understand the realm of phenomena, by means of discourse on the superknowledges (*abhijñā*).
By means of unerring speech for those who have been released by wisdom; by means of unchanging speech for those whose path has been protected;
and by means of speech free from possessions for those who long for knowledge equal to space.
By means of discourse on the pure foundation for those who have fulfilled the perfections;
by means of discourse on being well-gathered for those whose means of attraction are not yet complete;
and by means of discourse on equal application for those who seek the divine abodes.
For those who have not yet fulfilled the jewels of the factors of enlightenment, by means of discourse on the non-abiding departure;
for those with well-spoken knowledge whose minds are distracted, by means of discourse on the ocean-seal;
for those whose minds are curious about the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena, by means of discourse on certainty.

By means of discourse on non-forgetfulness for those whose minds have forgotten the Dharma as they heard it; by means of discourse that dispels the darkness for those who are not satisfied with one another’s well-spoken words; and by means of discourse on the abundance of merit for those who have not yet attained faith in the Three Jewels.
For those who are not satisfied with the raining down of the gateways of Dharma, [one speaks] by means of the discourse on the Cloud of Dharma;
for those with views that the Three Jewels are subject to cessation, by means of the discourse on the Array of Jewels;
for those devoted to actions that obstruct wisdom, by means of the discourse on the Incomparable.
For those who have entered into the bonds of all fetters,
by means of the expression "the gateway of space";
for those whose minds are not other than all phenomena.
By means of discourse on the seal of gnosis (*jñānamudrā*);

by means of discourse on the manifestation of worldly knowledge for those who have not yet perfected the qualities of a Tathāgata; and by means of discourse on the definitive miraculous displays for those who have performed meritorious service under previous Buddhas.

by means of the discourse on the principles of all phenomena for those [teachings] taught throughout kalpas reaching to the furthest limit through the gateway of a single dharma; by means of the discourse on the determination of the equality of the intrinsic nature of phenomena for those sūtras that have not been definitively resolved; and by means of the discourse on the principles of all phenomena for those [teachings] devoid of the six factors conducive to liberation.
For those not yet dedicated to the mental disposition for liberation, [he teaches] by means of discourse on the playful exercise of the superknowledges;
for those who have investigated the entry into the secrets of the Tathāgata, by means of discourse that is not led by others;
and for those not yet dedicated to the conduct of a bodhisattva, by means of discourse on the arrival of primordial wisdom.
For those who desire to see their kinsmen, by means of discourse that follows everywhere; for those whose bodhisattva conduct remains incomplete, by means of discourse on the consecration;
for those who have not yet perfected the ten powers of a Tathāgata, by means of discourse on being unassailable.

By means of discourse on the inexhaustible for those who have not yet attained the four grounds of self-confidence; by means of discourse on the unassailable for those who have not yet attained the unique qualities of a Buddha; and by means of discourse on the vow for those whose hearing and sight are never in vain.

May they understand the Dharma being taught so that they may realize all Buddha-qualities directly through the ocean-like utterance of the stainless for those whose hearing is turbid; through the perfectly awakened utterance for those whose omniscient wisdom is still incomplete; and through the utterance of infinite consummation for those who have not yet attained the intentions regarding the tasks of all Tathāgatas.

For those bodhisattvas who are free from deceit, free from guile, upright, and of an upright nature— for them, by the utterance of a single word, may I establish these qualities within the mental continuum of the immeasurable and incalculable beings set out upon the Mahāyāna: eighty-four thousand gateways to the Dharma, eighty-four thousand gateways to meditative concentration, and seventy-five thousand gateways to dhāraṇīs.
By means of which bodhisattva mahāsattvas may become armored with the great armor;

they may emerge preeminent through the excellence of inconceivable vows; they may be adorned with the sublime qualities of awakening consisting of inconceivable knowledge and vision—namely, being adorned with the body through the primary marks and secondary characteristics.
May they have speech adorned according to their intentions;
may they satisfy sentient beings with well-spoken words; and may they be adorned by learning through the state of non-discursiveness in meditative concentration.
They are adorned with mindfulness through the non-forgetfulness of dhāraṇīs;
they are adorned with the mind through being adorned with peace, by virtue of awakening to the miserable destinies;
they are adorned with intention through the firmness of their vows.
They are adorned with application by virtue of fulfilling their vows; they are adorned with resolute intention by virtue of transitioning from stage to stage;
they are adorned with generosity by virtue of relinquishing all things.
Adorned with ethical discipline through being well-heard, purified, and stainless;
adorned with patience through having a mind that is unimpeded toward all sentient beings;
adorned with vigor through the accumulation of all provisions.
They would be adorned with meditative concentration, sporting in all meditative attainments and supernormal knowledges,
and adorned with wisdom.
Having fully understood the latent tendencies of the afflictions,
they are adorned with loving-kindness and follow the protection of all sentient beings;
adorned with compassion, they abide in the non-abandonment of all sentient beings.
Adorned with sympathetic joy, they have attained freedom from doubt regarding all phenomena;
adorned with equanimity, they are free from the duality of elevation and depression;
adorned with the superknowledges, they possess mastery over all miraculous powers.

Adorned with merit, they have attained the state of having jewels of inexhaustible enjoyment in their hands; adorned with wisdom, they possess supernormal knowledge of the mental activities of all sentient beings;
adorned with intelligence, they are those who awaken all sentient beings through skillful means in the Dharma.

Adorned with light, may they obtain the light of the eye of wisdom; adorned with analytical knowledge, may they attain the analytical knowledges of meaning, phenomena, etymology, and eloquence; adorned with fearlessness, may they overcome all Māras and adversaries;
and adorned with virtues, may they attain the virtues of the Buddhas.
Adorned with the Dharma, they would constantly and continuously teach the Dharma to sentient beings through unimpeded eloquence;
adorned with light, they have attained the illumination of all Buddha-dharmas; adorned with radiance, they have attained the illumination of all Buddha-fields.

They are adorned with the miracle of manifestation (*ādarśanaprātihārya*), being those who grant unerring prophecies; they are adorned with the miracle of instruction (*anuśāsanīprātihārya*), being those who bestow instruction exactly as it is;
and they are adorned with the miracle of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*), having attained the supreme perfection of the four bases of psychic power (*catur-ṛddhipāda*).
May they be adorned by the empowerment of all Tathāgatas and have entered the secrets of the Tathāgatas;

may they be adorned by sovereignty over the Dharma and have attained knowledge that is not dependent on others; may they be adorned by the essence of the practice of all wholesome dharmas, and be invincible in every respect as those who act exactly as they speak.
With a single utterance of a word, may I satisfy immeasurable and incalculable beings who have set out in the Mahāyāna by means of a great accumulation for the purification of virtue;
thereby, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas may attain knowledge that is independent of others regarding all phenomena,
and they may become endowed with a great radiance of the Dharma.
"And may they swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Furthermore, O Venerable Blessed One, those beings who might exist in other world-systems—whether they be perpetrators of the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*), or those guilty of root downfalls (*mūlāpatti*), or those whose mental continuums are scorched; whether they belong to the vehicle of the Hearers (*śrāvakayāna*), the vehicle of the Solitary Buddhas (*pratyekabuddhayāna*), or the unsurpassed Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*)—by the power of their aspiration...
May they be reborn in my buddha-field.
For those who are possessed of unwholesome roots, harsh, evil-minded,
of cruel and stubborn disposition, perverted in intellect, and of grasping nature— may I teach them eighty-four thousand languages of the mind.
Furthermore, for the sake of those beings whose minds are indolent, I would extensively teach the eighty-four thousand heaps of Dharma;

and for those beings therein who belong to the unsurpassed Mahāyāna, I would extensively teach the Dharma of the six perfections— extensively teaching the perfection of generosity, and so on, up to extensively teaching the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, whatever beings there may be therein who belong to the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, who have not planted roots of merit,
yet long for a teacher—
I would establish them in the three refuges,
and thereafter I would direct them toward the perfections;
for those who delight in violence, I would establish them in the abstention from taking life.
I would establish those overcome by improper greed in the abstention from taking what is not given; I would establish those stained by unrighteous passion in the abstention from sexual misconduct;
and I would establish those who speak harsh words to one another in the abstention from false speech.
I would establish them;
I would establish those who delight in intoxication in the abstention from fermented liquor, spirits, and the negligence of intoxicants;
and for those beings who possess all five faults, I would establish them in the lay practitioner's vow of abstaining from the five faults.
Those beings who take no delight in wholesome qualities, may I establish them day and night in the eightfold precepts.

Those beings whose minds delight in meager roots of virtue, may I also cause them to draw near to the well-expounded Dharma and Vinaya, and establish them in the celibate life, in the ten precepts of the renunciant’s discipline.
Those beings who desire to seek wholesome qualities, I too shall encourage them toward wholesome qualities and establish them in the complete practice of the holy life (*brahmacarya*).

For the sake of such beings—even those who have committed the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*) up to those whose mental continuums are gripped by affliction—I shall teach the Dharma through various and manifold miracles of meaning, phrases, and syllables;
I shall demonstrate that the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases are impermanent, suffering, selfless, and empty.
May I establish them in the wholesome, secure, auspicious, and peaceful city of fearlessness that is nirvāṇa.
In this way, may I teach the Dharma to the fourfold assembly of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen;
and to those who seek debate, may I reveal the treatises on the discourse of the Dharma.

And for those who do not delight in wholesome qualities, I would prescribe for them tasks of service; for those who delight in recitation and who, with one-pointedness, proceed toward emptiness, meditative concentration, and liberation, I would provide instruction.
For the sake of each and every sentient being, I would travel on foot for many hundreds of thousands of yojanas;
with various and manifold means, phrases, syllables, and miraculous displays, I would strive tirelessly until I establish them in nirvāṇa.
"By the power of my concentration, may I relinquish five parts of my life-formations; and at the time of my final nirvana, may I myself divide my own body into pieces the size of mustard seeds,
and for the sake of compassion toward sentient beings, may I subsequently enter parinirvāṇa."
After my final nirvāṇa, may the True Dharma remain for a thousand years,
and may the semblance of the True Dharma remain for another five hundred years.

And may those beings who, after my final nirvāṇa, apply themselves to the desire to worship my relics with jewels, or even with musical instruments— down to the mere utterance of a single Buddha’s name, a single prostration, a single circumambulation, or the act of joining their palms in reverence— [attain their goal].
If they were to perform worship with even a single flower,
they would all become non-retrogressive according to their aspirations through the three vehicles.

Furthermore, those beings who, after my final nirvana, should take up even a single precept within my teaching, and having undertaken it as prescribed, abide by it— even if they should master or recite only a four-line verse— [they shall likewise attain this].
And they would teach it to others;

and those who might hear it, or whose minds might become serene, or who would offer worship to the Dharma-preacher— even with a single flower or even a single prostration— [would all attain this samādhi].
May they all become non-retrogressive according to their inclinations through the three vehicles;
and even when the true Dharma has disappeared, the torch of the true Dharma has been extinguished, and the banner of the Dharma has fallen,
may they descend into my birth-body and remain as long as the golden wheel endures in this Sahā Buddha-field.
At that time, there will be a famine of jewels; however, a jewel named Ketumati, made of vaidūrya and radiant as fire, shall remain.
Rising up from there, it will stay as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven and rain down a manifold shower of flowers.

A rain of flowers such as these would fall: *māndārava*, *mahāmāndārava*, *pārijātaka*, *mañjuṣaka*, *mahāmañjuṣaka*, *rocana*, *mahārocana*, *pūrṇacandra*, *vimala*, *śatapatra*, *sahasrapatra*, *śatasahasrapatra*, *samantaprabha*, *samantagandha*, *surucira*, *sadāphala*, *hṛdayanayanābhiramya*, *jyotiprabha*, *jyotirasa*, *anantavarṇa*, *anantagandha*, and *anantaprabha*.
Such was the rain of flowers that fell.

And then, from that rain of flowers, various sounds would issue forth, such as: the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," the sound of "Saṅgha," the sound of the "lay practitioner's vows," the sound of the "Uposatha fast endowed with the eight noble limbs," the sound of the "vows of the ten training rules for those who have gone forth," the sound of "generosity," the sound of "ethical discipline," the sound of "full ordination consisting of the complete perfection of the holy life," the sound of "service," and the sound of "study."

The sound of solitary retreat; the sound of appropriate mental attention; the sound of the foul; the sound of mindfulness of breathing; the sound of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;

the sound of the sphere of nothingness; the sound of the sphere of infinite consciousness; the sound of the sphere of infinite space; the sound of the spheres of mastery; the sound of the spheres of totality; the sound of calm abiding and insight; the sound of emptiness and wishlessness; the sound of the signless; and the sound of dependent origination.
The sound of the entire Śrāvaka-piṭaka would issue forth; the sound of the entire Pratyekabuddha-yāna-piṭaka would issue forth;
and the sound of all Mahāyāna discourses and the six pāramitās—those flowers would scatter [them].
And all the gods of the form realm (rūpāvacara) shall hear [this],

and they shall each remember their own previously performed roots of merit (kuśalamūla). Those great beings (mahāsattva), who are not to be disparaged regarding any wholesome qualities (kuśaladharma), shall descend from there and establish all humans in the Sahā world-system in the ten paths of wholesome action (daśakuśalakarmapatha).

In the same way, if all the gods of the desire realm were to hear [this], it would cause the cessation of all their mental states and mental factors— those characterized by the fetter of craving, delight in play, and attachment to joy—
and they would all remember their own previously cultivated roots of merit;
having descended from the world of the gods, they would all exhort and establish the humans in the Sahā world in the ten paths of wholesome action.

And those flowers would manifest in the sky as various kinds of jewels— namely, O Venerable Blessed One, silver, gold, precious gems, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, white silver, native gold, emeralds, and right-spiraling conches—
and such a rain of jewels would fall throughout the entire Sahā Buddha-field.
And may all strife, quarrels, disputes, famine, disease, foreign armies, harsh speech, and cruel poisons in the Sahā Buddha-field be entirely pacified;
and may the entire Sahā Buddha-field become established in security, health, freedom from strife, absence of imprisonment and conflict, and abundance.
And may whatever sentient beings see those jewels, touch them, or perform acts of enjoyment with them [attain these benefits].
May they all become irreversible from the three vehicles, and may they remain as far down as the Golden Wheel; even so,
O Venerable Blessed One, at the time of the intermediate eon of weapons, may those sapphire jewels remain once more as far up as the limit of the Akaniṣṭha heaven.
Having stood there, they would rain down various showers of flowers,

such as the māndārava, mahāmāndārava, and pāriyātra, up to those of infinite radiance; and from that shower of flowers, various pleasant sounds would issue forth, such as the sound of "Buddha," the sound of "Dharma," the sound of "Saṅgha," and so on, up to what was previously mentioned.
Furthermore, those relics would descend as far down as the golden wheel.

At that time, during the period of the intermediate aeon of famine, those relics would again ascend upwards as far as the limit of the Akaniṣṭha heaven, with a rain of flowers, just as previously described;
and this would continue until the end of the intermediate aeon of disease, just as previously described.

Just as in the Bhadraka Great Kalpa, after I have entered parinirvāṇa, they shall perform the work of spreading my relics, and I shall establish countless beings to be trained in the state of non-retrogression through the three vehicles;

even so, throughout five great kalpas equal in number to the atoms within five buddha-fields, may my relics train sentient beings and establish them in the state of non-retrogression through the three vehicles. When... (KpSū)

Afterwards, when incalculable eons, as numerous as the sands of a thousand Ganges rivers, have passed, may those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, arise in immeasurable and incalculable world-systems throughout the ten directions— those who, while I was a bodhisattva practicing the conduct for unexcelled perfect enlightenment,
were first inspired by me toward unexcelled perfect enlightenment and established therein.
May I also have inspired, introduced, and established [beings] in the six perfections.

And when I have attained awakening, may I likewise inspire, introduce, and establish beings in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening; and furthermore, may there be those beings who, even through the manifestation of my body after I have passed into parinirvāṇa, [are established] in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.

If they were to generate that thought, then later, in the ten directions— in immeasurable and incalculable world-systems, both those currently existing and those that have passed away during incalculable aeons as numerous as the sands of a thousand Ganges rivers— those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment would speak my praise, cause it to be heard, and raise their voices, saying: "Long ago, there was an aeon named Bhadra."
And when that great Bhadraka Kalpa had entered, there appeared a Tathāgata named Jinabhāskara, the fourth [in that kalpa],
by whom we were first inspired toward, established in, and settled upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

"Those whose mental continuums were scorched, who had fallen into unwholesome associations, who committed the deeds of immediate retribution, and even those with wrong views—we have been inspired, introduced to, and established by him in the six perfections.
By this means, we are now omniscient and turn the wheel of Dharma in all its aspects;
furthermore, having turned back the wheel of cyclic existence, we establish many hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of sentient beings in the heavenly realms and in the fruit of liberation."
And those beings who seek awakening, upon hearing my praise, renown, and fame in the presence of those Tathāgatas, should ask that Tathāgata:
"Perceiving what purpose did that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening while dwelling in this degenerate age of the five corruptions?
And those Tathāgatas [should explain] to those sons of good family or daughters of good family seeking awakening this [sūtra] of mine, which is endowed with great compassion.
They would speak of the first production of the thought of awakening, the array of qualities of the Buddha-field, and the preliminary application of their vows;
and those sons of good family or daughters of good family seeking awakening would be filled with wonder, they would possess noble resolve,
and they too would generate such great compassion for sentient beings and make such a vow.

In such a Buddha-field characterized by the intense fivefold corruption and the corruption of afflictions during this Kali age, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, shall accept as their disciples those who have committed the immediate transgressions and even those who have accumulated all manner of unwholesome deeds;

and those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, endowed with great compassion and seeking enlightenment, shall grant prophecies to those sons of good family or daughters of good family who desire awakening, using such a prophecy as accords with the aspirations of those sons of good family.
Or, by daughters of noble family who have made a vow during this degenerate age of the five turbidities and intense afflictions,

other Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, may— through the accounts of my past lives and former connections— expound in detail for the sake of sentient beings, sons of noble family, or daughters of noble family who seek awakening:
"In such a long time, there was a sun-like Victor (Jina) of such a name;..."

Even after his final nirvana, for the sake of suffering beings of such a kind over such a long period of time, he performed various miracles and diverse transformations of many sorts through his bodily manifestations; by means of those bodily transformations,
we were first inspired toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

“Because we have accumulated roots of merit for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, from the first production of the thought of awakening onwards, this exertion in the perfections has been undertaken,” [he said],

as was previously described in detail. Then, indeed, the brahmin Samudrareṇu, the chief priest, in the presence of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha and before the assembly of beings consisting of gods, gandharvas, and humans, [spoke] this [vow] endowed with great compassion.

He made five hundred vows and spoke thus: "If, O Venerable Blessed One, such a wish of mine should be fulfilled, then in a future time, during the Bhadraka Kalpa, while the age of intense afflictions, the turbidity of strife, and the Kali Yuga prevails, and when the world is blind and without a leader— "

"In this world cast into the darkness of the calamity of wrong views, for those who commit the deeds of immediate retribution— and as previously stated— if I am capable of accomplishing this entire work of a Buddha exactly as my vow was made,
and if I do not turn back from my vow for enlightenment,"
Nor do I dedicate my roots of merit toward any other field;
even so, O Venerable Blessed One, I apply my resolve.
Furthermore, by means of these roots of merit, I do not pray for the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas.
I do not seek the vehicle of the śrāvakas,
nor do I seek the sovereignty of gods and humans in the world of gods and men,
nor do I seek the lordship of gods and humans in the world of gods and men.
It is not for the sake of enjoying the five strands of sensual pleasure that I pray for rebirth as a god, nor do I pray for rebirth among the gandharvas, asuras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, nāgas, or garuḍas.
And I do not dedicate the roots of merit here.

For the Blessed One has said thus: "Generosity leads to great wealth; ethical discipline leads to rebirth in heaven; learning leads to great wisdom; and cultivation leads to dissociation from bondage."
And this was further stated by the Blessed One:
"The intention and resolve of a meritorious being succeed through the dedication of roots of virtue.
And whatever merit, O Venerable Blessed One, I may have acquired—whether consisting of giving, or morality, or learning, or cultivation—[may it be dedicated].
If such a hope as this is not fulfilled according to the vow I have made, then I dedicate all these roots of merit to the beings in the hells:
may those beings who experience sufferings in the fierce, terrible, and most horrific Avīci hell emerge from there by means of this root of merit,
and may they obtain rebirth as humans here in this buddhafield.
May they attain the Dharma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata and attain parinirvāṇa in the state of excellence.
And whatever karmic fruit of those beings remains unexhausted, may I, having passed away at this time, be reborn in the Avīci Great Hell.
May bodies of mine, as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, appear through the attainment of meditative absorptions;
and may each individual body of mine become vast, equal in size to Sumeru, the king of mountains.
And may each individual body of mine... [KpSū 272]
May I recognize such extremely painful sensations as this single body now experiences;
and may each and every one of my own bodies undergo intense, fierce, harsh, and hellish tortures for as long as there are atoms in a Buddha-field—
just as these beings in other worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, are undergoing them now.

In all world-systems, there may be sentient beings who have committed acts of immediate retribution (*ānantarya*)— deeds that lead ultimately to the Avīci hell— and who, throughout great eons as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, having gone to other buddha-fields in the ten directions as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, might commit or give rise to such acts of immediate retribution.
For the sake of all beings, may I alone remain and experience that karma in the great Avīci hell, so that no beings may be reborn in the hells,
and may all those beings please the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
If they could deliver them from saṃsāra and cause them to enter the city of nirvāṇa,
then I would be liberated from this hell after a long time.

Furthermore, in as many other Buddha-fields in the ten directions as there are atoms in a Buddha-field, if beings were to initiate such karma, be projected by it, and be destined for rebirth in the Pratāpana hell— as previously described— [the Tathāgata would know it].
Thus it is in Saṃtāpana, Mahāraurava, Saṃghāta, Kālasūtra, and Saṃjīvana; likewise, the various kinds of animal births are to be described,
and likewise it is to be told regarding the world of Yama.
In the same way, it should be said regarding the *yakṣas* and *dāridras*; likewise, the *kumbhāṇḍas*, *piśācas*, *asuras*, and *garuḍas* are to be addressed.
When beings in other world-systems in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field, have projected such karma, [the result follows].

And those humans who are blind, deaf, tongueless, handless, or footless— by whom [the offenses] must be committed with minds that have lost their mindfulness, and by whom impure things must be consumed—
the full account being as previously stated—
may I again be reborn thus in the great Avīci hell.

For as long as they continue to grasp at the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases within saṃsāra, for that long may I likewise undergo such various sufferings of rebirth among hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, yakṣas, asuras, rākṣasas, and even humans,
exactly as previously described; provided that my aspiration for this kind of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening is not fulfilled.
Furthermore, may my aspiration for such unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment—as previously described—be fulfilled;
may the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, be my witnesses!
May those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside, maintain themselves, and teach the Dharma in immeasurable and incalculable other world-systems in the ten directions, be my Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
They will become witnesses;
they will become embodiments of knowledge.
“Venerable Blessed One, may you grant me a prophecy regarding my attainment of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

May I become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, and so forth, up to a Buddha, a Blessed One, during the auspicious aeon when the lifespan of beings is one hundred and twenty years.
I am capable of accomplishing such a work of a Buddha as I have pledged.”

Then, at that very moment, the entire assembly—including the world of gods, gandharvas, humans, and asuras—whether situated on the earth or in the sky, with the exception of the Tathāgata himself, all shed tears; they prostrated at his feet with the five-pointed salutation and said:
"Excellent, excellent, O Great Compassionate One!"
Your mindfulness is profound, and great compassion has arisen for beings who are themselves profound;
you have made a profound great vow.

Therefore, with that resolute intention, all beings—those who have committed the immediate transgressions up to those who have fallen into the accumulation of unwholesome roots—have been embraced as disciples, being completely covered by your great compassion.

By this vow it is known that, from the first production of the thought of awakening, you have become a medicine for sentient beings, their protection and their refuge; since you have made this vow for the sake of liberating sentient beings from suffering, may your aspiration be fulfilled, and may the Blessed One grant you the prophecy of unexcelled, perfect awakening.”
And King Amṛtaśuddha himself, weeping, prostrated at the feet of the brahmin with the fivefold salutation and said:
"Aho! You are supremely profound and unattached to pleasures;
you have compassion for sentient beings; you are our guide."
[The passage continues as follows: Avalokiteśvara said:
"While beings are attached, you are unattached; while they are limited by the senses, you transcend the objects of the senses.
You exercise mastery over the senses here, and you shall speak the *dhāraṇī*, the treasury of knowledge."
... [and so on] ... Mahāsthāmaprāpta said:
"We have assembled for the sake of the virtue of many thousands of millions of beings."
O Compassionate One, you weep; this is a most supreme and difficult feat.
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī said:
"O you who possess firm vigor and meditative concentration, and are discerning through supreme wisdom,
you deserve worship from us with garlands, perfumes, and ointments."
The Bodhisattva Gaganamudra said:
"In this way you have bestowed a gift upon sentient beings; it is a great compassion.
In this degenerate age, O Protector, you shall become one endowed with the excellent marks."
(KpSū 277) The Bodhisattva Vajracchedaprajñāvabhāsa also spoke thus:
“Just as space is exceedingly vast, so too are you the locus of compassion.”
By you, this path of the conduct of awakening has been shown to sentient beings.”
The Bodhisattva Vegavairocana said:
"There are no others who possess such compassion for sentient beings as you, O Tathāgata,
you who are endowed with all virtues and are discerning through supreme wisdom."
Siṃhagandha said:
"In the future time, during the age of the Māra of the afflictions, when it is auspicious..."
You shall attain glory and renown; liberate sentient beings who are suffering.
The Bodhisattva Samantabhadra said:
"They are intent upon the wilderness of birth, trapped in the peril of false refuges;
their mental continuums are seized and scorched, and they feed upon flesh and blood."
Akṣobhya said:
"Cast into the eggshell of ignorance, arisen in the mire of afflictions, their mental continuums are seized and scorched."
“those who commit the immediate transgressions.”
Gandhahasta also said:
"Having seen the future peril as if in the circle of a mirror,
you have seized those whose mental continuums are scorched, who reject the true Dharma."
Ratnaketu also said: "Those who possess knowledge, ethical discipline, and meditative concentration, and are adorned with love and compassion—
those who revile such noble ones have seized and burned their own mental continuums."
(Vigatabhaya-saṃtāpa said:
"Having seen the suffering of sentient beings upon the path leading to the three lower realms, you..."
Having grasped [these things], their mental continuums are burned; they have resorted to a hollow fist.
Utpalahasta also said:

"Through compassion, wisdom, and vigor, you have subdued this assembly; those whose mental continuums are consumed by afflictions and who are tormented by birth and death have been taken up [by you]."
Jñānakīrti said: "Those afflicted by many diseases, impelled by the winds of the afflictions—
quench them with the water of wisdom."
"You crush the army of Māra."
Dharaṇīmudra also said:
"Our vigor was not firm enough for the liberation from the exhausted afflictions,
such that you, like the heroic sun, utterly crush the net of afflictions."
Utpalacandra also said:
"O you who possess firm vigor and exertion, and who rely upon virtue and compassion,
you shall liberate the three worlds bound by the fetters of existence."
Vimalendra said:
"O Mahākāruṇika, you have pointed out the sphere of activity of the bodhisattvas."
For we pay homage to you, having arisen from the cause of compassion.”
Balavegadhārī also said:
"In this degenerate age (kaliyuga) characterized by the conjunction of afflictions (kleśa), you have taken recourse to that awakening;
cut away the afflictions along with their roots, and your firm vow will be fulfilled."
Jyotipāla also said: “A stainless vow, equal to a treasury of knowledge, has been made.
(KpSū 283)
You abide in the conduct of awakening; you are the medicinal herb for sentient beings and their refuge.”

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Balasandarśana, weeping, prostrated at the feet of the brahmin with his five limbs, joined his palms in reverence, and said: "O lamp of wisdom, you who dispel the disease of the afflictions for sentient beings! Compassionate one, having kindled it, you liberate suffering beings."

And, noble son, that entire assembly—including gods, gandharvas, humans, and brahmins—having bowed at the feet of the brahmin with the five-fold prostration (pañca-maṇḍala), stood with palms joined in reverence; having praised him with various verses endowed with logical sequences and meaningful words, they remained there.
(KpSū 284) And when, noble son, the brahmin Samudrareṇu placed his right knee upon the ground before the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha,
at that very moment a great earthquake occurred throughout the ten directions, in as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms of dust.

In the Buddha-fields, the earth shook, trembled, and quaked; it stirred, was agitated, and was thoroughly shaken; it quivered, vibrated, and was intensely convulsed; it rattled, resounded, and reverberated.
Furthermore, a great radiance appeared.
And a rain of various flowers fell, such as the *māndārava* and *mahāmāndārava*, up to those of infinite radiance; such was the rain of flowers that fell.

It rained down upon the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside, stay, and maintain themselves in world-systems throughout the ten directions as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field—whether in pure or impure Buddha-fields—teaching the Dharma to sentient beings.
And those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who were seated there in the presence of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to hear the Dharma—
those bodhisattva mahāsattvas, having seen that earthquake, again questioned those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
“Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition for the manifestation in the world of this great earthquake and this great rain of falling flowers?”
Furthermore, at that time, in the eastern direction, beyond as many buddha-fields from this buddha-field as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River,
there is a world-system named Ratnavicaya. In that buddha-field, Ratnavicaya, there dwells and remains a Tathāgata,
Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Blessed One named Ratnacandra, who provides sustenance for immeasurable beings.
Surrounded and attended by incalculable bodhisattvas, he was teaching the Dharma—namely, discourses on the Mahāyāna—in that buddha-field.
In that buddha-field, there were two bodhisattva mahāsattvas named Ratnaketu and Candraketu;
those two bodhisattvas, having extended their joined palms in reverence toward the Tathāgata Ratnacandra, [addressed] Ratnacandra...

They said this to the Tathāgata: “Venerable Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition for the appearance of such a great earthquake in the world and for the raining down of such a great shower of flowers?

The Tathāgata Ratnacandra replied: “Noble son, in the western direction, beyond as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River from this Buddha-field, there is a world-system named Santīraṇa.”
There is a world-system; therein, in the Buddha-field Santīraṇa,
the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha— down to being a Buddha, a Blessed One— dwells, maintains himself, and bestows prophecies of unexcelled [enlightenment] upon many millions of bodhisattvas.
He was preaching the Dharma discourse titled "The Array of the Dhāraṇī Gateway of the Samādhi Array of the Vow that Manifests the Domain of Bodhisattvas for Perfect Enlightenment.
And therein, one bodhisattva mahāsattva, a Greatly Compassionate One, had made such a vow, being fully permeated by great compassion.
Speech was uttered concerning the prediction of the bodhisattvas to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; such vows were proclaimed that many millions of beings made the aspiration for enlightenment,
and they took hold of the magnificent arrays of qualities of buddha-fields as well as the beings to be trained.

And in every respect, he alone is the Great Bodhisattva endowed with great compassion, who, having surpassed that entire assembly, has taken as his disciples those to be trained— even those whose mental continuums are scorched, who have committed all the acts of immediate retribution, and who are caught up in the accumulation of all roots of unwholesomeness— within this Buddha-field, which is afflicted by the five corruptions and the strife of the age of defilements.
And that entire assembly, including the world with its gods, gandharvas, humans, and asuras, setting aside that Tathāgata Ratnagarbha,
became intent upon making offerings to that Mahākāruṇika, the last [Tathāgata]; having prostrated with the five-fold salutation and standing with palms joined, they spoke his praises.
And that Great Being sat before the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha, listening for his prophecy.
When that Great Being placed his right knee upon the ground before the Blessed One,
the Blessed One then manifested a smile such that it reached as far as Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms of dust in the ten directions.
The world-systems trembled and a rain of flowers fell;
and in all those buddha-fields, for the purpose of awakening them and to demonstrate the practice of the vows of the Bodhisattvas of Great Compassion,
those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas [arrived] from buddha-fields in the ten directions as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field.

“Those Tathāgatas displayed such miracles for the purpose of assembling the Bodhisattvas and Mahāsattvas, and for the purpose of speaking this Dharma-discourse on the gateways of meditative concentration, conduct, and fearlessness.
And those two sons of good family, O son of good family, questioned that Tathāgata Ratnacandra.”

"Venerable Blessed One, for how long has that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākāruṇika generated the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*)? For how long has he practiced the conduct of awakening (*bodhicaryā*), such that he appears at this time when the world is characterized by the five corruptions (*pañcakaṣāya*), amidst the fierce afflictions of the current age of strife (*kaliyuga*)?"

“Have those beings who have committed the immediate transgressions, even those who have reached the point of accumulating all unwholesome roots and whose mental continuums are scorched, been taken as disciples and accepted by him?
The Tathāgata Ratnacandra said: “Noble son, that Greatly Compassionate One has now first resolved his mind toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
Go, noble son, to that buddha-field Santīraṇa to see, pay homage to, and attend upon that Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One, Ratnagarbha.”
And you shall hear that Dharma discourse on the confidence in conduct, which is an exposition through the gateway of meditative concentration;
and you should ask that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahākāruṇika on my behalf, and speak thus:
“The Tathāgata Ratnacandra asks after you, O noble man; he has sent this flower, the stainless Candrarocavimala,
and has bestowed upon you his word of approval.”
