Then, for seven days, he performed worship with immeasurable and incalculable musical instruments, flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, parasols, banners, flags, and jewels;
furthermore, there he inspired, introduced, and established immeasurable and incalculable beings in the three vehicles.
At the conclusion of those seven days, he went forth together with eighty-four thousand living beings.

Having shaved off his hair and beard and donned saffron robes, he went forth from the home to the homeless life with perfect faith and kindled the teaching of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha after his parinirvāṇa;
for ten thousand years, he [upheld it].
He became a bearer of the true Dharma;
and there he exhorted, established, and settled immeasurable and incalculable beings in the three vehicles,
and he established them in the going for refuge to the Three Jewels.
They were established and settled in the lay follower’s vow, the novice monk’s vow, the full ordination, the state of a bhikṣu, and the vow of living the holy life.

Having directed many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings toward skill in the supernormal powers and miraculous transformations, and having directed them toward gentleness and the practice of the holy life, he directed them toward the thorough understanding of the aggregates that act as enemies, and toward the thorough understanding of the sense-bases as empty villages.
Having directed them toward the thorough knowledge of conditioned phenomena through the wisdom of the conditioned,

and having shown all phenomena to be like a reflection, like a mirage, and like the moon in water, he demonstrated the thorough knowledge of cessation— cessation that is without arising, without rebirth, peaceful, thoroughly pacified, stilled, supreme, sublime, and nirvāṇa—
and established them in the Noble Eightfold Path before passing away.

And in this very way, those beings performed the worship of the body for the body of that Greatly Compassionate One, the Great Śramaṇa, just as the worship of the body is performed for the body of a universal monarch (cakravartin).
In that same manner, at that time, those beings performed the worship of the body for the body of the Greatly Compassionate One, the Great Śramaṇa.
On the very day that the Great Compassionate One,

the Great Śramaṇa, passed away, on that same day the True Dharma of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha vanished, and those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, by the power of their vows, took rebirth in other world-systems.
Some were reborn in the Tuṣita heaven by the power of their vows;
some among humans, some among nāgas, some among asuras, and some were reborn in various animal wombs through the force of their vows.

And when the Great Śramaṇa Mahākāruṇika had passed away, noble son, by the power of his vow, he appeared in the southern direction, ten Buddha-fields beyond this Buddha-field, in a world-system named Saṃkarṣaṇa. There, the human lifespan was eighty years; the people were possessed of roots of unwholesomeness, fierce, blood-handed, intent on evil, and devoid of compassion.
Among all sentient beings, there were those who did not recognize their mothers or fathers and who saw no fear in the world beyond.
By the power of his vow, the Great Compassionate One, the Great Śramaṇa, was reborn in that Buddha-field of Saṃkarṣaṇa within a family of outcastes (caṇḍāla).
He possessed an exceedingly tall body; he was exceedingly strong, exceedingly swift, exceedingly mindful, exceedingly eloquent, and endowed with exceeding speed.
With firm strength and power, he gathered the beings together and said: "O beings, if you would desist from taking what is not given,
from sexual misconduct, and so forth, up to wrong view;..."
"Therefore, I shall grant you your lives and provide you with the necessities for living;
however, if you do not desist, I shall deprive you of your lives and depart."
Then those beings, having raised their joined palms, said:
"From this day forward, for as long as we live, we shall desist from taking what is not given, up to and including wrong view, according to the word of you, our protector.
That powerful Caṇḍāla went and informed the king or the king’s officers.

“I have need of the requisites for life—food, drink, solid food, soft food, or beverages; clothing, bedding, perfumes, gold, bullion, jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, silver, and refined gold.
Give me abundant requisites for life!
That powerful Caṇḍāla established those beings in the ten paths of wholesome action for as long as they lived.
Thereupon, those humans came to have a lifespan of five hundred years.
The king who was there passed away; then, by those royal ministers, that outcaste Balacaṇḍāla was consecrated with the royal inauguration and established in the kingdom, being named Puṇyabala.
Then, noble son, King Puṇyabala did not long remain before he ruled over that realm.
With firm vigor and prowess, he governed the second realm;
before long, King Puṇyabala became a powerful universal monarch (*balacakravartin*) over the entire Jambūdvīpa.

And when the king, through the power of his merit, had assumed sovereignty over the entire Jambudvīpa, he thereafter exhorted, introduced, and established sentient beings in the abstention from taking life; likewise, he exhorted them in the abstention from taking what is not given, up to the abstention from wrong view, and established them in right view.
Furthermore, according to their inclinations, he exhorted, introduced, and established sentient beings in the three vehicles.

Then King Puṇyabala, having established all the beings of Jambudvīpa in the ten paths of wholesome action and having directed them toward the three vehicles, caused a proclamation to be heard throughout the whole of Jambudvīpa:
"Whatever supplicants there may be, whether seeking food or even seeking jewels, let them all come;
I shall give all gifts."
Then, at a later time, all the beings of Jambudvīpa came and requested King Puṇyabala [for his kingdom];
King Puṇyabala, for their sake, gave various kinds of gifts.
There, an Ājīvika named Pāṃśughoṣa approached King Puṇyabala and said:
“If you, Great King, renounce various great gifts and sacrifices, and if you, Great King, desire unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
then you shall fulfill my wish.”
“You shall become, O Great King, a Jina, a lamp for the world.
The king asked, “What is your purpose?
The Ājīvika Pāṃśughoṣa replied, “Great King, I desire the state of a Vidyādhara; I wish to accomplish the rite known as ‘The Subduer of the Great Asura Armies.’”
"Therefore, standing before you, I entreat you: there is need for the skin of a living man, and there is need for his eyes.
Then, noble son, King Puṇyabala thought to himself:
"I have obtained the sovereignty of a wheel-turning king of power."
"Countless beings have been established in the ten paths of wholesome action and directed toward the three vehicles,
and immeasurable gifts have been given by me; and from this essence-less body, I am now extracting its essence— this is my spiritual friend."
The king said: "Be satisfied; I give you this ordinary eye of flesh, so that by it I may obtain the unsurpassed Dharma-eye.
With a serene mind, I give you this skin of my own, and by that I shall attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment."
Then, noble son, King Puṇyabala plucked out both his eyes with his right hand and gave them to the Ājīvika. With his face smeared with blood, he said:

"Listen to me here, O gods, yakṣas, and those of great supernatural power; whatever men, asuras, or spirits have come here—whether men who dwell in the sky or those who stand upon the earth—I have directed this auspicious gift toward awakening; may I attain the state of peace."
"I would deliver sentient beings from the terrible ocean of saṃsāra and establish them on the further shore in supreme, auspicious nirvāṇa.
He spoke again: (KpSū 352)
“If I am to attain unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, may my life-faculty not cease for as long as it takes, may my mindfulness not perish, and may no remorse arise in me,
until that spell of this Ājīvika has been mastered.”
He said, "Take the skin.
Then that son of good family, the scavenger Pāṃśughoṣa, took a sharp weapon and, having removed the skin from the body of King Dhriyamāṇa, took the skin and accomplished the mantra;
thus, for seven days, the life-faculty of King Puṇyabala was not extinguished.
His mindfulness was not lost,
he did not experience that painful sensation,
and not even for a single moment did regret arise within him.
What do you think, noble sons? That one who at that time, on that occasion, was named Mahākāruṇika—should he be seen as anyone else?
You should not see him so; for at that time, on that occasion, I myself was named Mahākāruṇika, the father of the Tathāgata Ratnagarbha.
This was my first production of the thought of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
And by my first production of the thought of enlightenment, I inspired beings beyond measure to attain unexcelled, perfect awakening;
this was my first heroic state and heroic deed.
By the power of my vow, having passed away from there, I was reborn in the Saṃkarṣaṇa buddha-field in a family of outcastes; this was my second heroic state and heroic deed.

Then, while remaining within the lineage of the Caṇḍālas, having established sentient beings in wholesome states through my own strength and prowess, I attained the status of a Wheel-Turning King of Power;
and throughout the entire Jambudvīpa, the defilements, strife, and quarrels of the Kali age were pacified.
And my lifespan was increased;
this was my first renunciation of self,
when I gave away my own eyes and renounced my own skin.
Having passed away from there, by the power of my previous vow, I was reborn in that very same field of Saṃkarṣaṇa on the second continent within a family of Caṇḍālas.
[The rest follows as before: And there, having directed sentient beings toward wholesome deeds through such firm vigor and prowess, I attained the status of a Wheel-turning King of Power.
And there, the impurities of the Kali age, as well as strife, enmity, and conflict, were pacified,
and the lifespan was increased;
and there, from his own body, he gave away his tongue and both ears.
Thus, throughout that entire Mahāsāhasra world-system of Saṃkarṣaṇa, in all its continents, such manly effort was exerted.

By means of the continuous power of firm vigor and resolve through his vows, and by the force of those vows, in as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā— each being a field of five corruptions— he performed such great manly deeds and established sentient beings in wholesome qualities.
They have been encouraged to take up the three vehicles,

and the defilements of the Kali age, as well as quarrels, strife, and conflicts, have been pacified. For this reason, O sons of good family, the buddha-fields of those other Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are completely pure.

When those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, while formerly practicing the conduct for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, did not reproach others for their transgressions, nor did they instill fear in others, nor did they encourage beings toward the vehicle of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
For this purpose, the buddha-fields of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, whose intentions are fulfilled, become completely pure; and in that buddha-field, there is no such thing as an offense,
nor any taking up of training rules.
Neither harsh speech nor unwholesome sounds are heard; rather, that buddha-field is filled with the sound of the Dharma, free from any unpleasant sound.
And therein, sentient beings are able to act according to their desires;
furthermore, there is no appearance of even the name or designation of the vehicles of the Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas.
And when, throughout great eons as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, during as many empty world-systems of the five corruptions as there are sands in the Ganges River, by me—

In various Buddha-fields, out of fear of harsh speech, beings were encouraged to abstain from taking life, and so on, until they were encouraged, introduced, and established in the three vehicles. By the remainder of that karma, my Buddha-field is now thus afflicted, filled with the sound of unwholesomeness, and populated by beings who have come together in a state of unwholesome roots.
I teach the Dharma by means of the three vehicles;
and just as I previously made my vow, so have I taken hold of such a buddha-field,
and with exactly such strength, vigor, and exertion as those beings whom I have taken hold of as disciples to be trained, I have practiced the conduct of awakening.
Just as the seed was sown, so has this Buddha-field been obtained;
it is exactly according to the form of the vow I made.
Briefly, noble son, I shall describe to you the perfection of generosity—how the relinquishment of gifts was practiced by me while I was engaged in the conduct of a bodhisattva.
Never before has such a gift been relinquished by any bodhisattva,
nor will there ever be any bodhisattva who, while practicing the conduct of awakening, relinquishes such a gift as I have relinquished while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva.
Elsewhere there were eight virtuous persons (*satpuruṣa*).
There was a virtuous person named Dharaṇidatta in the southern direction. (KpSū 356)

In the world-system Sarvaghoṣā, he has attained unexcelled, perfect enlightenment as the Tathāgata named Saṃkaramardārciḥ; while the lifespan of beings is one hundred years, he teaches the Dharma, and on the seventh day he will enter parinirvāṇa.
Thus, there was a bodhisattva named Vīryasaṃcodana.
In the eastern direction, in the world-system Ajavati, he fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment;
when the lifespan of beings was one hundred years, he performed the work of a Buddha for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges.
When that Tathāgata had passed away into unsurpassed final nirvāṇa,
Even today, the physical remains of that Greatly Compassionate One continue to perform the work of a Buddha in empty Buddha-fields amidst the five corruptions.
And thus they say: "The Bodhisattva Sārakusumita, possessing firm vigor and meditative concentration, practices the conduct of a Bodhisattva through the renunciation of power and speed.
After the passing of as many great eons as there are grains of sand in ten Ganges rivers, he will then appear in that northern direction as Sahetusaṃkarṣaṇa."

In a buddha-field characterized by the five corruptions, that virtuous man will attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; he will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and so forth, up to Buddha, Blessed One, named Sahetukṛṣṇavidhvaṃsanarāja (King Who Destroys Blackness Along with Its Cause),
who has crushed the wicked with the flame of wisdom.

The Bodhisattva Satpuruṣa, after the passing of one great eon, will— in the western direction, during a world-system named Bhairavatī, amidst a population with a lifespan of one hundred years in an age of five corruptions— awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
he will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and Blessed One named Sūryagarbhārcivimalendra.

Furthermore, after incalculable eons had passed, this Saṃrocana— in the world-system called Kṣāravarcanikuñjitā in the upper direction, during the eon of the five corruptions characterized by intense defilement and agitation— by virtue of his former vow,
[attained] unsurpassed [enlightenment] there in that Buddha-field, Kṣāravarcanikuñjitā, among beings whose lifespan was fifty years.
He will realize perfect enlightenment and become a Tathāgata named Acintyarocana, a Buddha, a Blessed One.
By virtue of his previous vow, he will perform the entirety of the Buddha-work for ten years and then enter final nirvana.
On that very day, the true Dharma of that Tathāgata will disappear,
and for ten years that buddha-field will remain empty.
Thereafter, that Bodhisattva Prahasitabāhu will attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in that buddha-field which has been transformed by the salt-water marshes.
There shall be a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Vairocanadharma.
He too, having performed the entirety of the Buddha-work for ten years, will pass into final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder.
And after he has passed away, the True Dharma will remain for seven years by virtue of his former vow.

There, two noble beings who had previously received their prophecy and had tasted the flavor of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One in his presence; then, with joy, gladness, and rapture, they rose into the air to the height of seven palm trees,
stood with palms joined, and addressed the Blessed One in a single voice with these verses:
“O Buddha, you shine just like the sun risen over Mount Meru in this world;
O pure-eyed, stainless Guide, you who have become the light—O Sugata, homage be to you!”
"Through many eons, cultivating vigor while seeking supreme enlightenment,
you have honored many Jinas in the past; yet those leaders of the past did not grant you a prophecy."
With passion abandoned and minds fully liberated, you have accomplished what was to be done here in all the world;
you teach the Dharma to those who have lost their way and deliver sentient beings from the ocean of existence.
Having ourselves gone forth in the teaching of the Self-Existent One, we shall train in the Prātimokṣa discipline taught by the Victor;
having trained with our faculties composed, may we always remain in close proximity to you alone.
“Independent, desiring the activity of life, having understood the Teacher and heard the Dharma,
I shall obtain the taste of the stage of consecration. Thus did the Jina declare this very meaning.
The Blessed One said: "Noble son, those two had not yet generated the thought of awakening;
and these four—Saṃrocana, Prahasitabāhu, Dharaṇidatta, Vīryasaṃcodana, Sārakusumita, and Prajñārciḥsaṃkopitadaṃṣṭra."
Listen to how these six virtuous men were first inspired by me toward awakening.
Long ago, noble son, in the past, after incalculable and immeasurable eons had passed,
at that time and in that age, this buddha-field was named Arajamerujugupsita.

At that time, O son of good family, while a great eon was proceeding and when the lifespan of beings was one hundred years, during the period of the counterfeit True Dharma under the teaching of the Tathāgata Gandhapadma, I myself, at that time, was a powerful universal monarch named Durdhana, a conqueror of Jambudvīpa who had a thousand sons;
I also inspired them all toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

At another time, they also went forth and entered the religious life under the teaching of the Tathāgata Gandhapadma; they caused the teaching of the Tathāgata Gandhapadma to flourish even more extensively, with the exception of six sons who did not go forth and did not wish to generate the thought of awakening.
And I, moreover, entreated them again and again.
“What is your intention, that you neither generate the thought of awakening nor go forth into homelessness?
They replied:
“We do not go forth.
For what reason?
Because one who has gone forth during the final age of destruction, when that which resembles the true Dharma prevails, is unable to fulfill the entire aggregate of ethical discipline.”
He is devoid of the seven riches and submerged in the mire of saṃsāra; yet,
he may at some time obtain the glory of gods and humans.
"He wanders constantly through the three lower realms and does not abide by undertaking the training of a Buddha;
for this reason, we do not go forth [into homelessness]."
I asked them again:
"Why then do you not generate the mind set on awakening?
They replied: "Even if one were to give us the entirety of Jambūdvīpa..."
“May we generate the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Having heard this, noble son, my mind was filled with supreme joy, and I thought:
“I have established all the people of Jambudvīpa in the taking of the three refuges;”
They have been encouraged to observe the noble eightfold fast and established in the three vehicles.
What if I were now to divide this Jambudvīpa into six parts and give them to my six sons;
having given it, I would then encourage them toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?
"And I shall go forth and renounce the world.
Thus, having divided all of Jambudvīpa into six parts, he gave them to his sons.

I, having gone forth and renounced the world, and those six kings of Jambudvīpa became mutually antagonistic, falling into various calamities such as quarrels, disputes, strife, disease, foreign invasions, and civil unrest.
Since a famine has arisen throughout the entire Jambudvīpa,
young grass does not grow,
and rain does not fall.
Leaves, flowers, and fruits do not grow from the trees;
medicinal herbs and grasses do not flourish;
and even the beasts and birds are tormented, their bodies set ablaze by hunger and thirst.
Then I think thus:
"At this time, I must perform the sacrifice of my own self, and I must satisfy sentient beings with my own flesh and blood."
“Then, having abandoned my hermitage and gone to the Middle Countries, I ascended Mount Darpapāla and made this vow:
‘Just as I renounce my own body and life for the sake of compassion, and not for the sake of heaven or wealth— ’”
For the world together with its devas, it would have a height here equal to a mountain.
Just as I renounce this perfection of beloved form— not for the sake of Śakra, Brahmā, or Māra—
so that you may accomplish your purpose in the world of the gods, let my flesh and blood abound.
"May the nāgas, humans, gods, and yakṣas, and whatever deities dwell upon this mountain, listen!
Out of compassion that has arisen for the sake of sentient beings, I shall satisfy all beings with my own flesh and blood."
And when I made my vow,
the three worlds were shaken.
The earth trembled, Mount Meru shook,
and the hosts of gods wept; thereupon, I threw myself down from Mount Dagapāla.
By the power of my vow, my body became as large as a mountain, a hundred yojanas in width and one yojana in height;
even humans, deer, and birds began to devour my flesh and blood.
And, noble son, as that body of mine is being consumed by sentient beings, it increases day by day; it has become a hundred thousand yojanas in width and a thousand yojanas in height.
Everywhere, human heads have appeared, complete with hair, ears, eyes, noses, lips, and teeth, along with tongues—many hundreds of thousands of faces having manifested.
And those mouths proclaim with human voices:
"O beings, O take what you need; eat this flesh!"
Drink the blood!
Seize the eyes!
Seize the ears, nose, hair, lips, teeth, and tongues!
For whatever purpose, by whatever means, and to whatever extent you have satisfied your bodies and fulfilled your intentions, generate the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment—
whether by the vehicle of the disciples or the vehicle of the solitary buddhas.
This enjoyment and utilization of yours shall never be exhausted.
"And you shall have no offerings made out of faith;
let there not be a swift end to your lives.
And those wise beings there, some of them conceived the aspiration for the Śrāvaka vehicle.
Some generate the mind for the vehicle of the Pratyekabuddhas, some generate the mind for unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, and some generate the minds for rebirth among gods and humans.
They devour flesh, drink blood,
and some seize out the eyes.
Some [cut off] the ears, some the nose, and some the lips.
Some seize those who have been tamed;
having seized them, they depart;
and by the power of their vows, they manifest before one another.
His flesh neither diminished nor was it exhausted;
for ten thousand years, he satisfied all the humans of Jambudvīpa, as well as the yakṣas, deer, and birds, with his own body.
And during those ten thousand years, I have given away eyes equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges;
I have given away blood equal in measure to the waters of the four oceans;
and I have given away flesh equal in measure to Mount Sumeru a thousand times over.

Tongues as large as the Cakravāḍa mountains were sacrificed by me; ears as large as the Yugandhara and Meru mountains were sacrificed by me; and noses as large as the Vipula and Sumeru mountains were sacrificed by me.
Bodily parts as large as this Vulture Peak Mountain have been sacrificed by me;
my own skin was sacrificed there, covering the entire Sahā Buddha-field to the extent that it could be measured.
Behold, son of good family, for ten thousand years I have thus sacrificed my own body—immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite times over—in exchange for a single life;
likewise, immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite beings have been fully satisfied by me;
yet not even for a single moment of thought has regret ever arisen in me.
And thus I made this vow there:
"If I shall awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, may this hope of mine be fulfilled."
Just as all sentient beings were satisfied by my own body on a single continent,

even so, for thousands of years equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, such a physical form of mine appeared on every continent within this Buddha-field— which is loathsome like a mountain of dust and Meru. Just as for ten thousand years on one continent, so too on all continents, having satisfied sentient beings with my own flesh, blood, skin, eyes, ears, nose, lips, tongue, and hair, I would cause them to be established in the three vehicles.

May I satisfy all humans, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and those belonging to any of the animal realms— whosoever subsist on food consisting of flesh and blood, including various yakṣas down to even the inhabitants of the world of Yama. And just as I would satisfy all sentient beings with my own body within a single buddha-field,
may it be exactly so throughout the ten directions in as many worlds as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā.

In those various Buddha-fields, having attained such a physical form, may I satisfy sentient beings with my own flesh, blood, skin, eyes, and even my tongues— indeed, with my very body and life— for as many great eons as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges throughout those respective Buddha-fields.

May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who have set in motion the wheel of Dharma in other Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions and who currently abide, maintain themselves, and teach the Dharma, be deceived regarding me if I should not awaken to unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment; and while wandering in saṃsāra, may I never hear the word "Buddha," nor the word "Dharma," nor the word "Saṅgha."

May I never hear the word "perfection" (pāramitā), nor the word "overcoming the power of Māra," nor the word "fearlessness" (vaiśāradya), nor even the word "wholesome" (kuśala) within saṃsāra; may I instead be reborn eternally in the Avīci hell,
if such a sacrifice of my own body for the sake of satisfying sentient beings does not come to pass.
May this vow of mine not remain unfulfilled, just as my hope and intention have been conceived.
Furthermore, in every single continent throughout this entire buddha-field, may such bodily forms be sacrificed and sentient beings be satiated with my flesh and blood;
and likewise, in other buddha-fields in the ten directions as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, may sentient beings be satiated with my own flesh and blood through such bodily forms.

Behold, noble son, the Tathāgata’s perfection of generosity through the relinquishing of his own body: the eyes that were relinquished by me in continuous succession at that time would, if gathered together, form a heap as large as this Jambudvīpa, extending even up to the Trayastriṃśa heaven.
This, noble son, is the Tathāgata’s perfection of generosity through the relinquishing of himself, in brief.
Furthermore, noble son, after the passing of immeasurable eons from that time, this buddha-field became known as Candravidyuta; it too was characterized by the five corruptions (*pañcakaṣāya*).
And I, in this Jambudvīpa, was a powerful universal monarch (*cakravartin*) named Pradīpapradyota.
And thus I have established all the beings of Jambudvīpa in wholesome deeds,
just as previously described;
afterwards, I went out to the pleasure groves to see my own domain.
And there I saw a man; seeing him with his arms bound tightly behind his back as he was being led away for execution, I asked the ministers,
"What has this man done?"
The ministers said to me: "This man has committed an offense against Your Majesty;
whatever young grass and grain this man produces in a year, a sixth part of that must be given to Your Majesty."
"Just as other householders who dwell in the god's cities, villages, districts, and market towns give from their income, while those who earn their livelihood through manual labor also give;
yet this man does not give."
I said this to them: "Release this man;
do not seize anyone's wealth or grain by force.
They replied:
“Your Majesty, no one gives with a truly serene mind;

for the food, drink, and daily enjoyment of Your Majesty day by day, as well as the enjoyments and possessions of the queens, of Your Majesty’s harem, and of the sons and daughters— all that is extracted from others, yet no one gives with a serene heart.”
And with a deeply troubled mind, I reflected:
"To whom shall I give this entire Jambudvīpa and its royal sovereignty?
Having established my five hundred sons in the pursuit of awakening, I—
Having divided this Jambūdvīpa into five hundred portions, he gave them to his sons.
I, having gone to a forest of asceticism, practiced the holy life according to the renunciant way of the seers;

dwelling at the foot of an udumbara tree in a grove not far from the great southern ocean, subsisting on a diet of fresh roots and fruits, I lived as a meditator and gradually attained the five superknowledges.
Now at that time, five hundred merchants from Jambudvīpa had set out upon the great ocean, and they obtained there a vast heap of jewels.
Among them was a caravan leader named Candra;
by that fortunate and wise man, the *cintāmaṇi* jewel was obtained.

Having taken from that island of jewels a vast heap of precious wealth and that *cintāmaṇi* gem, he set out. Thereupon, the ocean was agitated, the *nāgas* were distressed and wept, and the deities dwelling there were troubled. However, a bodhisattva seer named Aśvasta had been reborn there by virtue of his former vow; by that Great Being, that caravan was brought safely and securely across the great ocean. And for that caravan leader, one of his—
A wicked Rākṣasa, an adversary seeking an opportunity and searching for a vulnerability, followed closely behind them.
For seven days, he unleashed an extremely foul wind and rain;
consequently, those merchants, having lost their way and being utterly terrified, cried out, wept, and lamented at the top of their voices.
They implored the gods, from Śiva and Varuṇa down to their own parents, crying out for their beloved sons;
until I heard them with my divine ear, and having gone there, I comforted the merchants,
saying, "I have arrived."
"Do not fear;
I shall show you the way as far as Jambūdvīpa."
"You shall attain [your goal] with well-being and safety.
Then, having smeared a cloth with oil, wrapped it around my own hand, and set it ablaze, I made this declaration of truth (*satyavacana*):
"If, for thirty-six years, while dwelling in the forest groves for the sake of sentient beings through the four Brahma-abodes (*brahmavihāra*), by me—"
For the benefit [of others], by means of a diet of fresh roots and fruits, the mental continuums of eighty-four thousand nāgas and yakṣas were ripened,
and they were established in non-retrogression regarding unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. By that truth, by that word of truth, and through the ripening of my roots of merit, may my hand blaze!
"May the merchants obtain the path; may they reach Jambudvīpa safely and in security.
Thus, for seven days and nights, he held his hand aflame until those merchants were established in Jambudvīpa, whereupon I made this aspiration:
When Jambudvīpa is bereft of jewels,
may this aspiration of mine be fulfilled at that time when I awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
May I become a caravan leader in Jambudvīpa, having brought the wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*) seven times and caused a rain of various excellent jewels to fall;

and likewise, throughout all the islands in this buddha-field, and even in as many empty buddha-fields in the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā— those afflicted by the five degenerations— may I cause a rain of jewels to fall, just as previously described.
And thus my aspiration was fulfilled: during great eons as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, I became caravan leaders;
and in empty Buddha-fields afflicted by the five corruptions, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, I rained down jewels;
on each and every continent, I rained down various showers of precious gems seven times over.
In this way, immeasurable and incalculable beings were made to have their intentions fulfilled by means of jewels and were established in the three vehicles.
Behold, noble son, the ripening of the roots of merit characterized by the Tathāgata’s relinquishment of jewels!
Furthermore, noble sons, after the passing of immeasurable eons, during the interval when this buddha-field was named Timira,
while the aeon of Contentment was in progress and the human lifespan was five thousand years within the five corruptions, I became by my own vow a brahmin named Sūryamālagandha in this Jambūdvīpa,
a reciter of the Vedas.
At that time, beings for the most part held views of eternalism; they were full of enmity, lacking in prowess, and possessed of the basis for quarreling.
To those beings, I teach the Dharma through the application of the aggregates as being like enemies, by means of my own great strength, speed, and prowess.

I demonstrate the mental engagement of mindfulness of breathing, which is connected to the conditions of the contemplation of the sense-bases as an empty village and is accompanied by arising and passing away.
They were dedicated to the generation of the thought of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and the dedication of their roots of merit, and I myself became possessed of the five superknowledges.
And at that time, through my instruction and admonition, immeasurable and incalculable beings came to possess the five superknowledges (*pañcābhijñā*).

Likewise, immeasurable and incalculable beings, having abandoned quarrels, strife, and enmity, took refuge in forest groves; subsisting on roots and fruits in those groves, they spent their days and nights meditating with the four divine abodes (*brahmavihāra*).
Then, as the eon was coming to an end, when the entire Jambudvīpa was filled with those worthy of offerings (*dakṣiṇīya*), [I appeared].
And those strifes, quarrels, hostilities, conflicts, and disputes were pacified; untimely winds and rains were stilled;
and the grasses supported by the earth became excellent and full of vitality.
They became afflicted by various diseases due to the defects of the eon.
At that time, I thought to myself: "If I am unable to pacify the illnesses of sentient beings..."
The thought occurred to me:
"What if I were to assemble Śakra, Mahābrahmā, the world-protectors, and other divine seers, or nāga seers, or Śakra-seers, or human seers?"
"I shall demonstrate the treatise on medicinal requisites for the benefit of sentient beings.
Then, having gone there by means of my supernatural power, I shall announce it to Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors, the celestial sages, the naga sages, the śakra-sages, and the human sages:
'There is a mountain named Ekaviḍapati.'"
Having gathered there at the place named Viḍacarakamūrdha, which is a refuge for warding off spirits and a treatise for clarifying the wind, bile, and phlegm, I shall teach the protective scripture.
[Pejāla] Thus, the pacification of the diseases of immeasurable and incalculable beings was accomplished.
Therein I made a great vow: "Just as on this single day I have provided the illumination of wisdom for immeasurable and incalculable beings,"
They have been established in the three vehicles,
the paths to the lower realms have been closed, and they have been set upon the path to heaven.
Various diseases were pacified and they were set free;
thus, the light of wisdom was bestowed upon immeasurable and incalculable beings, and they were established in happiness.
Therefore, noble son,
by the ripening of this root of merit, this hope of my vow has been fulfilled;
and on a single day, the paths to the states of woe for immeasurable and incalculable beings were brought to cessation by me.
And she was established upon the path to heaven;

for the sake of providing requisites for the sick, hosts of celestial ṛṣis and yakṣas were assembled; and for the benefit of sentient beings, the world of the gods atop Mount Viḍacara was revealed in this very same way throughout all the continents of the Timitra Buddha-field.
And such human effort was exerted that beings were established on the path to heaven,
and gods, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, and sages were assembled by whom various fields of knowledge were revealed for the sake of sentient beings.

Just as in the Buddha-field Timira, even so in the Buddha-fields of the ten directions— equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges— which are characterized by the five corruptions, such a heroic effort has been made,
and sentient beings have been established in the three vehicles and set upon the path to heaven.
Various fields of knowledge have been illuminated in the world,
beings afflicted by disease have been liberated,
and, O son of good family, such aspirations as these of mine have been fulfilled in an unsurpassed manner.
Furthermore, in that Buddha-field Timira, in every continent, such a human effort was exerted as was made in his vow.

Moreover, by means of unsurpassed wisdom, in each and every one of the empty Buddha-fields in the ten directions— equal in number to the sands of the river Ganges, and characterized by the five corruptions— such a human effort was exerted in every continent.
Just as my former vow was made,
behold, noble son, the excellence of wisdom in the conduct of awakening; and this is the seed of the roots of merit from the Tathāgata’s three types of good conduct.

Likewise, at a later time, after an interval of more than incalculable *kalpas*, during the great eon known as Saṃśrayasa, this Buddha-field was named Vicitadoṣa; it too was characterized by the five corruptions (*pañcakaṣāya*).
In the eastern direction, in the fifty-first world-system of four continents, there was a Jambudvīpa named Vaḍa.
There too, for the sake of maturing sentient beings, I was born as a universal monarch named Ambara, the sovereign of the four continents.
And there, I incited, established, and settled sentient beings in the ten paths of wholesome action; I incited, established, and settled them in the three vehicles.
And he became one who gives everything, bestowing all things;
and there, beggars would come to me and ask for various kinds of jewels,
such as silver and gold.
As long as there were sapphire, great sapphire, jyotīrasa, and dakaprasādaka gems for the supplicants, so many abundant jewels were obtained.
Then I asked my ministers,
"From where is the appearance of these jewels?"
They said:
"The dragon kings reveal treasures; through the manifestation of treasures in the world, the manifestation of jewels occurs."
"It is not only those who are so many as the number of supplicants before Your Majesty who provide instruction.
Then I made this vow:

"If, while the world is abiding in the five corruptions, during the Kali Age which is a forest of intense afflictions, and while the lifespan of beings is but one hundred years, I should attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; [then may I...]
May this hope of mine be fulfilled:
that I may become a dragon king named Nidhidarśaka in this buddha-field;
and throughout this entire buddha-field called Vijitaghoṣa, in every single continent, may I take birth seven times.
And in each and every birth, may I manifest and bestow hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of treasuries filled with various jewels—
namely, gold, fine gold, up to sapphire, great sapphire, jyotīrasa, and dakaprasāda.
And having gone a thousand yojanas for each individual treasury, may I extensively display and bestow upon sentient beings even those treasures that are completely full of jewels.
And may I manifest such heroic conduct in this very Buddha-field;

likewise, in as many Buddha-fields in the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā— in world-systems of the five corruptions— may I take birth seven times in every single field and on every continent, just as previously described.

And when, noble son, I had made such a vow as this, then hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of deities in the expanse of the sky rained down a shower of flowers from the air and offered their applause, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, O Giver of All!
Such a hope of yours shall flourish just as you have made your vow."
A great multitude of people heard that King Ambara had been given the name "Giver of All" by the gods dwelling in the expanse of the sky;
having heard this, it occurred to them:
"What if we were now to ask him for a gift involving a difficult renunciation?"
"If he renounces her, then he shall have the name 'Giver of All'.
Thereupon, they all set about to ask King Ambara for his female attendants,
and to ask for the queen, the chief consort, as well as his sons and daughters.
Then King Ambara, with a gracious mind, granted them [their request]. This thought occurred to them: "It is not difficult for one who abandons his wife;
what if we were now to ask King Ambara for his limbs and members?"
"In that case, if he gives it, he will become a Giver of All;
but if he does not give it, he will not become a Giver of All.
Then, in the presence of King Ambara, a young brahmin named Jyotīrasa stood before him.

He entreated him, saying, "O Giver of All, grant me the kingdom. Upon hearing this, King Ambara, with a mind of supreme joy, personally bathed the brahmin, bound the turban upon his head, consecrated him with the royal inauguration, established him in kingship, and bestowed upon him the entirety of Jambudvīpa.
He made this vow:
"May I awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by renouncing all of Jambudvīpa;
if this hope of mine is fulfilled,"
"This king who has now been established by me over the whole of Jambūdvīpa— let his command prevail in Jambūdvīpa;
let him be long-lived,
a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) who remains for a long time."
"And when I shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, then you shall be prophesied as my heir-apparent to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Then a brahmin named Roca requested both my feet from me.
With a mind full of serene faith, I myself took up a sharp weapon, cut off my own feet, and gave them to him;
then he made this aspiration:
"May I obtain the unsurpassed feet of ethical discipline."
There, a brahmin named Drāṣṭāva requested both my eyes;
I plucked out both my eyes and gave them to him—
the rest as before.
He made a vow to attain the five unsurpassed eyes. Not long after, a brahmin named Saracchighoṣa requested both my ears from him;
I myself cut off my two ears and gave them to him.
And he made a vow for the sake of attaining the unsurpassed stream-entry;
he was an Ājīvika named Saṃjīvana,
and by him, the male sign— the male organ— was requested from me.
I myself cut it off and gave it away,
and I made a vow for the sake of attaining the mark of the unsurpassed secret organ;
furthermore, another person requested my flesh and blood.
I gave it myself,
and I made a vow for the sake of attaining the characteristic of golden color;
furthermore, there was a wandering mendicant named Kṣīrasa, and by him both my hands were requested.
And with my own right hand, I cut off my left hand and, having had my right hand cut off, I gave it [to him],
and I made a vow for the attainment of the supreme hand of faith.
And when my limbs and members were being severed, then too I made a vow with my body smeared with blood.

“If by this renunciation my hope for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment should be fulfilled, may I certainly obtain a recipient for this body. Then those merciless, ignoble, and ungrateful beings— the local kings and ministers— said:
“This man is evil-minded and of little intelligence; he has had all his limbs severed and has been deprived of all royal power and sovereignty.
What further use have we for this lump of flesh?
Having seized me, they cast me out onto the ground of the city cemetery and departed.
There, gadflies and mosquitoes came and drank my blood, and dogs, jackals, and vultures came and devoured my flesh;
and there, with a serene mind, I made this vow:
"And when I renounced all royal sovereignty, and even as I was relinquishing my entire body, limb by limb,
my mind did not experience regret for even a single moment."
And no anger has been aroused in me; by that, may my aspiration be fulfilled:
let this body of mine stand as a mountain of flesh; whatever beings there are who subsist on flesh and drink blood, let them eat my flesh and drink my blood!

"And for as long as sentient beings might eat my flesh and drink my blood, for that long may my body increase by the power of my vow; gradually, may my body grow to a height of one hundred thousand yojanas and a width of five thousand yojanas.
Therein, for a thousand years, I satisfied sentient beings with my own flesh and blood."

And as many tongues as have been sacrificed by me, even those consumed by beasts and birds, and as many others as have appeared through the power of my vows— if these were gathered into a single heap as large as Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, it would be for the sake of my constant vow to attain the mark of supreme, abundant, and inexhaustible tongues.
Having passed away from there, by virtue of my former vow, I was reborn among the nāgas in Jambudvīpa at Rūḍhavaḍa; I became a nāga king named Nidhisaṃdarśana.
On the very night I was reborn among the nāgas, on that same night hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of treasures were revealed, and I myself proclaimed:
"O beings, a treasure has appeared in this place!"
It is filled with various jewels, such as gold and fine gold, up to crystal-clear water.
You all, take them!
Having taken them, O beings, proceed by undertaking the ten paths of wholesome action.
"Generate the mind set upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; or generate the mind [set] by means of the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas.
Go, take as many jewels as you require."

And there, in that flourishing Jambudvīpa, through seven cycles of births as a nāga, immeasurable and incalculable treasures were revealed and bestowed over seven hundred thousand nayutas of koṭīs of years;
and likewise, immeasurable and incalculable beings there were established in the three vehicles and established in the ten paths of wholesome action.
Having been fully satisfied with various kinds of jewels,
he made a vow for the attainment of the thirty-two unsurpassed marks.
In this manner, on the second continent, he performed such manly exertion throughout seven successive births as a nāga.

In this way, throughout the entire world-system Vijitadōṣā, from the third [continent] up to all its continents, such human exertion was performed. Likewise, in the ten directions, in as many empty Buddha-fields afflicted by the five corruptions as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, on each and every continent, for seven cycles of births as a nāga, and for as long as seven hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of years, I have thus provided immeasurable and incalculable treasures for sentient beings.
As previously described:
"Behold, noble son, the bodhisattva conduct of the Tathāgata— how the Tathāgata practiced the conduct for awakening by seeking the thirty-two marks with intense strength and vigor."
Just as there were no such bodhisattvas in the past who have practiced the conduct of awakening with such intense strength and vigor, so too there is none at present.

Furthermore, there will never again be any bodhisattva who shall practice the course toward unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment with such intense force of effort, power, and speed, except for those eight previously mentioned.
Then, after the passing of incalculable eons, at a later time, this buddha-field was named Pravāḍodupāni.
During the great eon called Utpala, in this world-system of four continents while the five corruptions prevailed in the void, I was Śakra, named Savirōcana.
I saw in this Jambūdvīpa the conduct of sentient beings seeking after unwholesome things;
having seen it, I manifested myself in the form of an extremely terrifying yakṣa, descended into this Jambūdvīpa, and stood before the humans.
And seeing me, they were afraid and asked me,
"What is your need?
We shall give it to you."
I said, "I have need of food. They asked,
"What kind of food do you require?"
I said:
"I kill and eat humans;
however, I do not devour those humans who have abstained from taking life for as long as they live."
“Even those who have desisted from wrong views,
whether they resolve their minds upon unexcelled perfect enlightenment, or resolve their minds upon the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas or the vehicle of the śrāvakas— even them I do not devour.”

And there, when those beings saw the emanated beings having finished their meal, those beings, out of fear, desisted from taking life for as long as they lived, and desisted from taking what is not given, up to and including wrong view.
Some generated the mind set on unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; some generated the mind set on the vehicle of the solitary buddhas; and some generated the mind set on the vehicle of the disciples.
I established all beings of the four continents in the ten paths of wholesome action and in the three vehicles; there I made this vow:
"If my aspiration for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment should be fulfilled, then let this vow of mine be fulfilled."
And just as I have established the beings of the four continents on the path of virtue,
even so may the beings in every part of this entire buddha-field, across all four continents, behold me with such fear that I may establish them in the ten paths of virtuous action.
"And may I establish them in the ten paths of wholesome action and enjoin them to the three vehicles.

In this very way, throughout the ten directions, in empty Buddha-fields characterized by the five corruptions, may I establish sentient beings in the ten paths of wholesome action and enjoin them to the three vehicles.
In this very way, noble son, my hope and vow were fulfilled everywhere in the world-system Pravāḍodupānā, where humans were disciplined in wholesome qualities by me in the form of a yakṣa.

Likewise, in the ten directions, in as many empty buddha-fields afflicted by the five corruptions as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges, humans have been established by me in the practice of the path of virtue in the form of a yakṣa.
And just as I established many beings in virtuous conduct out of fear,

by the remainder of that karma, now that I am seated upon the adamantine throne at the foot of the Bodhi tree, desiring to fully awaken to enlightenment, Māra the Evil One has approached with a great army for the purpose of causing distraction from my awakening.
Noble son, this is, in brief, my perfection of giving.

While practicing the conduct of awakening, I attained profound patience, profound dhāraṇī, and profound samādhi; I acquired the five mundane superknowledges; and I performed such great deeds of a Great Being.
In this way, immeasurable and incalculable beings were encouraged, introduced to, and established in unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening.

In this way, immeasurable and incalculable beings were encouraged, introduced, and established in the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas; likewise, immeasurable and incalculable beings were encouraged, introduced, and established in the vehicle of the śrāvakas.

Setting aside those [beings], as many Blessed Buddhas as there were whom I have attended upon while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva— Buddhas equal in number to the atoms within a Buddha-field— [I have not seen anyone like you].

In the presence of each and every Buddha, I have grasped virtues as numerous as drops of water in the ocean; I have made offerings to incalculable Pratyekabuddhas, and I have made offerings to incalculable Śrāvakas of the Tathāgatas.
In this way, worship was performed for my parents and for the sages possessing the five superknowledges.
Previously, while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva out of compassion, I satisfied sentient beings with my own flesh and blood;
even now, they have been satisfied by means of the Dharma.
Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "Generosity," in the *Śrī Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka*, a Mahāyāna sūtra.

(KpSū 388) VI (Epilogue): "O son of good family, as I behold with my Buddha-eye the Blessed Buddhas in the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms within Buddha-fields, who have entered final nirvana— those whom I first inspired, established, and settled in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening— "
Those whom I first inspired to practice the perfection of generosity, up to and including the perfection of wisdom, and whom I established and settled therein—

I now behold those immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, Blessed Ones, in the eastern direction, who have set in motion the wheel of Dharma in accordance with the truth, and who remain, maintain themselves, and teach the Dharma;
they are the ones whom I first inspired to generate the mind directed toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and whom I established and settled therein.
In this same manner, it should be stated for all six perfections;
likewise, it should be stated for the southern, western, northern, downward, and upward directions.
"Noble son, I see that in the eastern direction, beyond ninety-one hundred thousand Buddha-fields from this Buddha-field," (KpSū 389)
In the world-system Saṃpuṣpita, there dwells, remains, and sustains himself a Tathāgata named Vimalatejaguṇarāja, and he teaches the Dharma.

It was under that Blessed One that I first generated the mind set on unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, and he inspired, introduced, established, and confirmed me in it; likewise, it was under him that I was first inspired in the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom, and so forth.
In the eastern direction, in the buddha-field Abhirati, there is a Tathāgata named Akṣobhya;
in the buddha-field Jambūnada, there is a Tathāgata named Sūryagarbha; in the buddha-field Ratīśvara, there is a Tathāgata named Ratīśvaraghoṣajyotis.
In the buddha-field Sūryapratiṣṭhita, there is a Tathāgata named Jñānabhāskara;
in the buddha-field Jayavaiśraya, there is a Tathāgata named Nāganirnardita; in the buddha-field Saṃjīvane, there is a Tathāgata named Vajrakīrti.
In the buddha-field Svaraja, there is a Tathāgata named Vyāghraraśmi; in the buddha-field Arati, there is a Tathāgata named Sūryagarbha;
and in the buddha-field Vairaprabha, there is a Tathāgata named Kīrtiśvararāja.
In the buddha-field Meruprabha,
there is a Tathāgata named Acintyarāja;
in the buddha-field Saṃvara, there is a Tathāgata named Jyotiśrī.
In the buddha-field Kusumaprabhā, there is a Tathāgata named Prabhāketu;
in the buddha-field Kṣamottarā, there is a Tathāgata named Merusvarasaṃdarśanameru;
and in the buddha-field Dharaṇāvatī, there is a Tathāgata named Jñānabimba.
In the Buddha-field named Kusumavicitra, there is a Tathāgata named Vimalanetra.

Having made him my precursor, noble son, I behold with the Buddha-eye immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, Blessed Ones, currently residing, maintaining themselves, and teaching the Dharma in the eastern direction— those who,

having previously not yet generated the thought of awakening, were inspired by me toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening, and were first established by me in the perfection of giving up to the perfection of wisdom.

"And by me, they were first brought into the presence of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who were then dwelling and maintaining their lives, where they received for the very first time the prophecy regarding their unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Then, at that moment, in that world-system Sampuṣpitā, the seat of that Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja trembled;
and those Bodhisattvas who were there [beheld] that Vimalaguṇatejarāja.
Seeing the Tathāgata’s seat tremble, they asked that very Tathāgata:
“Venerable Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, for this unprecedented trembling of the Blessed One’s seat?
That Tathāgata said to them: “Noble sons, in the western direction, beyond eighty-nine Buddha-fields from this Buddha-field, there is...”
There is a world-system named Sahā, where a Tathāgata named Śākyamuni resides, stays, and maintains his life.
He is currently teaching the Dharma to the fourfold assembly, beginning with their past connections.
By that Tathāgata, while he was formerly a bodhisattva, they were inspired toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

By that Tathāgata, through whom my first thought of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment arose, I was first encouraged, introduced to, and established in the perfection of generosity, up to the perfection of wisdom; by that Tathāgata, while formerly practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, I was first brought into the presence of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who were staying and maintaining themselves.
It was there that I first received the prophecy of my unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

That Tathāgata Śākyamuni, who is my spiritual friend, dwells and remains active in the Sahā world-system; he teaches the Dharma to the fourfold assembly, beginning with this account of our former connection.
“By that empowerment of the Tathāgata, my seat trembles.
Son of good family, who among you is able to go to the Sahā buddha-field at my word, to inquire after the health and well-being of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni?”
Then those bodhisattvas said to the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja:

"Venerable Blessed One, those who are here in this Saṃpuṣpita buddha-field—possessing supernatural powers and having attained the perfections of all bodhisattva qualities—having seen a great radiance this morning, have arrived from another buddha-field through miraculous power; therefore, this..."
For a moment there was an earthquake and a rain of flowers.
Those bodhisattvas said,
"Venerable Blessed One, we too shall go to that Sahā buddha-field to pay homage to and attend upon that Śākyamuni, and [to hear] that entrance into the dhāraṇī-gate of the aspects of omniscience."
"in order to hear this Dharma discourse.
Those many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas set out from that buddha-field by means of their own supernatural power;
they did not know where they should go.
They also said,

"Venerable Blessed One, we do not even know the direction in which the Sahā world-system, the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, is located. Then, that Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja extended his arm and emitted various rays of light from his five fingers.
Then those rays illuminated eighty-nine thousand Buddha-fields,
reaching as far as this Sahā Buddha-field.
Thereupon, those bodhisattvas beheld this entire Sahā Buddha-field filled with bodhisattvas, and the expanse of the sky filled with gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and asuras.
Having seen this, those bodhisattvas then addressed the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja:
"Venerable Blessed One, we see the entire Sahā buddha-field completely filled; there is not even space enough there, not even for the setting down of a staff, that is not filled with bodhisattvas."
"We see that the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is looking at us and teaching the Dharma.
Then, the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja said to those bodhisattvas: "O sons of good family, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is All-Seeing.
O sons of good family, whatever beings there may be in the Sahā world-system, whether dwelling on the earth or dwelling in the atmosphere, each and every one of those beings perceives thus:"
“The Tathāgata Śākyamuni gazes upon me with his entire mind and teaches the Dharma beginning with me alone.
Furthermore, noble son, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni teaches the Dharma which is established in a single color, yet he teaches it in all colors.
And those beings there, noble son, who are devoted to Brahmā perceive the Tathāgata Śākyamuni as Brahmā.
They hear the Dharma through the discourse of Mahābrahmapati; even those who are devotees of Māra and those who are devotees of the Sun.
Those who are devoted to Candra, those who are devoted to Vaiśravaṇa,
and those who are devoted to Virūḍhaka.
Those beings who are devotees of Virūpākṣa,
those who are devotees of Dhṛtarāṣṭra,
and those who are devotees of Maheśvara, perceive the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and hear the Dharma through the form, color, shape, speech, and discourse of Maheśvara.
"Even as many as eighty-four thousand thousands of beings—each with their own color, shape, inclination, form, and speech—they likewise behold the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and hear the Dharma.
In that assembly were the bodhisattva named Rahagarjita and a second bodhisattva named Jyotiraśmi.
Then the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja addressed those bodhisattvas:
“Go, sons of good family, and in the Sahā world-system inquire on my behalf after the Tathāgata Śākyamuni’s health, well-being, and state of ease.
Those bodhisattvas replied, “Venerable Blessed One, we shall inquire after the entire Sahā buddha-field, including both its earth and its sky.”
“We clearly perceive the world to be filled with Bodhisattvas; there is not even space for a single being here, whether on the earth or in the sky, where we might find a place to stand.
Then that Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja said, “Sons of good family, do not speak thus.
“There is no space in the Sahā buddha-field.
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni possesses vast space through his inconceivable buddha-qualities;
by virtue of his former vows, the Tathāgata’s compassionate teaching and its entryway are vast.
He teaches the Dharma beginning with the going for refuge to the Three Jewels and the teaching of the Dharma of the three vehicles,
and he teaches the threefold restraint of the training.
He demonstrates the three doors of liberation,
delivers sentient beings from the three miserable realms,
and establishes them upon the three auspicious paths.

At one time, noble son, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, having recently attained perfect awakening, out of regard for the beings to be trained, spent seven days in a single cross-legged posture in the Sāla Cave within the abode of the yakṣa Indrākṣa on Mount Madhyamaśaila,
experiencing the blissful joy of liberation.
The entire Sāla cave was filled by the body of the Tathāgata;
there was not even a space the size of four finger-widths there that was not filled by the body of the Tathāgata.

And at the conclusion of those seven days, twelve nayutas of bodhisattvas from the ten directions stood facing that mountain in this Sahā world-system in order to pay homage to, attend upon, and hear the Dharma from the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
And, noble son, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni performed a miraculous feat (*ṛddhy-abhisaṃskāra*) there in that assembly; and that Sāla cave became thus vast and thus expansive,
so that when those twelve *nayuta* of bodhisattvas entered that Sāla cave, they saw it as having ample space.
And each individual bodhisattva there, having performed worship of the Tathāgata through various miraculous transformations of a bodhisattva,
each one created a seat made of the seven precious gems upon which they sat to hear the Dharma.
Thus, noble son, was that Tathāgata Śākyamuni possessed of such vast space.

Having heard the Dharma from that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, those bodhisattvas bowed their heads at the feet of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, circumambulated him three times, and departed for their respective buddha-fields. Not long after those bodhisattvas had left, the Sāla cave returned to its former state.
(KpSū 397) There, in that world-system of four continents, Śakra named Kauśika, his lifespan having come to an end and being terrified by the fear of rebirth in the animal realm,
approached the Sāla Cave where the Blessed One was together with eighty-four thousand gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven.
Having approached and stayed near the Sāla-cave residence of Indrākṣa,
through the power of that Blessed One, this thought occurred to him:
"What if we were now to entreat Pañcaśikha, the son of the Gandharvas?"
"And when that Pañcaśikha praises the Blessed One face-to-face with his sweet voice,
then the Blessed One will arise from his meditative absorptions and concentrations.
Thereupon, Śakra made a request to Pañcaśikha, the son of the Gandharvas.
Then Pañcaśikha, with his charming singing and instrumental music, through the majestic power of the Blessed One, extolled the Blessed One’s praises with five hundred hymns.

And when, noble son, Pañcaśikha began to praise the Blessed One, the Blessed One Śākyamuni then entered the meditative absorption named Sughoṣavairocanaketu; by means of that absorption, all the yakṣas and rākṣasas of great supernatural power who were in the Sahā world-system [were affected].

Whether they were asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, gandharvas, or all the gods of the desire realm (*kāmāvacara*), and all the sons of the gods of the form realm (*rūpāvacara*), they gathered there. Those who were devoted to his voice became serene upon hearing his voice;
those who were devoted to his physical beauty and fame [became serene] upon hearing the Blessed One’s description of his own qualities.

Having heard [the sound], those who had conceived intense love, serene faith, profound respect, and wonder in the presence of that Blessed One became filled with serenity; likewise, those who were devoted to the flute music became serene upon hearing the flute.
Then the Blessed Śākyamuni, arising from that meditative absorption, caused the door of the Sāla cave to be revealed.
Śakra approached and asked the Blessed One,
“Blessed One, where shall we sit?
The Tathāgata Śākyamuni replied, “Sit down, O Yakṣas, as many as have gathered here.”
Then that Sāla cave became so vast that as many yakṣas as there are grains of sand in twelve Ganges rivers entered it.

Once that assembly was seated, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni delivered such a Dharma teaching that those seated in that assembly who belonged to the vehicle of the hearers (śrāvakayāna) heard a discourse on the vehicle of the hearers.
Therein, nine hundred and ninety million attained the fruit of stream-entry;
and those in that assembly who belonged to the vehicle of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment heard the pure discourse on the Mahāyāna;
and there, led by the gandharva Pañcaśikha, eighteen nayutas became established in non-retrogression regarding unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
And among those who had not yet generated the mind directed toward the three vehicles, some there generated the mind for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
There, some generated the aspiration for the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, and some generated the aspiration for the vehicle of the śrāvakas;
and there, Kauśika Śakra was liberated from fear.
His lifespan increased to a thousand years,
and he became irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Thus, noble son, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni possesses such vast scope.
Thus vast is the vocal range of this Tathāgata;
it is impossible for anyone to grasp the limit of that Tathāgata’s vocal range, nor to calculate it. Vast also is the skillful means of that Tathāgata and his ripening of sentient beings.
It is impossible to grasp the limit of that Tathāgata’s skill in means.
Furthermore, O son of good family, the body of the Tathāgata is vast;
it is impossible for anyone to behold his crown of the head.
Or to reach the limit of his body;

and as many sentient beings as are currently gathered there in that Sahā buddha-field, if those sentient beings were to enter the womb of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, they would all move about therein, and those sentient beings would [all] be within a single pore of that Tathāgata.
They might enter and emerge [from it],
yet they would not be able to grasp the limit of that Tathāgata’s single-hair pore— neither its deficiency nor its fullness—
even with a divine eye.
Thus, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni possesses such an expansive body.
Furthermore, noble son, the Buddha-field of that Tathāgata Śākyamuni is vast;
indeed, it would be as full as all the Buddha-fields in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
As for those beings— for example, just as all those beings might now enter this Sahā buddha-field and all of them could move about there—
why is that?
In the same way, that Tathāgata had previously made a vow for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment at his first production of the thought of awakening.
"Let alone, noble son, world-systems as numerous as the sands of a single Ganges River;
suppose, noble son, that there were as many Buddha-fields in the ten directions as the sands of a thousand Ganges Rivers, each so vast in extent."

For example, if right now this Sahā buddha-field were filled with sentient beings, and all of them were to enter this Sahā world-system and all were to move about there— such was the vow made by that Tathāgata in the past upon first generating the mind directed toward the attainment of unsurpassed knowledge.
In this way, noble son, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni possesses an extensive buddha-field;
by these four qualities, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni is more distinguished. Noble sons, you should grasp these stainless flowers, radiant as the moon, exactly as they are.
"Go to the western direction and, having seen for yourselves the Sahā buddha-field, inquire after the health and well-being of that Tathāgata Śākyamuni in my name.
Then, that Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja, taking flowers as pure as the radiance of the moon, [entrusted them] to the Bodhisattva Raharāja.
Having given [the command] to the bodhisattva Jyotiraśmi, he said: "Go, sons of good family, to the Sahā world-system through the empowerment of my supernatural power.
Thereupon, twenty thousand living beings said:
"Venerable Blessed One, we too would go to the Sahā world-system by the majesty of the Tathāgata, in order to see, pay homage to, and attend upon that Tathāgata Śākyamuni."
The Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja said, "Go, noble sons, according to your intention.
Then those two bodhisattvas, Raharāja and Jyotiraśmi, together with twenty thousand bodhisattvas,
set out from that Saṃpuṣpitā world-system by the power of the supernatural might of the Tathāgata Vimalaguṇatejarāja.
In a single moment of thought, they arrived at this Sahā Buddha-field and alighted upon Vulture Peak Mountain.
Bowing with palms joined toward where the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, was, they said:
“Blessed One, there exists [this matter]. (KpSū 402)
In the eastern direction, beyond eighty-nine thousand Buddha-fields, there is a world-system named Saṃpuṣpita.
There dwells a Tathāgata named Vimalaguṇatejarāja.

That Tathāgata, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas, while proclaiming the praise and renown of the qualities of the Tathāgata, spoke thus: "The Tathāgata named Śākyamuni resides in the Sahā Buddha-field."

He sustains [the world]. And by that Tathāgata, while he was formerly a bodhisattva practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, I was first of all exhorted, introduced, and established in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; and by his word, I [was established] in unexcelled [enlightenment].
That Tathāgata first generated the mind set on perfect enlightenment and established me in the perfection of giving,
up to what was previously mentioned.
Thus, by these four qualities, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni is more distinguished.
"Just as he has sent these *candrarocavimala* flowers and inquires after your health and well-being.
Thus, from the Buddha-field of Abhirati, the seat of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya shook.
And those bodhisattvas who were assembled there, seeing that the seat of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya had shaken, also inquired about it.
The full passage is as previously stated.
This should be said for all of them.
And at that time, immeasurable and incalculable Bodhisattvas who were messengers of the Tathāgatas from the eastern direction [came to] this Sahā world-system.
They had arrived from the buddha-field Sahacandrarocavimala with flowers to inquire after, worship, pay homage to, attend upon, and listen to the Dharma from the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
Immediately after the names of the buddha-fields and the Blessed Buddhas in the eastern direction had been proclaimed by the Blessed One, they were dismissed.
Then the Blessed One began to proclaim the southern direction:

"I see, noble son, that to the south of this buddha-field, beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, there is a world-system named Sarvaśokāpagata; there a Tathāgata named Aśokaśrī resides, stays, and maintains himself."
When I was first practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva in the past, I was the very first to inspire that Blessed One toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
just as previously described.
In the buddha-field Jambūprabha, there is a Tathāgata named Dharmeśvaravinardi.
In the buddha-field Merupratiṣṭhita, there is a Tathāgata named Gatīśvarasālendra; in the buddha-field Guṇendraniryūha, there is a Tathāgata named Siṃhavijṛmbhitarāja.
In the Buddha-field Maṇimūlavyūha, there is a Tathāgata named Nārāyaṇavijitagarbha; in the Buddha-field Muktāprabhasaṃcaya, there is a Tathāgata named Ratnaguṇavijṛmbhitasaṃcaya;
in the Buddha-field Devasoma, there is a Tathāgata named Jyotigarbha.
In the buddha-field Candanamūla, there is a Tathāgata named Nakṣatravidhānakīrti;
in the buddha-field Viśiṣṭagandha, there is a Tathāgata named Puṇyabalasālarāja;
in the buddha-field Suvidita, there is a Tathāgata named Manojñaghoṣasvaravinardita.
In the Duraṇya buddha-field, there is a Tathāgata named Sālajayabindurāja;
in the Nardaśoca buddha-field, there is a Tathāgata named Tejeśvaraprabhāsa;
and in the Abhigarjita buddha-field, there is a Tathāgata named Sumanojñasvaranirghoṣa.
In the Buddha-field Ratnaviśabha, there is a Tathāgata named Ratnatalanāgendra;
in the Buddha-field Palāmaratnavṛkṣaratna, there is a Tathāgata named Dharmameghanirghoṣeśvarasaumya.
The full passage is as previously stated.
In this way, the seats of immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the southern direction trembled;
all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, proclaimed the beauty, fame, and renown of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.

At that time, immeasurable and incalculable Bodhisattvas who were messengers of the Tathāgata from the southern direction arrived in this Sahā Buddha-field with *candrarocavimala* flowers, in order to inquire after the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and to hear the Dharma.
Furthermore, the Blessed One said: "Noble son, I see that in the western direction, beyond ninety-seven hundred thousand nayutas of Buddha-fields from this Buddha-field..."
There, in the buddha-field named Upaśāntamati, there dwells, remains, and sustains himself a Tathāgata named Ratnagiri,

and he teaches the Dharma. Formerly, when I was a bodhisattva practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, I was the very first to inspire that Blessed One toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
As previously stated,
[the description of] the Buddha-fields is to be expanded in full;
there was a Tathāgata named Vararaśmikośa.
The Tathāgata named Svarajñakośa,
Haritālakīrti, and Samantagarbha;
Brahmakusuma,
Karadharavikrama,
Dharmaveśapradīpa.
Asamantamerusvaravighuṣṭarāja, Brahmendraghoṣa,
as previously described.

In this way, the seats of those immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, the Blessed Ones of the western direction, whose names were proclaimed by the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, trembled. At that time, immeasurable and incalculable Bodhisattvas who were messengers of the Buddhas from the western direction arrived at this Sahā Buddha-field with flowers as pure as the radiance of the moon, and sat down to listen to the Dharma.
The same applies to the subsequent directions;
likewise for the zenith, the nadir,
and the southeastern direction.
In the same way [it was] in the south-west, in the same way in the west-north, and in the same way in the north-east.”
Again, the Blessed One Śākyamuni said: "I see, O son of good family, that in the northeastern direction, beyond ninety-eight hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of Buddha-fields from this Buddha-field,
there is a Buddha-field named Vijaya."
There was a Tathāgata named Vigatasaṃtāpa-bhavavaishravaṇasālarāja.
Formerly, when I was practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva as a bodhisattva, I was the very first to inspire that Tathāgata toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment,
and [to establish him] in the six perfections.
As soon as I was first brought into the presence of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who were then dwelling and maintaining their course—
there, where he received the prophecy of his unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment—
the moment his name was proclaimed, that seat trembled.
As many as eighty-four thousand thousands of beings—differing in complexion, devotion, configuration, form, and speech—behold the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and hear the Dharma.
And in that assembly there were two bodhisattvas:
one named Vigopaśikhara and the second named Saṃrocanabuddha.

And that Tathāgata named Vigatasaṃtāpodbhavavaiśravaṇasālarāja, having addressed those two Bodhisattvas, spoke thus: "Go, sons of good family, to the Sahā Buddha-field; in my name, inquire after the Tathāgata Śākyamuni’s freedom from illness and pain, and his state of dwelling in comfort."
The two of them said:
"Venerable Blessed One, we behold the entire Sahā buddha-field, including both the earth and the sky;
yet there is not even space for a single sentient being on the earth or in the sky where we might establish ourselves."
And that Tathāgata said: "Do not speak thus, son of good family, saying, 'There is no room in the Sahā buddha-field. For what reason?"
Noble sons, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni possesses vast space through his inconceivable buddha-qualities;
by virtue of his former vows, the entry into and practice of that Tathāgata’s compassionate teaching is extensive,
as is the taking of the three refuges.
He teaches the Dharma by means of the three vehicles,
teaches the threefold restraint of training,
and elucidates the three gates of liberation.
He delivers sentient beings from the three lower realms and establishes them upon the three auspicious paths.

At one time, noble son, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, not long after his full awakening, out of regard for those beings to be trained, was in the abode of the yakṣa Indrākṣa, in the midst of the Viṣamaśailendra mountain range.
He dwelt in the Sāla Cave;
for seven days he passed the time in a single cross-legged posture,
