experiencing the joy and bliss of liberation.
And that entire Sāla cave was filled by the body of the Tathāgata;
there was not even a space the size of four finger-breadths there that was not filled by the body of the Tathāgata.
And at the end of those seven days, twelve nayutas of bodhisattva mahāsattvas from the ten directions arrived in this Sahā world-system to pay homage to that Tathāgata Śākyamuni;
[they did so] because that Tathāgata Śākyamuni is more distinguished by these four qualities than other Tathāgatas.
"Take up, O sons of good family, these flowers, pure and radiant as the moon;
having taken them, go to the southwestern direction,
so that you may yourselves see that Sahā buddha-field."
"In my name, inquire after the health and well-being of that Tathāgata Śākyamuni.

Then, the Tathāgata Vigatasaṃtāpodbhavavaiśravaṇasālarāja, taking flowers as pure as the light of the moon, gave them to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vigopaśikhara and to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Saṃrocanabuddhi.
And he spoke thus: “Go, sons of good family, to the Sahā buddha-field by means of the empowerment of my supernatural power. Thereupon, twenty thousand living beings said:
“We too, Blessed One, shall go to the Sahā buddha-field through the majesty of the Tathāgata, in order to see, pay homage to, and attend upon the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.”
The Tathāgata said, "Go, sons of good family, according to your intention.
Then those two bodhisattvas, together with twenty thousand bodhisattvas, set out from that Viraja Buddha-field by the supernatural power of that Tathāgata;
in a single instant, they arrived here in this Buddha-field and alighted upon Vulture Peak Mountain.
Standing to one side, they bowed with palms joined toward where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni was and said:
"Venerable Blessed One, there is [a land] in the northeastern direction,
as previously described."
"That Tathāgata has sent these Candra-roca-vimala flowers and inquires after the Blessed One’s health and well-being.
Thus was the seat of the Tathāgata Mārabhavana-vidhvaṃsana shaken.
And those bodhisattvas who had assembled there, having seen that seat of the Tathāgata— which destroys the realm of Māra— tremble, and they question the Tathāgata,
as was previously described; such were Sālendrarāja, Vikramaraśmi, and Padmottara.
Candana, Merurāja, Sāgara, Sārajyotis, and Jñānavikrama Tathāgata—

during that time, immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas from the northeastern direction, together with those bodhisattvas, arrived here in this Sahā buddha-field with *candrarocavimalapuṣpa* flowers for the sake of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
For the purpose of questioning, honoring, paying homage, and hearing the Dharma.

At that very moment, through the supernatural power of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the physical bodies of all those beings who had assembled in the Sahā Buddha-field became each as large as one *yojana* in measure; and the entire Sahā Buddha-field was filled with such beings, such that there was no space whatsoever in the field—neither on the earth nor in the sky—that was not occupied by beings, even down to a space the size of a single applicator of collyrium. Not even a spot the size of a needle’s point remained unfilled by beings.
And all those beings see empty space,
yet they do not see one another;
nor do mountains such as Sumeru, Cakravāḍa, or Mahācakravāḍa come within the range of their vision.

Neither the intermediate spaces between worlds, nor the divine palaces, nor anything from above down to the golden wheel below appeared within his vision, with the exception of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
They behold the Tathāgata,
and there the Blessed One has entered the meditative absorption of the "Pervasion of Space" (*ākāśaspharaṇa*), which is the tranquility of the non-obstruction of phenomena;
consequently, those stainless flowers with the luster of the moon enter all the pores of the Blessed One’s body.

And all those beings saw themselves as included within the Sahā world-system, having departed from the mental applications and forms manifested within the minds and mental factors of all sentient beings;
they gazed upon the pores of the Blessed One’s skin,
and there they beheld a garden.

They see those trees covered with various kinds of jewel-trees, various leaves, various flowers, and various fruits, and adorned with various garments, parasols, banners, flags, armlets, pearls, and necklaces—
just like the pleasure groves in the world-system of Sukhāvatī.
And this thought occurred to all those beings:
“Let us go to see this garden.
And all those beings who were included within the Sahā world-system [went along].
With the exception of those in the hells, the world of Yama, the animal realm, and the formless sphere,
all remaining sentient beings entered the body of that Tathāgata through the pores of his skin.
Then the Blessed One withdrew that miraculous power and arose from that state.
Then those beings, seeing one another, said, "Where is the Tathāgata Śākyamuni?
The Bodhisattva Maitreya said, "Be fully aware, all you beings; consider this: we have all gathered within the womb of the Tathāgata."

Then those beings, having seen the body of the Tathāgata both inside and out, perceived it for themselves: "Just as we have entered and gathered within the womb of the Tathāgata," this thought occurred to them:
"From where did we enter the womb of the Tathāgata?"
“By whom have they been brought into this place?
Then Maitreya, addressing the entire assembly with his voice, said: “Listen, sirs, to this miraculous display of supernatural power of the Tathāgata;
you must attend with your whole mind to the Dharma that our Teacher, who acts for our benefit, is about to teach.”
Then the entire assembly joined their palms in reverence,
and the Blessed One taught the Dharma of the practice of all-happiness.
In that regard, what is the practice of all-happiness?
It is as follows: rescuing [beings] from the mire of saṃsāra, establishing them on the noble eightfold path, and the fulfillment of omniscience and self-arisen gnosis.
In this context, there is a tenfold manner of entering meditative absorption, generating the thought of awakening, and dedicating [merit].

Namely: the empowerment of the mind of great compassion toward all sentient beings; the production of things that are beneficial; and the provisioning of a great vessel by means of ferrying across those sentient beings who have not yet crossed over.
The armor of liberating those not yet liberated, by means of completely liberating them from unreal distortions;
the armor of not being terrified by the great lion’s roar, by means of discerning the dharma of selflessness;
the armor of traveling to all world-systems, by means of awakening to all phenomena as being like illusions, dreams, and reflections.
The armor of illuminating and adorning all world-systems through the purity of the foundation of the aggregate of ethical discipline;
the armor of perfecting the ten powers of a Tathāgata through the fulfillment of all perfections;
and the armor of attaining the four grounds of self-confidence through acting exactly as one has spoken.

Up to the armor of attaining the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha without exception— this tenfold practice of the gateway to the Dharma of establishment for Bodhisattvas consists of the practice of the way of thorough knowledge through the gateway of signlessness, which is the mental attention to the selflessness of all phenomena, and the non-arising and non-ceasing of the mind at any time. (KpSū 415)
The stage of non-retrogression is where there is no cessation of the cycles of dissolution and evolution, and which is neither eternal nor distracted.

Furthermore, while this Dharma discourse was being spoken, beings equal in number to the sands of eighty *koṭis* of Ganges rivers, who were within the Tathāgata’s womb, became irreversible from unsurpassed [enlightenment];
and there were Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas beyond counting who had attained various kinds of dhāraṇīs and patiences.
Furthermore, all those who had emerged from the pores of the Tathāgata’s body, filled with wonder,
bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and departed toward the ten directions.
They departed for their respective buddha-fields in order to make known the extent of the Tathāgata’s own body, which is the sphere of his voice.

Therein, those immeasurable and incalculable bodhisattvas who travel toward the eastern direction pass through as many buddha-fields as there are in that eastern direction, yet the sphere of the voice of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is not obstructed.
And thus they hear the voice there, with its various words, meanings, and phonemes;
just as the Dharma was heard by those seated before the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, in that very same way they hear his Dharma.
Moreover, even there, neither the diminution nor the increase of the body of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is perceived;
the body of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is seen clearly by the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, and immeasurable,
incalculable bodhisattvas and śrāvakas are seen entering and emerging from a single pore of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni’s body.
In this way, they are seen entering and emerging from the second pore, and so on from all the pores;
and the same should be stated for the ten directions.

And that entire assembly, having entered into the body of the Blessed One, emerged from the pores of the Blessed One’s body; they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and stood facing the Blessed One, praising him with various expressions of meaning, words, syllables, and sounds.

Then, at that very moment, the sons of the gods belonging to the desire realm and the form realm rained down a diverse shower of perfumes, garlands, and ointments; they played divine musical instruments and,
intent upon worshipping the Blessed One, offered divine parasols, banners, flags, garments, fine cloths, and ornaments.
Thereupon, a bodhisattva named Vaiśāradyasamuddhāraṇi joined his palms in reverence toward the Blessed One and addressed the Blessed One as follows:
“Venerable Blessed One, what is the name of this great sūtra of prophecy?
The Blessed One replied: “It is called ‘The Entrance into the Door of the Dhāraṇī of the Aspects of Omniscience.’”
The one named *Bahubuddhaka*, the one named *Bahusannipāta*,
and the one named *Bodhisattvavyākaraṇa*.
The one named "Crossing Over the Path of Fearlessness," the one named "Descending into the Eon of Concentration," and the one named "Manifestation of the Buddha-field."
“Named Sāgaropama, named Gaṇanātikrānta, and named Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka.”

Again he asked: "To what extent, Blessed Lord, will a son of good family or a daughter of good family produce a mass of merit who hears this Dharma-discourse, takes it up, bears it in mind, recites it, explains it in detail to others, writes it down, or causes it to be written down—
even if only a single verse?"
He said: "I have previously described the mass of merit here;
now I shall speak of it in brief.
Whoever shall hear this Dharma-discourse, take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, and explain it in detail to others—even if only a single verse—[shall obtain such merit]."
Moreover, whoever shall preserve [this sūtra] by having it written down at least during the final five hundred years,
that person will produce a much greater mass of merit than the mass of merit of a bodhisattva who practices the six perfections for sixteen great aeons.
For what reason?

Because it is the pacifier of all diseases for the world with its gods, its Māras, and its Brahmās; for the generation including śramaṇas and brahmins; and for the yakṣas, nāgas, gandharvas, kumbhāṇḍas, pretas, piśācas, kinnaras, asuras, and those with malicious minds.
It pacifies all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes;
it pacifies all epidemics, untimely deaths, and diseases;
and it brings about the pacification of all famines.
It brings about security, it brings about abundance of food, and it brings about health and harmony.
He brings the happiness of fearlessness to those who are afraid, he brings about the pacification of the afflictions,
and he brings about the increase of the roots of virtue.

He brings about liberation from the suffering of the miserable realms; he reveals the path by means of the three vehicles; he causes the attainment of meditative concentrations, dhāraṇīs, and patient acceptance;
and he provides sustenance for all sentient beings.
He who performs the act of sitting upon the vajra-throne, he who performs the act of subduing the four Māras,
and he who performs the act of fully awakening to the factors conducive to enlightenment.
He is the one who sets the wheel of Dharma in motion;
he causes the perfection of the factors of enlightenment for those beings who are destitute of the seven noble riches;
and he possesses a vast retinue.
“I have spoken this Dharma discourse for the purpose of enabling entry into the city of the Fearless.
To whose hands do I entrust this Dharma discourse?
Who will protect this Dharma discourse of mine during the final five hundred years?”
"How will he proclaim [this] into the ears of beings who stand upon the ground of unrighteousness and of monks whose moral conduct is broken;
how will he cause those who are stained by passion for unrighteousness, overcome by perverse greed, habituated to false teachings, and whose minds are immature, to feel spiritual urgency?"
The entire assembly, having understood the mind of the Blessed One with their own minds, [became silent].
In that assembly sat a yakṣa-ṛṣi named Merupuṇya.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya took that yakṣa-ṛṣi Merupuṇya and led him into the presence of the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said: "Receive this Dharma-discourse, O Great Seer;
proclaim it into the ears of those irreversible Bodhisattvas who have gone to other lands during the final five-hundred-year period.
And today, generate the irreversible mind. [He replied: "So be it, Venerable Blessed One. For eighty-four great eons..."

"O Venerable Blessed One, transcending that which was previously established by my vow when I attained the state of a yakṣa-king, while practicing the conduct of awakening for the sake of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, I have established countless beings in the four divine abodes and established them on the stage of non-retrogression."
"And I myself shall bring beings to maturity, even until the final five-hundred-year period, for whoever shall take up this Dharma-discourse,
and even whoever shall preserve from it a single four-line verse."
Thus spoke the Blessed One; and the entire assembly, including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, being uplifted in mind, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
Thus concludes the Mahāyāna sūtra entitled the Śrī-Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka.
May there be auspiciousness.
Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has declared their cause, and also their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa.
May there be auspiciousness at all times!
Auspicious! Auspicious! Auspicious!
